summary:
I compared OLD a8d954e and NEW 12739d2 in this area, using 88bd144 to tell which changes are ours and which came from Shadlix. The buffer cache was rewritten upstream/in Shadlix. OLD created one VkBuffer per range and merged overlaps by copying (JoinOverlap). It also had preemptive downloads, which only ran for 2 serials, and its garbage collector never actually freed anything. NEW uses sparse "arena" buffers, a separate FaultManager, a 512 KB readback window and tracked barriers. Our fork changed almost nothing in these paths: gpuReadbackSpeed() in region_manager.h, and DescribePage/ForceWritable plus the from_fault flag in page_manager.cpp. Our biggest effect comes from config.

Most likely reason a player sees lower FPS in NEW:
1. OLD defaults to readbackSpeedMode = Disable, which means no readbacks. NEW sets Readback Speed to Low on a new install and on "Restore Defaults" (ApplyRecommendedSettings). In this release UFC 4 also runs Disable/Unsafe as Low. With Low, pages the GPU wrote are read-protected, and every CPU read of them costs a synchronous scheduler.Finish().
2. Even in Disable mode, NEW does not skip readbacks the way OLD did. MemoryTracker::InvalidateRegion lost OLD's `readbackSpeed() != Disable` check, so a CPU write to a page the GPU wrote now triggers a full synchronous download.
3. The "Fast" mode changed meaning. In OLD it did no read-protection at all. In NEW, Fast behaves the same as Low and Default; the only difference left is the flush counters, which nothing uses anymore.

Things that make NEW faster:
- When readbacks are on, each download is cheaper. NEW downloads a 512 KB window per fault and unprotects all of it, while OLD handled each 4 KB page with its own fault and its own Finish().
- Uploads use lighter tracked barriers instead of OLD's full-buffer barriers.
- Buffers are no longer merged or recreated by copying.
- There is less locking in IsRegion*Modified.

Small costs in NEW:
- A Shadlix "IsFastPathGame" check compares the game serial against 13 strings, twice per page, on every page-protection change.
- Page protection is updated with a separate OS call for each run of pages instead of one merged pass.
- The page-state table is 3x larger (+512 MiB of committed RAM).
- New memory regions are made resident with a raw vkAllocateMemory call plus vkQueueBindSparse when first touched.

A/B test: GPU.readbackSpeedMode in config.toml (0 = Disable, 2 = Low). For UFC 4 this only takes effect on the beta (cdfb6fa), where Off really means Disable, but the heads break. The beta removes the UFC 4 force-to-Low, but it does not restore OLD's skip-on-write-fault behaviour in Disable.

findings.title: Default Readback Speed: OLD Disable (no readbacks) vs NEW Low on a new install or Restore Defaults; UFC 4 forced to Low even when the player picks Disable or Unsafe
findings.old_behavior: OLD config.cpp:173 `readbackSpeedMode(ReadbackSpeed::Disable)`; reset at config.cpp:1764 is also Disable. In Disable, region_manager.h ChangeRegionState<GPU,true> runs UpdateProtection<!enable,false> (OLD lines ~103-104), so GPU-written pages are never read-protected. CPU reads never fault and never download. OLD memory_tracker.h:102 also skipped the download on write faults in Disable. Net effect: zero GPU->CPU sync stalls from the buffer cache.
findings.new_behavior: NEW config.cpp:280 still defaults to Disable, but ApplyRecommendedSettings (config.cpp:1958-1970) sets `readbackSpeedMode.base_value = ReadbackSpeed::Low`. It runs on first start when config.toml is missing (config.cpp:1976) and on Restore Defaults (config.cpp:3007). Separately, gpuReadbackSpeed() (config.cpp:1237-1261, fork commit ef844c9) returns Low for CUSA14204/CUSA14209 when the user chose Disable or Unsafe. In Low, region_manager.h:108-109 / 153-154 calls UpdateProtection<enable,true>, which read-protects every page the GPU writes (storage buffers, CopyBuffer/DMA targets). The first CPU read of such a page faults. The fault goes to BufferCache::ReadMemory -> DownloadMemory (buffer_cache.cpp:104-168), which issues runtime.CopyBuffer + scheduler.Finish() (line 159): a full CPU<->GPU serialization each time. A fault on a game thread also blocks on liverpool->SendCommand<true> (line 126).
findings.conditions: Every new install of NEW (any game, any GPU), and Restore Defaults. Always for UFC 4 (CUSA14204/14209) on 12739d2 regardless of the setting. Hurts most when the game reads GPU results on the CPU every frame (UFC 4 head compute), and on Intel Arc/iGPU where Finish() latency is high. An OLD user with an existing config (Disable) running UFC 3 keeps Disable.
findings.ab_toggle: config.toml [GPU] readbackSpeedMode (0 = Disable, 2 = Low) or the Readback Speed combo. On 12739d2 this has no effect for UFC 4, which is always Low. On beta cdfb6fa it is the On/Off switch (Off = Disable; UFC 4 force removed, heads break).
findings.evidence: NEW src/common/config.cpp:280, 1237-1261 (GameNeedsReadbacks/gpuReadbackSpeed), 1958-1970 (ApplyRecommendedSettings: `readbackSpeedMode.base_value = ReadbackSpeed::Low;`), 1976, 3007. OLD src/common/config.cpp:173, 1764. NEW src/video_core/buffer_cache/region_manager.h:99-117,143-157. NEW src/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.cpp:104-128 (ReadMemory), 130-168 (DownloadMemory, `scheduler.Finish();` at 159). Fork commits b7285a7 (recommended settings) and ef844c9 (UFC 4 Disable/Unsafe as Low).

findings.title: Disable/Unsafe no longer skip downloads on CPU write faults: NEW InvalidateRegion always flushes GPU-modified pages
findings.old_behavior: OLD memory_tracker.h InvalidateRegion (lines ~93-114): `if (Config::readbackSpeed() != Config::ReadbackSpeed::Disable && manager->IsRegionModified<Type::GPU>(offset, size)) return true;`. In Disable, a CPU write to a write-protected page the GPU had written only marked it CPU-modified; no download, no GPU wait. OLD BufferCache::InvalidateMemory (buffer_cache.cpp:159-170) also returned early when no buffer was registered in the range (IsRegionRegistered).
findings.new_behavior: NEW memory_tracker.h:91-105 checks only `IsRegionModified<Type::GPU>` and has no readback-mode check. ChangeRegionState still sets GPU bits in Disable mode; only the read-protection is skipped. So a CPU write to a page the GPU wrote calls on_flush -> BufferCache::ReadMemory(..., is_write=true) -> DownloadMemory with scheduler.Finish() (buffer_cache.cpp:98-102, 159). Disable in NEW is therefore not readback-free: CPU writes into GPU-written memory (reused ring buffers or compute output buffers) cause synchronous GPU stalls and stutter that OLD Disable never had.
findings.conditions: Readback mode Disable or Unsafe (e.g. UFC 3 with an old config, or UFC 4 on beta cdfb6fa with Off). Games where the CPU rewrites memory the GPU wrote earlier. Any GPU vendor.
findings.ab_toggle: none (no setting restores OLD's skip; it happens even with readbacks Off)
findings.evidence: OLD src/video_core/buffer_cache/memory_tracker.h InvalidateRegion: `if (Config::readbackSpeed() != Config::ReadbackSpeed::Disable && manager->template IsRegionModified<Type::GPU>(offset, size)) { return true; }`. NEW src/video_core/buffer_cache/memory_tracker.h:91-105: `manager->lock.lock(); if (manager->template IsRegionModified<Type::GPU>(offset, size)) { manager->lock.unlock(); on_flush(); } ...`. Identical at 88bd144 (git diff 88bd144 12739d2 does not touch memory_tracker.h). NEW buffer_cache.cpp:98-102, 159.

findings.title: 'Fast' readback mode changed meaning: OLD Fast = no read-protection; NEW Fast = same as Default/Low (full readbacks)
findings.old_behavior: OLD region_manager.h ChangeRegionState: `else if (readbackSpeed() == Fast) { UpdateProtection<!enable, false>(); }` (line ~101-102). GPU-written pages were not read-protected, so CPU reads caused no faults and no downloads. Write faults still flushed, and flush counting/preemptive downloads (buffer_cache.cpp:713-727) were active, but preemptive copies were only queued for the 2 'defer' serials. So OLD Fast was close to Unsafe.
findings.new_behavior: NEW region_manager.h:102-103: `else if (readback == Fast) { UpdateProtection<enable, true>(); }`, the same as Low/Default. In NEW, Low, Default and Fast act the same in the buffer cache: the only difference left is the ++flushes counter (lines 113-117), which the new buffer cache no longer reads. A user who picked 'Fast' in OLD for speed now gets full readback stalls.
findings.conditions: Users with readbackSpeedMode = 4 (Fast) in config.toml or the per-game config. Any game or GPU.
findings.ab_toggle: readbackSpeedMode (set 0/1 to avoid readbacks). On beta cdfb6fa, Fast is read as On (Low).
findings.evidence: diff a8d954e..12739d2 src/video_core/buffer_cache/region_manager.h: `-        } else if (Config::readbackSpeed() == Config::ReadbackSpeed::Fast) {\n-            UpdateProtection<!enable, false>();` -> `+        } else if (readback == Config::ReadbackSpeed::Fast) {\n+            UpdateProtection<enable, true>();`. 88bd144 already has `Fast -> UpdateProtection<enable, true>` (only the gpuReadbackSpeed refactor is ours).

findings.title: Cheaper readbacks when they are enabled: 512 KB download window instead of per-page fault/Finish
findings.old_behavior: OLD ReadMemory (buffer_cache.cpp:238-243) -> DownloadBufferMemory<false> (172-236) downloaded only the GPU-modified ranges inside the faulting 4 KB tracker page (8-byte fault). It then unprotected only that page (UnmarkRegionAsGpuModified(device_addr, size)). A CPU walking a GPU-written buffer therefore took one fault plus scheduler.Finish() per 4 KB page.
findings.new_behavior: NEW ReadMemory (buffer_cache.cpp:104-128) widens the request to a 512 KB-aligned window clamped to the arena (lines 110-118). DownloadMemory copies every GPU-modified island in the window in one copy and one Finish(), then unprotects the whole window (line 167). Far fewer faults and GPU syncs for sequential CPU reads. Same Finish() cost per event.
findings.conditions: Only when readbacks are active (Low/Default/Fast, or UFC 4 forced Low). Helps most in games that read large GPU-written areas. A player who ran OLD with Low should see fewer readback stalls in NEW.
findings.ab_toggle: readbackSpeedMode (only shows when readbacks are on)
findings.evidence: NEW src/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.cpp:110-118 (`constexpr u64 WindowSize = 512_KB;`), 130-168. OLD src/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.cpp:172-243 (download of the requested range only, `scheduler.Finish(); write_data();` at 232-233). Present at 88bd144 (lines 112-117).

findings.title: Shadlix 'IsFastPathGame' serial string compares in the page-protection hot path
findings.old_behavior: OLD PageState was a 1-byte bitfield (num_write_watchers:7, num_read_watchers:1). AddDelta and WritePerm were pure integer operations.
findings.new_behavior: NEW PageState::IsFastPathGame() (page_manager.cpp:51-58) compares MemoryPatcher::g_game_serial (a std::string) with 13 string literals. It is called in AddDelta (line 81) and WritePerm (line 61), i.e. twice per 4 KB page in every UpdatePageWatchers loop (248-292), under the page range locks. Every buffer upload (write-protect), every GPU write with readbacks on (read-protect), every download and every fault handled therefore costs about 26 failed string compares per page for UFC (not in the list). Roughly 0.1-0.3 us per page. That is about 1 ms per frame if around 20 MB of protection changes happen per frame, and more on frames with heavy uploads or readbacks.
findings.conditions: All games not in the list (including UFC 3/4), all GPUs. Scales with the amount of memory whose protection changes per frame. Larger with readbacks on.
findings.evidence: NEW src/video_core/page_manager.cpp:47-110 (`bool IsFastPathGame() const noexcept { const auto& serial = MemoryPatcher::g_game_serial; return (serial == "CUSA03173" || ... );`), 248-292. OLD src/video_core/page_manager.cpp:42-85. Present at 88bd144 (3 occurrences).

verdict.title: Shadlix 'IsFastPathGame' serial string compares in the page-protection hot path
verdict.notes: Verified at page_manager.cpp:51-58. It is called from WritePerm (via Perms) and AddDelta on each page in UpdatePageWatchers. OLD had a 1-byte bitfield and only integer operations. The serial for UFC (9 chars) does not match any entry, so each call costs 13 failed compares: size check plus a short memcmp, which fails at the 5th-6th char. That is probably 20-60 ns per call, around 0.05-0.15 us per page. The analyst's 0.1-0.3 us is on the high side but the same order. It only matters on frames with many MB of protection changes. The cost is small next to the VirtualProtect syscalls in the same loop. Upstream/Shadlix (unchanged by our fork).

findings.title: UpdatePageWatchersForRegion: one Protect pass per contiguous run instead of a single merged pass
findings.old_behavior: OLD page_manager.cpp:287-~350 took one lock for the 4 MB region and walked from the first to the last masked page. It extended the pending protect range across pages that were not updated but had the same permissions (potential_range_bytes), so a fragmented mask was often handled with a few VirtualProtect calls.
findings.new_behavior: NEW page_manager.cpp:297-306 loops `for (auto range : mask)` and calls UpdatePageWatchers per contiguous run. Each call takes the range locks again and does at least one Protect (VirtualProtect on Windows: a syscall plus TLB shootdown across cores). Fragmented GPU/CPU dirty masks (scattered small writes) mean more syscalls. NEW also drops OLD's per-call rasterizer->IsMapped ASSERT (a shared lock plus an interval lookup), which slightly offsets this.
findings.conditions: Scattered small uploads or GPU writes within a 4 MB region. Windows (VirtualProtect). All GPUs.
findings.evidence: NEW src/video_core/page_manager.cpp:296-307 (`for (auto range : mask) { ... UpdatePageWatchers<track, is_read>(start_addr, size); }`). OLD src/video_core/page_manager.cpp:286-352 (single-pass loop with potential_range_bytes, ASSERT IsMapped at ~249).

verdict.title: UpdatePageWatchersForRegion: one Protect pass per contiguous run instead of a single merged pass
verdict.notes: Verified. NEW page_manager.cpp:296-306 calls UpdatePageWatchers per run of the mask, which means one RangeLockGuard and at least one Protect per run. OLD (~287-350) took one lock and walked all pages from the first run to the last, merging Protect ranges across unchanged pages with equal perms. Fragmented masks therefore cost more VirtualProtect calls on Windows. NEW also drops OLD's per-call ASSERT(rasterizer->IsMapped) on the contiguous path. Small effect. Upstream.

findings.title: Buffer cache architecture: sparse arenas (vkAllocateMemory + vkQueueBindSparse on first touch) vs per-range VkBuffers with overlap-merge copies
findings.old_behavior: OLD FindBuffer/CreateBuffer (buffer_cache.cpp:546-711) created a VMA DEDICATED allocation per buffer (BDA flag). When ranges grew or overlapped, ResolveOverlaps/JoinOverlap copied the old buffers into a new one with full barriers and deleted them, which causes stutter whenever a buffer region grows. It wrote BDA page-table entries through the staging buffer. The garbage collector never freed anything (RunGarbageCollector:1203-1226 never calls clean_up).
findings.new_behavior: NEW maps the whole 40-bit space onto 4 GB sparse arena VkBuffers (GetArena 230-282). EnsureResident (284-338) calls instance.GetDevice().allocateMemory() directly (no VMA pooling) for each new gap, logs LOG_INFO 'Making range ... resident' each time, and queues sparse binds. These are submitted through graphicsQueue.bindSparse plus a timeline-semaphore wait before the next submit (SubmitPendingArenaBinds 417-454). No buffer is ever recreated or merged, which removes OLD's merge-copy stutter. But the first touch of new memory costs a WDDM allocation plus a sparse bind (slow on some Windows drivers, NVIDIA/Intel). Arena-page migration logs 'Migrating arena'. Memory is never freed.
findings.conditions: Mostly loading, first matches and new areas (first touch of new GPU-used memory); steady-state play is mostly unaffected. Sparse-bind cost depends on the driver (Intel Arc, NVIDIA and AMD Windows drivers differ).
findings.evidence: NEW src/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.cpp:58-88 (sparse probe, block_size), 230-282, 284-338 (`allocateMemory(alloc_info)` at 300, LOG_INFO at 318), 417-454 (`bindSparse` at 450). NEW buffer.cpp:118-122 (Sparse buffers created without VMA). OLD buffer_cache.cpp:562-711 (ResolveOverlaps/JoinOverlap/CreateBuffer), 852-895 (Register, BDA writes).

findings.title: Uploads use tracked, batched barriers instead of full-buffer pre/post barriers on every sync
findings.old_behavior: OLD SynchronizeBuffer (buffer_cache.cpp:897-954) did scheduler.EndRendering() and two BufferMemoryBarrier2s covering the whole buffer (AllCommands -> Transfer -> AllCommands) around every upload. InlineData/WriteDataBuffer/CopyBuffer did the same (1104-1201, 382-469). Each of these is a pipeline bubble.
findings.new_behavior: NEW SynchronizeMemory (buffer_cache.cpp:340-365) goes through Runtime::CopyBuffer (vk_runtime.cpp:110-132). It only flushes barriers when the touched range was already accessed (IsBufferAccessed/AccessBuffer tracking), so there are fewer full-pipeline barriers per draw with dirty CPU data.
findings.conditions: Draws/dispatches that upload CPU-modified buffer data (most frames), all GPUs. Larger benefit on GPUs where barriers are expensive.
findings.evidence: NEW src/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.cpp:340-365; src/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_runtime.cpp:110-132. OLD src/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.cpp:897-954.

verdict.title: Uploads use tracked, batched barriers instead of full-buffer pre/post barriers on every sync
verdict.notes: Verified. NEW SynchronizeMemory (340-365) uses Runtime::CopyBuffer (vk_runtime.cpp:110-132), which flushes barriers only if IsBufferAccessed. OLD SynchronizeBuffer (897-954) emitted full-buffer pre and post barriers on every upload. Note that NEW CopyBuffer still calls scheduler.EndRendering() each time, so render-pass breaks remain and only the barrier count drops. Small gain. Upstream.

findings.title: Less locking and cheaper queries in memory tracker / region manager
findings.old_behavior: OLD IsRegionCpuModified/IsRegionGpuModified took manager->lock for every 4 MB region queried (memory_tracker.h ~28-42). IsRegionModified built a 1024-bit RegionBits copy and called Any(). OLD BufferCache::IsRegionGpuModified also scanned gpu_modified_ranges_pending.
findings.new_behavior: NEW memory_tracker.h:28-40 queries without the lock. region_manager.h:181 uses bits.AnyInRange(start,end). This is called on every ObtainBuffer (stream path check), ObtainBufferForImage, etc. Less contention between the GPU thread and the fault handler.
findings.conditions: All games and GPUs. Many small buffer binds per frame.
findings.evidence: diff memory_tracker.h: `-                std::scoped_lock lk{manager->lock};` (twice). region_manager.h: `-        RegionBits test(bits, start_page, end_page);\n-        return test.Any();` -> `+        return bits.AnyInRange(start_page, end_page);`. OLD buffer_cache.cpp:529-538.

verdict.title: Less locking and cheaper queries in memory tracker / region manager
verdict.notes: Verified in the diff: the scoped_lock was removed from IsRegionCpuModified/IsRegionGpuModified, and RegionBits copy+Any was replaced by AnyInRange. OLD BufferCache::IsRegionGpuModified also scanned gpu_modified_ranges_pending (529-538). It is a real but microscopic CPU saving. Marked not FPS-relevant in practice.

findings.title: Page-state table grew from 1 to 3 bytes per page: 256 MiB -> 768 MiB zero-initialized at startup
findings.old_behavior: OLD PageState = 1 byte (bitfields). cached_pages has 2^28 entries = 256 MiB, value-initialized (memset) in Impl.
findings.new_behavior: NEW PageState = 3 x u8 (num_watchers, num_write_watchers, num_read_watchers; page_manager.cpp:47-49). 2^28 entries = 768 MiB, value-initialized at page_manager.cpp:309, so about 512 MiB more of private memory is committed and touched. That memory is cold afterwards but dirty, so it adds commit charge and possible paging.
findings.conditions: Systems low on RAM, especially AMD/Intel iGPU laptops where VRAM shares system RAM (8-16 GB). Windows.
findings.evidence: NEW src/video_core/page_manager.cpp:47-49, 115, 309 (`std::array<PageState, NUM_ADDRESS_PAGES> cached_pages{};`, NUM_ADDRESS_PAGES = 1<<28). OLD src/video_core/page_manager.cpp:44-47, 356.

verdict.title: Page-state table grew from 1 to 3 bytes per page: 256 MiB -> 768 MiB zero-initialized at startup
verdict.notes: Verified. NEW PageState has 3 u8 fields (page_manager.cpp:47-49). OLD had a 1-byte bitfield. NUM_ADDRESS_PAGES = 2^28 in both, and `cached_pages{}` is value-initialized inside the Impl that make_unique creates, so 768 MiB vs 256 MiB is written at startup. It costs more commit and working set and only matters on RAM-starved systems such as iGPU laptops. It does not affect steady per-frame cost. Upstream.

findings.title: Stream buffer for small read-only binds doubled (64 MB -> 128 MB); ObtainBufferForImage always CPU-copies non-GPU-modified ranges
findings.old_behavior: OLD UboStreamBufferSize = 64_MB (buffer_cache.cpp:28). When the per-frame stream usage wrapped, StreamBuffer::WaitPendingOperations waited on the GPU. ObtainBufferForImage (501-519) reused an existing cached buffer containing the range and only uploaded CPU-dirty pages.
findings.new_behavior: NEW STREAM_BUFFER_SIZE = 128_MB (buffer_cache.cpp:26), so fewer wrap waits. ObtainBufferForImage (193-202) memcpys the whole requested range into the staging pool unless it is GPU-modified, which is more CPU copying for image uploads that OLD served from an existing buffer.
findings.conditions: Many small UBO/read-only binds per frame (stream buffer: NEW faster). Frequent texture re-uploads from guest memory (image path: NEW slightly slower).
findings.evidence: NEW src/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.cpp:26, 170-202. OLD src/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.cpp:28, 471-519.

findings.title: Fault buffer / BDA page table sized by sparse block size (smaller on GPUs with 64 KB sparse alignment)
findings.old_behavior: OLD used fixed 16 KB caching pages: BDA page table 2^26 x 8 B = 512 MB, fault buffer 8 MB. The fault-parse compute dispatch covered 2^26 pages on every submit that used DMA (buffer_cache.cpp:729-850, called from Rasterizer::OnSubmit).
findings.new_behavior: NEW FaultManager (fault_manager.cpp:19-24, 87-182) sizes both from block_size = max(sparse alignment, 16 KB) (buffer_cache.cpp:70-84). With 64 KB blocks, typical for NVIDIA, the BDA table is 128 MB and the fault scan 4x smaller. The fault buffer is processed at most once per submit (TickFrame). There is a scheduler.Wait only if all 8 pending fault areas are still in flight.
findings.conditions: Shaders using DMA/BDA. GPUs with a 64 KB sparse alignment.
findings.evidence: NEW src/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.cpp:70-87; src/video_core/buffer_cache/fault_manager.cpp:16-24, 87-92, 153-156. OLD src/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.h (CACHING_PAGEBITS=14, BDA_PAGETABLE_SIZE, FAULT_BUFFER_SIZE), buffer_cache.cpp:729-793.

findings.title: Fork fault-path additions (from_fault flag, fault-storm detector, DescribePage/ForceWritable) are negligible in normal play
findings.old_behavior: OLD GuestFaultSignalHandler called rasterizer->InvalidateMemory(addr, 8) / ReadMemory(addr, 8) with no extra bookkeeping.
findings.new_behavior: NEW page_manager.cpp:221-228 passes is_gpu_thread and from_fault=true. Rasterizer::InvalidateMemory (vk_rasterizer.cpp:1565-1605) updates thread_local counters per fault, and only after 64 faults in a row on the same page logs and calls PageManager::ForceWritable (page_manager.cpp:325-328). This costs almost nothing per fault. The extra texture_cache.InvalidateMemory(..., from_fault) work belongs to the texture-cache area.
findings.conditions: Only matters in a fault storm, where it converts a livelock into progress.
findings.evidence: git diff 88bd144 12739d2 -- src/video_core/page_manager.cpp (+DescribePage, +ForceWritable, InvalidateMemory(..., true)); NEW src/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_rasterizer.cpp:1572-1603 (fork commit 84c6ede).

verdict.title: Fork fault-path additions (from_fault flag, fault-storm detector, DescribePage/ForceWritable) are negligible in normal play
verdict.notes: Verified via git diff 88bd144 12739d2 on page_manager.cpp/h and NEW vk_rasterizer.cpp:1565-1605. The per-fault cost is a few thread_local integer operations. Logging and ForceWritable only kick in after 64 consecutive faults on the same page. The from_fault flag passed to the texture cache belongs to another area. No buffer-cache FPS impact.

findings.title: Host memory fallback option (new in Shadlix) can push stream/device-local buffers into system RAM
findings.old_behavior: OLD buffer.cpp MemoryUsageVma: DeviceLocal/Stream always VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_AUTO_PREFER_DEVICE.
findings.new_behavior: NEW buffer.cpp:55-68: if Config::getUseHostMemoryFallback() is set, DeviceLocal and Stream use VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_AUTO_PREFER_HOST (the stream buffer for UBOs, GDS, BDA table). The default is false (config.cpp:257), so this only matters if a player enabled it. Sparse arenas are not affected (they use a device-local type directly).
findings.conditions: Only with useHostMemoryFallback = true in config.toml or the per-game config; worst on discrete GPUs.
findings.evidence: NEW src/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer.cpp:55-75; NEW src/common/config.cpp:257, 624-626. Present at 88bd144 (buffer.cpp:59).

missed_by_analyst:
No major FPS difference in this area beyond the analyst's list was verified. Minor verified points:

(1) OLD PageState::WritePerm returned ReadWrite when there were no write watchers (OLD page_manager.cpp ~49-52). As a result, OLD Perms() = ReadPerm|WritePerm was ReadWrite for a page with a read watcher but no write watcher, so OLD Low read-protection only took effect on pages that were also write-watched. NEW WritePerm returns Write in that case (page_manager.cpp:60-67), and Windows Protect ASSERTs perms != Write (211-217). Normally GPU-written pages are write-protected first by ForEachUploadRange, so in practice this rarely differs. It was not proven to matter for FPS.

(2) NEW handles read and write faults raised on the GPU command thread inline (assume_locks = is_gpu_thread, page_manager.cpp:221-228, buffer_cache.cpp:121-127). OLD always went through liverpool->SendCommand<true> (OLD buffer_cache.cpp:238-243). This is a correctness and latency improvement for GPU-thread faults only, with small FPS impact.

(3) The flush counter `++flushes[page]` (region_manager.h:113-117) runs on every unmark when the mode is not Low, but nothing in the NEW buffer cache reads NumFlushes (only ForEachPreemptiveFlushPage, which has no caller). This is dead work of negligible cost.

The dominant buffer-cache FPS factor for UFC 4 remains finding 1 (readbacks forced to Low by our fork). For UFC 3 with an existing Disable config, the main one is finding 2 (write-fault flushes in Disable, from upstream).

summary:
The texture cache changed a lot between OLD a8d954e and NEW 12739d2. Most of the change came from upstream/Shadlix: the Vulkan Runtime refactor, synchronous image downloads, RT/storage alias sync, and a GC that is no longer called. Our fork added BC/storage write-back, the flush on CPU writes, linear storage readback and the depth-as-color alias. Ranked by likely cost:
(1) Image downloads went from async to fully synchronous. OLD copied images into a stream buffer and a background thread waited on the GPU semaphore. NEW ProcessDownloadImages calls DownloadImageMemory(id, true), and that does scheduler.Finish() for each queued image. In NEW it also runs at every EOP/EOS/ReleaseMem/WriteData/Rewind, not only on submit. Anything queued for download now stalls the GPU thread until the GPU is idle. With default settings these sources fill the queue: 1x1 render targets (Shadlix rt_sync, active for UFC serials), linear 2D storage images of 64x64 or more written by compute (our fork, e565b66), and linear volume storage images (upstream).
(2) The texture-cache GC never runs in NEW. Rasterizer::OnSubmit only calls RunGarbageCollectorAsync, which drains a queue that only RunGarbageCollector fills. Nothing calls RunGarbageCollector, and gc_tick stays 0. OLD ran the GC on every submit. VRAM can grow over a session and spill into system memory on 6-8 GB cards and iGPUs.
(3) Image barriers are now emitted every time the previous access was a shader/transfer write, even when layout and access are unchanged. Every storage-image bind now gets an AllCommands-to-AllCommands barrier, which serializes back-to-back compute dispatches.
(4) Render-target alias sync is new since OLD. It copies an RT into other images at the same address once per submit when they are sampled. When sample counts differ it allocates a temporary VMA image for each copy.
(5) Our fork's GPU-side write-backs. Storage images are lazily tiled back into memory when they alias other images or BC textures. BC views of uncompressed images now go through a tile, free and detile cycle instead of ExpandImage's host copy.
(6) Our fork's CPU-write-fault flush. A guest thread blocks on SendCommand<true> when it writes into memory of a GPU-only RT or storage image. This is a stutter risk.
(7) Our fork's depth-as-color alias does a compute conversion of the whole depth image on every bind. It hits UFC 3/4 shadow maps that are read as R16_UINT.
Faster in NEW: tiling shaders are precompiled SPIR-V with specialization constants, where OLD compiled GLSL with glslang on first use. Tile and detile scratch memory now comes from a staging pool, where OLD did a vmaCreateBuffer for every texture upload and write-back. So texture streaming costs less CPU and stutters less. The per-submit GC CPU cost is also gone, compatible formats (UNORM/SRGB) are reused as views more often, and MSAA images can skip the storage flag.
Readback default: readbackLinearImages is false in both builds, and ApplyRecommendedSettings does not touch it. When a user turns it on, NEW also downloads tiled RTs of width 8 or less, and does it synchronously (OLD did it async).
A/B env vars: SHADPS4_LINEAR_STORAGE_READBACK=0, SHADPS4_LAZY_WRITEBACK=0/1, SHADPS4_BC_MODE (0-3), SHADPS4_FLUSH_CPU_WRITE=0, SHADPS4_DEPTH_AS_COLOR=0. No setting or env var controls the sync downloads themselves, the GC, the barrier rule or rt_sync. rt_sync is only disabled for a hardcoded serial list that does not include UFC.

findings.title: Image downloads became synchronous: scheduler.Finish() per queued image at every fence/EOP/submit
findings.old_behavior: OLD texture_cache.cpp: ProcessDownloadImages (line 89) ran only from Rasterizer::OnSubmit. DownloadImageMemory tiled the image into the Download stream buffer and pushed {tick, addr} to downloaded_images_queue. A separate DownloadedImagesThread (started at line 57, defined at line 149) waited on the master semaphore and memcpy'd to guest memory, so the GPU thread never waited.
findings.new_behavior: NEW texture_cache.cpp:102-108: ProcessDownloadImages calls DownloadImageMemory(image_id, true). At 110-149, the sync branch at line 137 calls scheduler.Finish(), a full submit plus CPU wait for GPU idle, then Invalidate and TryWriteBacking, once per image. The async thread is gone. ProcessDownloadImages is also called much more often: vk_rasterizer.cpp:649 (OnSubmit), 672 (OnFence), and liverpool.cpp:770, 791, 846, 890, 1257, 1293 (EventWriteEos, EventWriteEop, WriteData, Rewind, compute ReleaseMem/WriteData). Each image in the download set therefore costs a full CPU-GPU sync at the next fence.
findings.conditions: Any game or GPU where download_images is non-empty each frame. With default settings it is fed by: (a) 1x1 render targets, through rt_sync_.Schedule1x1Readback (vk_rasterizer.cpp:1351-1355, active for UFC 3 and UFC 4 because they are not in the serial lists); (b) linear 2D storage images of 64x64 or more written by compute (fork, see the next finding); (c) linear volume storage images (upstream, texture_cache.cpp:968-970); (d) when readbackLinearImages=true, every linear RT and every tiled RT of width 8 or less (texture_cache.cpp:988-991). A per-frame 1x1 RT, for example HDR luminance or auto-exposure, would remove CPU/GPU overlap every frame. That is worst on slower GPUs (iGPU, GTX 1660) and in GPU-bound scenes.
findings.ab_toggle: No toggle for the sync behaviour itself. Sources can be cut individually: SHADPS4_LINEAR_STORAGE_READBACK=0; readbackLinearImages=false (default). The 1x1 readback has no toggle; ShouldDisableSync() is serial-hardcoded at vk_rasterizer.cpp:40-50.
findings.evidence: Sync download: git diff a8d954e 88bd144 shows `- DownloadImageMemory(image_id);` becoming `+ DownloadImageMemory(image_id, true);`, the DownloadedImagesThread removal, and `if (sync) { scheduler.Finish(); ...}`. NEW src/video_core/renderer_vulkan/render_target_sync.cpp:67-69 (Schedule1x1Readback -> AddDownload). NEW vk_rasterizer.cpp:1351-1355. Call sites: liverpool.cpp:770/791/846/890/1257/1293. OLD vk_rasterizer.cpp:378 is the only call.

verdict.title: Image downloads became synchronous: scheduler.Finish() per queued image at every fence/EOP/submit
verdict.notes: Confirmed. NEW texture_cache.cpp:102-108 always calls DownloadImageMemory(id, true), and the sync branch at :136-140 does scheduler.Finish() once per image. The async DeferPriorityOperation path at :141-148 is still there but nothing uses it. OLD a8d954e texture_cache.cpp:89-176 tiled the image into the Download stream buffer and a DownloadedImagesThread waited on the master semaphore, so the GPU thread never waited. In OLD the only call site was vk_rasterizer.cpp:378 (OnSubmit). In NEW and in 88bd144 there are also calls at liverpool.cpp:770/791/846/890/1257/1293 and vk_rasterizer.cpp:672 (OnFence), so this came from upstream/Shadlix. When the download set is empty these calls cost only a mutex. The 1x1 RT readback (vk_rasterizer.cpp:1351-1355 -> render_target_sync.cpp:67-69 -> AddDownload) is active for CUSA14204/14209/06534, because none of them are in ShouldDisableSync or the extra exclusion list. I could not verify from code that UFC 3/4 actually render a 1x1 RT every frame. If they do, every frame gets one full GPU-idle wait (more if several images are queued), and >15% is plausible. If they don't, the cost is near zero. Note that GpuModified is never cleared after a download, so a queued image is downloaded again on every bind. No toggle. The quickest A/B is a code change to pass sync=false in ProcessDownloadImages.

findings.title: Texture cache garbage collector is never invoked (VRAM never reclaimed by LRU)
findings.old_behavior: OLD vk_rasterizer.cpp:372-382: OnSubmit called texture_cache.RunGarbageCollector() on every submit. It evicted LRU images older than 16/80/160 ticks once used memory passed the trigger, pressure or critical thresholds, and gc_tick advanced every submit.
findings.new_behavior: NEW vk_rasterizer.cpp:647-665: OnSubmit only calls texture_cache.RunGarbageCollectorAsync() every 60 submits when used memory is above the trigger. RunGarbageCollectorAsync (texture_cache.cpp:1359-1374) only drains gc_queue, and only RunGarbageCollector (1296-1352, via EnqueueForGc at 1336) fills that queue. git grep finds no caller of RunGarbageCollector, so the queue is always empty and gc_tick stays 0. Images are freed only by overlap resolution or unmap. VRAM use can grow without bound over a session. Images are created with VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_WITHIN_BUDGET_BIT and AUTO_PREFER_DEVICE, so once over budget they land in host-visible system memory, which is much slower to sample, or eventually fail an assert. Side effect in NEW's favour: no per-submit GC CPU work.
findings.conditions: Long sessions or many distinct textures (menus, Create Fighter, many fighters or arenas). Worst on GPUs with little dedicated VRAM: GTX 1660 (6 GB), Arc A3xx, AMD iGPUs with small carve-outs. Shows up as FPS dropping over time and stutter, not as a constant offset.
findings.evidence: `git grep RunGarbageCollector 12739d2 -- src` finds only texture_cache.cpp:1296 (definition) and vk_rasterizer.cpp:662 (RunGarbageCollectorAsync). OLD a8d954e vk_rasterizer.cpp:379 `texture_cache.RunGarbageCollector();`. The same OnSubmit is in 88bd144 vk_rasterizer.cpp:451-469, so it came from Shadlix.

verdict.title: Texture cache garbage collector is never invoked (VRAM never reclaimed by LRU)
verdict.notes: Confirmed: git grep finds RunGarbageCollector only at its definition (NEW texture_cache.cpp:1296). OnSubmit (vk_rasterizer.cpp:657-664) calls RunGarbageCollectorAsync every 60 submits. That only drains gc_queue, and only RunGarbageCollector fills it, so nothing is freed and gc_tick stays 0. OLD a8d954e vk_rasterizer.cpp:379 ran RunGarbageCollector on every submit. 88bd144 has the same NEW OnSubmit (lines 451-469), so this is upstream/Shadlix. One caveat on magnitude: images are still freed by ResolveOverlap (incompatible image at the same address, safe_to_delete after 32 ticks) and by unmap. Because games recycle memory pools, growth is bounded roughly by the guest's GPU-visible footprint and is not literally unbounded. The risk is real on 6-8 GB cards (GTX 1660, Arc A3xx/A5xx, 4060 Ti 8GB): VMA WITHIN_BUDGET plus AUTO_PREFER_DEVICE (image.cpp:109-110, same as OLD) spills to system memory, which shows up as FPS dropping over a session. On iGPUs everything is system memory anyway. In NEW's favour, OLD's eviction and re-upload hitches are gone. No toggle.

findings.title: Image barriers now forced whenever previous access was a write (storage images get a full barrier on every bind)
findings.old_behavior: OLD Image::GetBarriers returned no barrier when layout and access mask matched the last state. A storage image rebound in eGeneral with ShaderRead|ShaderWrite generated no barrier, so consecutive dispatches or draws could overlap.
findings.new_behavior: NEW image.cpp:289-293 (per-subresource path) and 323-328 (full path) emit a barrier whenever the last access contains TransferWrite, ShaderWrite or MemoryWrite, even with identical layout and access. Every storage bind (vk_rasterizer.cpp:1232-1236, AllCommands to AllCommands, ShaderRead|ShaderWrite) and every force_general or feedback bind now records a barrier, and FlushBarriers ends any active render pass. Back-to-back compute dispatches on the same storage image are serialized. This is more correct (it handles WAW hazards) but slower. Partial-subresource images can also produce one barrier per mip/layer.
findings.conditions: Compute-heavy frames: post-processing chains, GPU texture compression, particle simulation. Graphics draws that also bind storage images break the render pass every draw. Biggest effect on GPUs that overlap compute dispatches well (NVIDIA, AMD).
findings.evidence: git diff a8d954e 88bd144 -- src/video_core/texture_cache/image.cpp: `- if (last_state.layout == dst_layout && last_state.access_mask == dst_mask) { return {}; }` replaced by `+ const bool is_write = ...; if (... && !is_write) return;`. NEW src/video_core/texture_cache/image.cpp:289-293, 323-328. NEW src/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_rasterizer.cpp:1232-1236.

verdict.title: Image barriers now forced whenever previous access was a write (storage images get a full barrier on every bind)
verdict.notes: Confirmed: NEW image.cpp:288-293 and :323-328 add `|| is_write` for TransferWrite, ShaderWrite and MemoryWrite. The change is already in 88bd144 (upstream/Shadlix). Storage binds at vk_rasterizer.cpp:1232-1236 always request ShaderRead|ShaderWrite in eGeneral, so every rebind of a storage image emits a barrier, and Runtime::FlushBarriers (vk_runtime.cpp:723-741) calls EndRendering. ColorAttachmentWrite is not in the write set, so plain RT and texture use is unaffected, and transitions after TransferWrite already changed layout in OLD. The extra cost is limited to back-to-back storage writes on the same image. Those are usually dependent anyway, and OLD's missing barrier was a WAW hazard. A per-draw render-pass break only happens if pixel shaders write UAVs, and I found no evidence of that for UFC. No toggle.

findings.title: Render-target alias sync: extra GPU image copies (and temp image allocations) when a texture aliases an RT written in the same submit
findings.old_behavior: OLD had no render_target_sync. A texture image at the same address as an RT image was not refreshed from the RT, so no copies were made.
findings.new_behavior: NEW vk_rasterizer.cpp:1157-1160: every texture bind calls rt_sync_.CopyFromLastRt(). If an RT at that address was written in the current submit and the texture is a different image, render_target_sync.cpp:26-52 copies the RT into it (copyImage, with Transit and FlushBarriers, and EndRendering when sample counts differ). This happens once per texture per submit. On a sample-count mismatch it creates a new VMA image for the resolve on every copy and destroys it later (render_target_sync.cpp CopyRtToAlias). The RT is then transitioned back to color attachment, so more barriers and render-pass breaks follow.
findings.conditions: Games that sample an RT through a differently-described image at the same address, for example a format reinterpretation or an MSAA/non-MSAA alias. Active for UFC 3 and UFC 4 because they are not in the ShouldDisableSync serial list. Not vendor specific.
findings.evidence: Not present in a8d954e: no render_target_sync or storage_image_sync files under src/video_core/renderer_vulkan. Present in 88bd144 (render_target_sync.cpp:67). NEW src/video_core/renderer_vulkan/render_target_sync.cpp:26-52 and 104-200 (UniqueImage temp.Create per MSAA-mismatch copy). NEW vk_rasterizer.cpp:1157-1160, 1351-1355.

verdict.title: Render-target alias sync: extra GPU image copies (and temp image allocations) when a texture aliases an RT written in the same submit
verdict.notes: Confirmed. OLD has no render_target_sync. NEW vk_rasterizer.cpp:1157-1160 calls CopyFromLastRt on every texture/storage bind, but it returns early unless an RT at exactly that address was written in this submit, is not the same image, and is at least as large. Copies are deduplicated per texture per submit (render_target_sync.cpp:26-52). On an MSAA mismatch it creates a temp UniqueImage, resolves, copies, and destroys it deferred (render_target_sync.cpp:104-200). It is active for the UFC serials, but whether UFC hits same-address alias images every frame is unverified. When it does fire, it costs one copy per alias per submit plus a render-pass break. That is not a big FPS cost unless it hits many textures. Origin: upstream/Shadlix (present in 88bd144). PushPendingRtAliases has no caller in NEW. No toggle.

findings.title: Fork: storage images aliasing other images are written back to memory on the GPU (tile pass + alias re-detile/upload)
findings.old_behavior: OLD had no storage-image sync. A storage image written by compute was never written back for its aliases. The cost was zero, though aliases read stale data.
findings.new_behavior: After every dispatch, StorageImageSync::Sync (storage_image_sync.cpp:59-78) calls WriteBackIfAliasesCompressed. That runs ForEachImageInRegion under the cache mutex, then the image is deferred (DeferWriteBackLocked, texture_cache.cpp:151-190) when it aliases a BC image or any image at the same address. The aliases are marked GpuDirty. On the next upload of an alias, RefreshImage (1054-1062) runs FlushPendingWriteBacks, then TileImageToBuffer (an image-to-staging copy, a tiling compute dispatch and a full memory barrier, 222-243), then the alias's detile and upload. If the game alternates the storage image and its alias every frame, that is a full tile plus detile round trip per frame. The lazy mode saved about 87% of the traffic compared with the immediate mode and Shadlix's scheduler.Finish() version, but OLD did none of this.
findings.conditions: GPU texture compression or texture generation in compute, such as UFC 4 Create Fighter skin atlases, and any game writing storage images that are also sampled through another image at the same address. Not vendor specific.
findings.ab_toggle: SHADPS4_BC_MODE (bit 1 = write back storage aliases of BC images; set 0 or 1 to disable), SHADPS4_LAZY_WRITEBACK=0 (immediate write back, slower). The non-BC alias write back has no toggle.
findings.evidence: Commits 01b32f4, 5b0e995. NEW src/video_core/texture_cache/texture_cache.cpp:151-243 (WriteBackIfAliasesCompressed, DeferWriteBackLocked, FlushPendingWriteBack(s), WriteBackImage, TileImageToBuffer), 1054-1062 (RefreshImage flush), 894-911 (FindImage writes back storage aliases before creating a BC image). NEW src/video_core/renderer_vulkan/storage_image_sync.cpp:59-78. The Shadlix base (88bd144) did a synchronous TileImage + scheduler.Finish() + TryWriteBacking here, so our fork is faster than Shadlix but still does more than OLD.

verdict.title: Fork: storage images aliasing other images are written back to memory on the GPU (tile pass + alias re-detile/upload)
verdict.notes: Confirmed: storage_image_sync.cpp:59-78 calls WriteBackIfAliasesCompressed (texture_cache.cpp:151-176), then DeferWriteBack or WriteBackImage. RefreshImage (:1054-1062) flushes pending write-backs before uploading a BC or GpuDirty alias. OLD had none of this. The origin is mixed: Shadlix 88bd144 StorageImageSync::Sync did TileImage + scheduler.Finish() + InvalidateMemory synchronously for every storage image with a same-address alias, which is far heavier, and our fork made it lazy and GPU-only. Against OLD it is extra GPU work: a tile dispatch to HostCached staging, then a detile and upload of the alias, with no CPU wait. The alias scan runs only for storage images of dispatches. In fights this is probably rare; Create Fighter pays more. Toggles: SHADPS4_BC_MODE (bit 1) for the BC part and SHADPS4_LAZY_WRITEBACK. The non-BC alias write-back has no toggle.

findings.title: Fork: block-compressed view of an uncompressed image goes through memory (tile, free image, detile) instead of ExpandImage copy

That is about 3 GPU passes instead of 1, and the uncompressed image must be recreated if the game writes it again.

findings.title: Fork: guest CPU write faults on GPU-only RT/storage memory block the guest thread on the GPU thread (flush before CPU write)
findings.old_behavior: OLD InvalidateMemory on a write fault just marked overlapping images CpuDirty/MaybeCpuDirty and untracked them. The guest thread never waited.
findings.new_behavior: NEW texture_cache.cpp:317-330: on a guest write fault (from_fault && !assume_locks, vk_rasterizer.cpp:1571), FlushBeforeCpuWrite (385-428) checks overlapping images. For any GPU-modified, non-dirty, not-written-back RT or storage image, it calls liverpool->SendCommand<true>(...), a blocking wait for the GPU command thread to run TileImageToBuffer. Then it returns without invalidating; the write retries, faults again, and the buffer cache downloads the flushed range, which needs another GPU wait. A guest thread can stall for as long as the GPU thread is busy, so streaming writes into reused RT memory give hitches. FlushWaitUs and FlushWaitMaxUs perf counters record this.
findings.conditions: Games that CPU-write into memory that recently held render targets or storage outputs, for example memory pools reused by the streaming system (UFC 4 skin atlases next to streamed assets). Windows signal path (GuestFaultSignalHandler, page_manager.cpp:221-225). Not vendor specific.
findings.evidence: Commit 01b32f4. NEW src/video_core/texture_cache/texture_cache.cpp:317-330, 385-428 (`liverpool->SendCommand<true>([this, &to_flush] { ... TileImageToBuffer(image, TileReason::CpuWrite); ...});`). NEW src/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_rasterizer.cpp:1565-1571, src/video_core/page_manager.cpp:221-225.

verdict.title: Fork: guest CPU write faults on GPU-only RT/storage memory block the guest thread on the GPU thread (flush before CPU write)
verdict.notes: Confirmed: texture_cache.cpp:318-330 and :385-428 (from 01b32f4). The guest thread waits on liverpool->SendCommand<true>, which waits for the GPU command thread to process the queued lambda. TileImageToBuffer itself does not Finish (:222-243 records a copy, a dispatch and a barrier), so this is not a GPU-idle wait. The retried write then goes through the buffer cache fault path. It triggers only when a CPU write faults on a still-tracked page overlapping a GpuModified, non-dirty, not-written-back RT or storage image. After one flush the image is WrittenBack and invalidated normally, so the cost is a stall per event, not a steady FPS cost. It can show up as hitches if streaming reuses RT memory. SHADPS4_FLUSH_CPU_WRITE=0 disables it.

findings.title: Fork: depth image read as color format gets a full compute depth->color conversion on every bind
findings.old_behavior: OLD bound a color view of the depth image directly, an invalid view that produced garbage on Arc and AMD, at no extra GPU cost.
findings.new_behavior: NEW vk_rasterizer.cpp:1196-1209: when a single-sample D16/D32 image is bound with a non-depth format, it calls texture_cache.GetDepthColorAlias (texture_cache.cpp:1382-1400, an unregistered R16/R32Uint image created once), then ConvertDepthToColor (vk_rasterizer.cpp:82-211). That does scheduler.EndRendering(), barriers, and one compute dispatch per mip over all layers. It runs on every bind, with no dirty check. UFC 3/4 have 6-layer spotlight shadow arrays. The commit reports unchanged frame rate because the reads are in compute shaders, but a fragment-shader read inside a render pass would break the pass on every draw.
findings.conditions: UFC 3 and UFC 4 shadow maps (D16 read as R16_UINT), all GPUs.
findings.evidence: Commit 7225129. NEW src/video_core/texture_cache/texture_cache.cpp:1382-1400 (GetDepthColorAlias), 1425-1433 (freed with the depth image); NEW src/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_rasterizer.cpp:72-80 (DepthAsColorEnabled), 147-204 (EndRendering + Transit + dispatch per level), 1196-1209.

verdict.title: Fork: depth image read as color format gets a full compute depth->color conversion on every bind
verdict.notes: Confirmed: vk_rasterizer.cpp:1196-1209 and :82-204 (from 7225129). There is no dirty check, so every bind gets EndRendering, barriers, and one dispatch per mip covering all layers. Shadow maps are small (D16, 6 layers). The commit reports the UFC 3 quick-fight frame rate unchanged, and the reads it targets are in compute shaders, where there is no render pass to break. Applies to UFC 3/4 on all GPUs. SHADPS4_DEPTH_AS_COLOR=0 disables it.

The default is still false in both builds (config.cpp:281 NEW / 174 OLD), and ApplyRecommendedSettings (config.cpp:1958-1969) does not change it.

verdict.notes: Confirmed: NEW texture_cache.cpp:988-991 adds tiled RTs with width <= 8, and the downloads are sync. OLD :596-599 downloaded linear RTs only, asynchronously. The default is false in both builds (NEW config.cpp:281, OLD :174), and ApplyRecommendedSettings (:1958-1969) does not touch it. So it matters only for players who turned it on. In that case it is medium to high, because every linear RT bound each frame forces a Finish().

findings.title: Small extra CPU work per bind or fault in the texture cache
findings.old_behavior: OLD FindView and GetBarriers did no string compares. GetSampler was a lock-free hash lookup. InvalidateMemory had no extra region scans.
findings.new_behavior: Image::FindView (image.cpp:215-216) and GetBarriers (241-242) compare MemoryPatcher::g_game_serial against two strings on every call. GetSampler takes samplers_mutex and touches an LRU on every call (texture_cache.cpp:~1140-1155). Every write fault runs an extra ForEachImageInRegion under the mutex (FlushBeforeCpuWrite). RefreshImage runs FlushPendingWriteBacks over the region for BC or GpuDirty images. WriteBackIfAliasesCompressed scans the region for each storage image after every dispatch.
findings.conditions: CPU-bound scenes with many draws; matters most on weak CPUs. Typically under 1-2%.
findings.evidence: NEW src/video_core/texture_cache/image.cpp:215-216, 241-242 (upstream/Shadlix); texture_cache.cpp:151-170, 1058-1062, 385-399 (fork).

verdict.title: Small extra CPU work per bind or fault in the texture cache
verdict.notes: Confirmed, but negligible. image.cpp:215-216 and :241-242 compare g_game_serial to two literals on every call. GetSampler (texture_cache.cpp:1141-1157) now takes samplers_mutex and touches an LRU, where OLD :751-756 did neither. The extra scans are per fault or per storage dispatch only. Well under 1% in practice.

findings.title: Tiling/detiling: precompiled SPIR-V with specialization constants and staging-pool scratch (less stutter and CPU per texture upload)
findings.old_behavior: OLD tile_manager.cpp:137 compiled the tiling GLSL at runtime with glslang (Vulkan::Compile with #defines) the first time each tile mode/bpp was used, which caused first-use hitches. Every DetileImage (line 189) and TileImage (line 274) called GetScratchBuffer, a fresh vmaCreateBuffer of guest_size (78-95), plus a deferred vmaDestroyBuffer. That is one VMA allocation per texture upload or write-back.
findings.new_behavior: NEW tile_manager.cpp:153 uses precompiled SPIR-V per bpp and micro/macro mode with specialization constants (pipeline creation only, no GLSL compile). Scratch memory comes from runtime.GetStagingPool().Request(...) (lines 221, 306, 395), so there are no per-upload VMA allocations, and barriers are batched through Runtime. Texture streaming (loading screens, fighter swaps) should hitch less and use less CPU.
findings.conditions: Texture uploads, detiling and write-backs, all GPUs. Most visible during streaming and first appearance of new tile modes.
findings.evidence: diff a8d954e..88bd144 src/video_core/texture_cache/tile_manager.cpp: `- const auto& module = Vulkan::Compile(HostShaders::TILING_COMP, ...defines)` replaced by `+ const auto module = Vulkan::CompileSPV(code, device);`, and `- GetScratchBuffer(info.guest_size)` replaced by `+ runtime.GetStagingPool().Request(info.guest_size, MemoryType::DeviceLocal, 256, false, true)`.

verdict.title: Tiling/detiling: precompiled SPIR-V with specialization constants and staging-pool scratch (less stutter and CPU per texture upload)
verdict.notes: Confirmed. OLD tile_manager.cpp:137 compiled GLSL at runtime once per pipeline variant, and :78-95, :189 and :274 did vmaCreateBuffer per detile or tile plus a deferred destroy. NEW uses CompileSPV at :153 and StagingPool.Request at :221, :306 and :395. The gain is mostly in streaming and loading (fewer first-use hitches, less VMA churn), not steady-state FPS in fights. One counterpoint: NEW TileImage now writes its output to HostCached staging (:306) instead of device-local scratch plus a stream buffer. Origin: upstream.

findings.title: More cached-image reuse: format-compatible views instead of new image + copy; MSAA images may skip storage usage
findings.old_behavior: OLD ImageInfo::IsCompatible required the exact same pixel_format, so for example an UNORM view of an SRGB image created or expanded a new image. All color images, MSAA included, got eStorage usage, which can disable MSAA compression on some drivers.
findings.new_behavior: NEW image_info.cpp:147-151 IsCompatible accepts IsVulkanFormatCompatible in either direction, so ResolveOverlap reuses the cached image as a view more often. NEW image.cpp:36-37 adds eStorage to MSAA images only when the device supports multisample storage. Our fork (texture_cache.cpp:581-590) expands rather than drops a compatible-format image that needs more mips, which avoids a stale re-upload. One minor counterpoint: block-compressed images now get eStorage usage (image.cpp:42-47), which should be harmless.
findings.conditions: Games using SRGB/UNORM reinterpretation (common), MSAA render targets on GPUs without MS storage support.
findings.evidence: diff a8d954e..88bd144 image_info.cpp: `- return (pixel_format == info.pixel_format && ...` replaced by `+ return (IsVulkanFormatCompatible(pixel_format, info.pixel_format) || IsVulkanFormatCompatible(info.pixel_format, pixel_format)) && ...`; image.cpp `+ if (info.num_samples == 1 || instance.IsMultisampleStorageImageSupported())`.

verdict.title: More cached-image reuse: format-compatible views instead of new image + copy; MSAA images may skip storage usage
verdict.notes: Confirmed: image_info.cpp:147-151 relaxes IsCompatible, and image.cpp:45-46 adds eStorage for MSAA images only when MS storage is supported. Arc, NVIDIA and AMD all expose shaderStorageImageMultisample, so the MSAA part changes nothing on the players' GPUs. The format reuse saves an occasional copy. Negligible either way.

missed_by_analyst: 1) NEW keeps the async download path in DownloadImageMemory (texture_cache.cpp:141-148, DeferPriorityOperation) but never uses it, because ProcessDownloadImages hardcodes sync=true (:105). Flipping that one argument is the cheapest A/B for the biggest suspected regression, and no setting or env var exposes it. 2) In both builds GpuModified is never cleared after a download, so in NEW any image that keeps getting queued (1x1 RT on every RT bind, linear storage on every storage bind) pays a Finish() each time, with no check for whether it changed. 3) Besides never evicting, the dead GC means gc_tick stays 0. All LRU touches (images and the new sampler LRU) then record tick 0, and the RunGarbageCollector thresholds (pressure_gc_memory and critical_gc_memory, which got new floors in NEW) are never consulted. Even an explicit RunGarbageCollector call would start from broken LRU ages, since ticks_to_destroy = min(..., gc_tick) = 0. 4) For context on origin: Shadlix 88bd144 StorageImageSync::Sync did TileImage + scheduler.Finish() synchronously for every aliased storage image after each dispatch. Our fork's lazy write-back (5b0e995) is therefore a large improvement over the Shadlix base, though it is still more work than OLD. I found no other texture-cache sync point. The only Finish() calls in NEW src/video_core/texture_cache are :137 (sync download) and :1348 (inside the dead GC).

summary:
I read the full diff of vk_rasterizer.cpp/.h and vk_scheduler.cpp/.h. render_target_sync, vk_predication, vk_runtime and vk_staging_buffer_pool do not exist in OLD, so I read the whole NEW files. I also followed calls into storage_image_sync.cpp, texture_cache.cpp and liverpool.cpp where the rasterizer triggers them.

The biggest new costs in NEW are four things OLD did not do at all:
1. Every draw into a 1x1 render target queues a synchronous image download. RenderTargetSync::Schedule1x1Readback leads to TextureCache::ProcessDownloadImages, which calls DownloadImageMemory(sync=true) and then scheduler.Finish(). ProcessDownloadImages runs at every EOP/EOS fence, so each such frame gets a full CPU-GPU stall. This came from Shadlix, has no toggle, and UFC serials are not on its exclusion list. OLD downloaded asynchronously on a worker thread and never read back 1x1 targets.
2. Our fork's depth-as-color path (commit 7225129) re-converts the whole depth image with a compute pass on every texture bind. It also ends the render pass each time. This hits UFC 3, which reads its D16 shadow map as R16_UINT. A/B with SHADPS4_DEPTH_AS_COLOR=0.
3. RenderTargetSync::CopyFromLastRt copies a render target into a same-address alias texture. Each copy breaks the render pass and copies the whole image. The once-per-submit dedup resets every time the render target is bound again. This came from Shadlix.
4. StorageImageSync::Sync runs after every compute dispatch, for each storage image it writes. It costs texture-cache lock and region-walk CPU time, plus deferred tile write-backs. Shadlix did scheduler.Finish() here on every dispatch; our fork made it lazy, but it is still more work than OLD.

Smaller costs from our fork: the FMASK-decompress fast-clear expansion (SHADPS4_FMASK_DECOMPRESS) and the CMASK fill (SHADPS4_CMASK_EXPAND).

Unclear direction: real ZPASS occlusion queries. Note that PredicationManager::supported is never set, so GPU conditional rendering is never used. Predicated packets are only skipped on the CPU, from counters already in guest memory.

Changes that make NEW faster, all from upstream/Shadlix:
- Barriers are batched in Runtime, with exact buffer-range hazard checks.
- Buffer uploads use a separate upload command buffer, so they no longer break the render pass.
- Staging buffers never wait on the GPU.
- Garbage collection moved off the per-submit path.
- Compute image clears become vkCmdClear, and fills/copies use CPU paths when the memory is not GPU-modified.
- The DMA path is much cheaper (DMA is off by default in both).

No default setting in my area differs in a way that matters: Readback Linear Images, DMA and Collect Debug Logs default to off in both builds. Buffers were bound as storage buffers in OLD too, so that is not a difference.

findings.title: 1x1 render targets force a synchronous GPU readback (scheduler.Finish) at every fence
findings.old_behavior: No readback of 1x1 render targets. Image downloads (only with readbackLinearImages) were recorded and handed to DownloadedImagesThread, which waited on the semaphore on its own thread. The emulator thread never stalled.
findings.new_behavior: BeginRendering calls rt_sync_.Schedule1x1Readback(image_id) for every draw whose color target is 1x1, which queues TextureCache::AddDownload. At the next EOP/EOS fence, liverpool calls ProcessDownloadImages, which calls DownloadImageMemory(id, sync=true). That records a copy and then calls scheduler.Finish(): submit, then wait until the GPU is idle. CPU and GPU stop overlapping for the rest of that frame.
findings.conditions: Any game that renders to a 1x1 target, which is typical for auto-exposure/average luminance and GPU-to-CPU result pixels. UFC 3/4 serials (CUSA14204/14209/06534) are not on the exclusion list (only CUSA11227, 12982, 00093, 00003, 01778, 01627 and the ShouldDisableSync list). Applies to every GPU vendor. It costs most where the CPU and GPU frame times are close.
findings.ab_toggle: none (excluded only by a hard-coded game serial list; no setting or env var)
findings.evidence: NEW vk_rasterizer.cpp:1347-1356 (`if (!ShouldDisableSync() && serial != "CUSA11227" ...) { rt_sync_.RecordRtWrite(...); if (desc.info.size.width == 1 && desc.info.size.height == 1) rt_sync_.Schedule1x1Readback(image_id); }`). render_target_sync.cpp:67-69 (AddDownload). texture_cache.cpp:102-108 (ProcessDownloadImages -> DownloadImageMemory(image_id, true)) and 136-140 (`if (sync) { scheduler.Finish(); ...`). liverpool.cpp:768-771 and 789-792 (EOS/EOP call ProcessDownloadImages + OnFence). The same Finish already exists at 88bd144 (Shadlix). OLD texture_cache.cpp:96-147: async download via downloaded_images_queue + DownloadedImagesThread, no Finish.

verdict.title: 1x1 render targets force a synchronous GPU readback (scheduler.Finish) at every fence
verdict.notes: Confirmed. NEW vk_rasterizer.cpp:1346-1356 calls Schedule1x1Readback for any 1x1 color target unless the serial is excluded. UFC serials are not excluded. render_target_sync.cpp:67-69 calls texture_cache.AddDownload. texture_cache.cpp:102-108 ProcessDownloadImages calls DownloadImageMemory(id, true) once per queued image, and lines 136-140 call scheduler.Finish(). That means one full submit-and-wait-for-idle per queued image. The drain runs from more places than the analyst listed: OnSubmit (vk_rasterizer.cpp:649), OnFence (672), and liverpool.cpp EOS 770, EOP 791, WriteData of 8 bytes or less 846, Rewind 890, 1257 and 1293. So it can stall more than once per frame. The same code is already in 88bd144 (Shadlix). OLD has no 1x1 readback, and its downloads were asynchronous (OLD texture_cache.cpp:89-147 DownloadedImagesThread). The image re-qualifies every frame it is rendered to, because FindRenderTarget sets GpuModified. Unconfirmed: whether UFC 3/4 render to a 1x1 target, as typical auto-exposure chains do. If they do, CPU/GPU overlap is lost every frame, and >15% is plausible on GPU-bound systems. If they don't, the cost is zero. No setting or env var controls it; only a hard-coded serial list.

findings.title: Depth image read as a color format is re-converted by a compute pass on every bind (UFC 3 shadow map)
findings.old_behavior: A depth image sampled through a color format (e.g. D16 read as R16_UINT) was bound directly. That view is invalid in Vulkan and gives garbage on Intel/AMD, but costs nothing extra.
findings.new_behavior: BindTextures calls ConvertDepthToColor(depth, alias) every time such a texture is bound. Each call does scheduler.EndRendering() (render pass break), up to two layout barriers, and a compute dispatch over every mip and layer of the full depth image into an R16/R32 alias. Nothing records whether the depth changed since the last conversion, so every draw sampling the shadow map converts it again and restarts the render pass.
findings.conditions: Games that sample depth through a color format. Confirmed for UFC 3 (its D16 shadow map). It scales with the number of draws sampling it per frame and with the shadow map size and layer count. All GPUs.
findings.ab_toggle: SHADPS4_DEPTH_AS_COLOR=0 (restores the old direct bind; shadows break on Intel/AMD)
findings.evidence: Fork commit 7225129. NEW vk_rasterizer.cpp:75-81 (DepthAsColorEnabled), 83-212 (ConvertDepthToColor: EndRendering at 146, Transit/FlushBarriers at 150-158, per-level dispatch loop ending in `cmdbuf.dispatch((w + 7) / 8, (h + 7) / 8, layers)`), 1197-1208 (called unconditionally in BindTextures when `!is_storage && is_depth && !IsFormatDepthCompatible(view fmt)`). texture_cache.cpp:1382-1402 caches only the alias image, not whether it is up to date.

verdict.title: Depth image read as a color format is re-converted by a compute pass on every bind (UFC 3 shadow map)
verdict.notes: Confirmed. This is our fork (7225129); see git diff 88bd144 12739d2. Lines 1194-1208 run inside the second pass of BindTextures, which is part of BindResources and runs before BeginRendering, on every draw or dispatch that samples the depth surface through a non-depth format. ConvertDepthToColor (83-212) always calls scheduler.EndRendering() (146), transitions the depth image to DepthStencilReadOnly and the alias to General over the full range, then flushes. It dispatches over every level and layer. There is no 'already converted since last depth write' check. Back in BindTextures (1232-1239), the alias then moves General->ShaderReadOnly, which is another barrier. So every such draw costs a render pass restart, 2-3 barriers and a full-resolution compute copy. With N draws sampling a 2048^2 D16 map, that is about N x 16 MB of traffic. Large on iGPUs and Arc. Only games that read depth as color are affected (UFC 3 according to the code comment; UFC 4 is not confirmed). A/B: SHADPS4_DEPTH_AS_COLOR=0. The OLD direct bind is invalid Vulkan but costs nothing.

findings.title: Render-target to same-address alias copies on texture bind (RenderTargetSync::CopyFromLastRt)
findings.old_behavior: No render-target-to-alias synchronization. A texture at the same address as a render target but in a different cached image kept stale data, with no copies.
findings.new_behavior: For every texture binding, CopyFromLastRt looks the address up among render targets recorded this submit. If the render target is a different image, it transitions both images (FlushBarriers, which ends the render pass) and copies the whole image (vkCmdCopyImage). It then transitions both back and flushes barriers again. The once-per-submit dedup (pending_rt_copied_) is erased by RecordRtWrite every time that render target is bound again, so alternating render/sample patterns copy on every draw. For MSAA-to-single-sample it creates and destroys a temporary VkImage per copy (allocation) and does a resolve plus a copy.
findings.conditions: Games that render to an address and sample it through a different-format or different-size image (format aliasing, ping-pong post effects). Not on the excluded serial list for UFC. All GPUs.
findings.evidence: NEW vk_rasterizer.cpp:1157-1160 (CopyFromLastRt in the first pass of BindTextures) and 1351 (RecordRtWrite per color attachment per draw). render_target_sync.cpp:20-24 (RecordRtWrite erases dedup), 26-53, 102-195 (MSAA path: temp.Create, EndRendering, resolve + copy, FlushBarriers), 197-223 (copy + 2x FlushBarriers). Not in OLD. Not in the fork diff 88bd144..12739d2.

verdict.title: Render-target to same-address alias copies on texture bind (RenderTargetSync::CopyFromLastRt)
verdict.notes: Confirmed in NEW vk_rasterizer.cpp:1157-1160 and render_target_sync.cpp:20-53 and 102-223. Not in OLD. Already present in 88bd144, so it came from upstream/Shadlix. A copy happens only when FindImage returns a different image from the render target recorded at the same address in this submit, and the render target is at least as large. The common case, where the texture resolves to the RT image itself, returns early (rt_id == tex_id). RecordRtWrite (line 23) erases the dedup entry on every draw to that RT, so alternating render-then-sample patterns copy again each time. The non-MSAA path ends with an unconditional FlushBarriers, and transitions mean a render pass break. The MSAA path creates and destroys a VkImage per copy. Whether UFC hits this is unverified; real cost happens only with format or size aliasing. No setting or env var controls it (serial list only).

findings.title: Storage-image alias sync after every compute dispatch
findings.old_behavior: After a dispatch, only ResetBindings ran. Storage images aliased by other images were not synchronized.
findings.new_behavior: After every DispatchDirect/DispatchIndirect, StorageImageSync::Sync runs for each storage image written. It does ~30 serial compares, then WriteBackIfAliasesCompressed, which takes the texture-cache mutex and walks the region (BcMode default 3). Then HasAliasAtAddress walks the page table. If an alias exists, DeferWriteBack takes the mutex, walks the region again and marks every alias GpuDirty. The real tile-to-buffer write-back happens later, when an alias is used, and the alias is re-uploaded. Shadlix 88bd144 did a scheduler.Finish() per dispatch here; our fork made it lazy, so it is far cheaper than Shadlix but still more than OLD.
findings.conditions: Compute-heavy scenes that write storage images with aliases at the same address (UFC 4 Create Fighter, post-processing). CPU cost on every dispatch with storage images; GPU cost when aliases are later sampled.
findings.ab_toggle: SHADPS4_LAZY_WRITEBACK=0 (immediate GPU write-back instead of deferred), SHADPS4_BC_MODE (bit 2 controls the compressed-alias write-back); no way to disable the whole sync except the serial list
findings.evidence: NEW vk_rasterizer.cpp:586-590 and 628-632 (`if (!ShouldDisableSync()) for (...) storage_sync_.Sync(id)`), 1225-1230 (pending_storage_image_ids_). storage_image_sync.cpp:45-79. texture_cache.cpp:152-178 (WriteBackIfAliasesCompressed, mutex + ForEachImageInRegion), 188-208 (DeferWriteBackLocked). Fork diff storage_image_sync.cpp removed the Shadlix `scheduler.Finish()` write-back (fork commit 5b0e995).

verdict.title: Storage-image alias sync after every compute dispatch
verdict.notes: Confirmed: NEW vk_rasterizer.cpp:586-590 and 628-632, storage_image_sync.cpp:45-79. OLD DispatchDirect (old 304-332) only does ResetBindings. pending_storage_image_ids_ also collects storage images bound by graphics draws, but Sync only runs after dispatches. With the default lazy write-back, the per-dispatch cost is CPU-side: serial compares, texture-cache mutex plus region walk (WriteBackIfAliasesCompressed, BcMode bit value 2), and a page-table lookup. GPU work is recorded only when an alias exists: deferred tiling and an alias re-upload when the alias is next used. Our fork removed Shadlix's per-dispatch Finish (fork diff of storage_image_sync.cpp), so NEW is much cheaper than Shadlix 88bd144. Against OLD it is a small CPU cost plus GPU cost only in alias-heavy scenes, such as UFC 4 Create Fighter (code comment). I downgrade the magnitude to low for fights, medium only in such menus. A/B: SHADPS4_LAZY_WRITEBACK, SHADPS4_BC_MODE.

findings.title: Synchronous downloads for linear storage/volume images (Finish per fence)
findings.old_behavior: FindTexture queued a download only when readbackLinearImages was on, and the download was asynchronous on a worker thread.
findings.new_behavior: FindTexture always queues a download for linear volume storage images. With our fork it also queues every linear 2D storage image of at least 64x64 written by compute (ReadbackLinearStorage, default on). Each queued image costs a scheduler.Finish() at the next fence (same path as the first finding).
findings.conditions: Games that write linear images with compute. UFC 4 does this for fighter picture encoding (save path), so mostly menus; other games may do it every frame. All GPUs.
findings.ab_toggle: SHADPS4_LINEAR_STORAGE_READBACK=0 (fork part); readbackLinearImages setting (default off in both builds) for render targets
findings.evidence: Mixed origin: the sync Finish is from Shadlix; the ReadbackLinearStorage trigger is ours (fork commit e565b66). texture_cache.cpp:87-97 (ReadbackLinearStorage, fork), 962-982 (FindTexture queues download), 102-108/136-140 (sync Finish). OLD texture_cache.cpp FindTexture: only `if (Config::getReadbackLinearImages() && !is_tiled)` and async download.

verdict.title: Synchronous downloads for linear storage/volume images (Finish per fence)
verdict.notes: Confirmed at NEW texture_cache.cpp:962-982. 'Storage' here means any image binding with is_written (texture_cache.h:75), from graphics or compute, not only compute. Any linear, non-depth, non-block image of 64x64 or larger that is bound writable is queued, and each one costs a scheduler.Finish at the next drain point. OLD (old texture_cache.cpp FindTexture ~584-588) queued only when readbackLinearImages was on (default false in both builds), and the download was asynchronous. Origin is mixed: the volume-image path and the sync Finish are Shadlix (88bd144:645-646, 101); the ReadbackLinearStorage trigger is our fork (e565b66). If UFC writes such an image every frame, this is a per-frame full stall (could be high). The fork comment says only the save-picture path does, which would make it mostly menus. Not verified for gameplay. A/B: SHADPS4_LINEAR_STORAGE_READBACK=0 covers the fork part only.

findings.title: Real ZPASS occlusion queries and CPU-side predication instead of fake counters
findings.old_behavior: SET_PREDICATION was ignored (all draws executed). PixelPipeStatDump wrote a fake, always-visible counter right away on the CPU.
findings.new_behavior: While the game enables ZPASS counting, every draw gets vkCmdBeginQuery/vkCmdEndQuery (query slots are host-reset in bulk). Without hostQueryReset, every draw would also end the render pass, but all target GPUs have it. Counters reach guest memory only through a DeferOperation after the GPU tick completes. PredicationManager::supported is never set to true, so GPU conditional rendering is never used. EnableFromZpass/EnableFromBool fall back to CPU-static: predicated packets are skipped only when guest memory already holds final counters showing nothing visible. That can save GPU work, which makes NEW faster.
findings.conditions: Games using occlusion queries or predication (not confirmed for UFC). Late counters could stall a game that waits on them on the CPU.
findings.evidence: NEW vk_rasterizer.cpp:435-449 and 516-532 (PrepareDrawQuery/BeginDraw/EndDraw per draw). vk_predication.cpp:319-349, 351-379, 210-237 (deferred counter write), 239-267 (`if (!supported ...) SetStatic(nullopt)`). vk_predication.h:112 (`bool supported{};` never assigned). liverpool.cpp:290-299 (CPU skip), 456-487, 725-745. OLD liverpool.cpp:411-412 (`Unimplemented IT_SET_PREDICATION`) and 611-620 (fake counter).

verdict.title: Real ZPASS occlusion queries and CPU-side predication instead of fake counters
verdict.notes: Confirmed. vk_predication.cpp:319-379 (PrepareDrawQuery/BeginDraw/EndDraw). The per-draw query is used only while counting_enabled. The EndRendering-per-draw path applies only without hostQueryReset, which all targets support. vk_predication.h:112 `bool supported{}` is never set, so GPU conditional rendering is never used. Nothing shows that UFC uses ZPASS or predication, so I treat it as not FPS-relevant unless that is shown.

findings.title: Every written storage buffer invalidates cached images at the same address
findings.old_behavior: texture_cache.InvalidateMemoryFromGPU was called only for buffers that are both written and formatted.
findings.new_behavior: It is called for every written buffer binding on every draw/dispatch: texture-cache mutex plus ForEachImageInRegion. Matching images are marked GpuDirty and are re-uploaded on next use.
findings.conditions: Shaders writing storage buffers (UAVs, GDS-style counters), most often in compute-heavy games. CPU cost per write binding, plus re-uploads when an image starts at the same address.
findings.evidence: NEW vk_rasterizer.cpp:1089-1092 (`if (desc.is_written) texture_cache.InvalidateMemoryFromGPU(...)`). OLD vk_rasterizer.cpp ~605: `if (desc.is_written && desc.is_formatted)`.

verdict.title: Every written storage buffer invalidates cached images at the same address
verdict.notes: Confirmed. NEW vk_rasterizer.cpp:1089-1092 versus OLD 595-597 (`is_written && is_formatted`). InvalidateMemoryFromGPU is the same function in both builds (mutex plus ForEachImageInRegion, marking GpuDirty only for images whose base address matches exactly). Small CPU cost per written buffer binding. A re-upload happens only when an image shares the exact base address. Origin upstream/Shadlix (not in the fork diff).

findings.title: New depth/stencil layout and per-draw depth attachment elision can add render pass restarts
findings.old_behavior: A depth target without depth writes always used DepthStencilReadOnlyOptimal (even with stencil writes). It was attached whenever depth or stencil was enabled and valid.
findings.new_behavior: With stencil writes on and depth writes off, the layout is eDepthReadOnlyStencilAttachmentOptimal (correct). Draws that switch between this and the other layouts need a layout barrier, so FlushBarriers ends the render pass. GetEffectiveDepthStencilState also drops the depth attachment for draws where depth/stencil have no effect. That changes RenderState and restarts rendering when neighbouring draws differ, though it can also avoid work.
findings.conditions: Scenes that alternate stencil-writing passes (light volumes, masks) with depth-tested draws on the same depth buffer.
findings.evidence: NEW vk_rasterizer.cpp:1418-1430 (stencil_write layout selection), 297-298 / 1754-1757 (GetEffectiveDepthStencilState). vk_depth_stencil_state.h:18-80. OLD vk_rasterizer.cpp:806-812.

verdict.title: New depth/stencil layout and per-draw depth attachment elision can add render pass restarts
verdict.notes: Confirmed. NEW vk_rasterizer.cpp:1418-1427 adds eDepthReadOnlyStencilAttachmentOptimal when stencil_enable is set with depth writes off. OLD 806-811 used DepthStencilReadOnly. Alternating between the two layouts costs a barrier and a render pass break. GetEffectiveDepthStencilState (334) can drop the attachment. No evidence that UFC alternates like this. Cost is speculative and small, and could go either way.

findings.title: FMASK decompress now expands fast clears
findings.old_behavior: FMASK decompress draws were skipped and did nothing.
