findings.new_behavior: Each FMASK decompress pass calls EliminateFastClear: a texture-cache FindImage/FindRenderTarget lookup, and if the CMASK is cleared, or the target is MSAA and was never rendered, a ClearImage (EndRendering + vkCmdClearColorImage).
findings.conditions: MSAA render targets with fast clear (UFC 4 tattoo layer). A few times per frame.
findings.evidence: Fork commit 789551b. NEW vk_rasterizer.cpp:262-273, 361-384 (undefined_msaa check, runtime.ClearImage). OLD vk_rasterizer.cpp:69-73 (only a marker).

verdict.title: FMASK decompress now expands fast clears
verdict.notes: Confirmed. Fork 789551b, NEW vk_rasterizer.cpp:262-273 and 366-398. Runs only on FMASK-decompress passes, at most a few per frame. A ClearImage happens only when the CMASK is cleared or MSAA is undefined. Negligible for FPS. A/B: SHADPS4_FMASK_DECOMPRESS=0.

findings.title: CMASK reads trigger a GPU fill of the CMASK range
findings.old_behavior: Shaders reading CMASK as a buffer read whatever was in it.
findings.new_behavior: On every bind of a buffer that is a registered CMASK, runtime.FillBuffer(0xFFFFFFFF) runs: EndRendering, a barrier if needed, and vkCmdFillBuffer. The next draw that reads it then sees a write hazard and flushes barriers again.
findings.conditions: UFC 4 native-resolution UI composite, about once per frame.
findings.evidence: Fork commit 630b4e7. NEW vk_rasterizer.cpp:1058-1080.

verdict.title: CMASK reads trigger a GPU fill of the CMASK range
verdict.notes: Confirmed. Fork 630b4e7, NEW vk_rasterizer.cpp:1058-1080. Runs once per bind of a read-only buffer whose base is a registered CMASK, about once per frame in UFC 4. One fill buffer plus EndRendering is negligible. Adds one IsMeta lookup per buffer binding. A/B: SHADPS4_CMASK_EXPAND=0.

findings.title: Extra per-draw CPU bookkeeping
findings.old_behavior: None of these checks existed.
findings.new_behavior: ShouldDisableSync() does ~24 string_view compares and runs for each texture binding, each color target and each dispatch. StorageImageSync::Sync adds ~30 more compares per storage image. RecordRtWrite does a robin_map insert and a std::map erase per color target per draw. PopPendingOperations now takes a recursive mutex per draw. ResetBindings adds interval-set entries per bound buffer. With Collect Debug Logs on, there is also a std::set emplace per >=1280-wide render target per draw. Each item is cheap, but together they add maybe a few hundred ns to ~1 us per draw.
findings.conditions: CPU-bound scenes with many draws (weak CPUs, Intel/AMD iGPU laptops).
findings.ab_toggle: Collect Debug Logs / SHADPS4_DEBUG_LOGS=0 for the debug part only
findings.evidence: NEW vk_rasterizer.cpp:40-50, 1157, 1346-1356, 586, 628. storage_image_sync.cpp:46-58. render_target_sync.cpp:20-24. vk_scheduler.cpp PopPendingOperations (pending_ops_mutex). Debug-log part is ours: vk_rasterizer.cpp ~1333-1345 in the fork diff.

verdict.title: Extra per-draw CPU bookkeeping
verdict.notes: The individual items exist: ShouldDisableSync at 40-50 (about 24 compares), RecordRtWrite with a robin_map insert and a std::map erase of a usually missing key, an uncontended recursive_mutex in PopPendingOperations, and the debug-only std::set. PerfAdd and NotifyComputeDispatch are no-ops unless debug logs are on. Sub-microsecond per draw in total. Not a plausible cause of a noticeable FPS difference.

findings.title: Batched, range-precise barriers via Runtime (faster)
findings.old_behavior: Every Image::Transit call immediately did EndRendering plus its own pipelineBarrier2 (src AllCommands). Buffer barriers came per buffer whenever its whole-buffer access mask changed.
findings.new_behavior: Transits and buffer accesses are collected in Runtime. There is at most one pipelineBarrier2 per draw/dispatch (FlushBarriers), and only when a real overlapping hazard exists (write_ranges/read_ranges interval checks). Fewer barrier calls and fewer render pass breaks for read-only buffers.
findings.conditions: All games and GPUs. Most noticeable with many draws per frame.
findings.evidence: NEW vk_runtime.cpp Transit (~158-164), IsBufferAccessed/AccessBuffer/FlushBarriers (~681-756). vk_rasterizer.cpp:428-431, 1235-1252, 819-834 (ResetBindings). OLD vk_rasterizer.cpp:590-595 (vk_buffer->GetBarrier) and OLD image.cpp Transit (EndRendering + pipelineBarrier2 per call).

verdict.title: Batched, range-precise barriers via Runtime (faster)
verdict.notes: Partly overstated. OLD Image::Transit (old image.cpp ~302-325) issued EndRendering plus a barrier only when GetBarriers returned something, that is, on a real layout or access change, not on every call. NEW batches transitions into one FlushBarriers per draw (vk_runtime.cpp:723-751), which is cheaper. There is a counter-case, though. NEW IsBufferAccessed (vk_runtime.cpp ~680-688) flushes, which also ends rendering, on any overlap with a range written since the last flush, including write-after-write. OLD Buffer::GetBarrier (old buffer.h:128-149) skipped the barrier when the access mask and stage were unchanged. So consecutive draws writing the same storage range now break the render pass every draw, where OLD did not. Net effect is probably slightly positive. I call it low, not medium.

findings.title: Uploads in a separate command buffer, staging buffers that never wait on the GPU, priority deferred-op thread (faster)
findings.old_behavior: Buffer-cache uploads were recorded in the main command buffer with scheduler.EndRendering(), breaking the render pass on each upload. Stream/utility buffers could wait for GPU reuse.
findings.new_behavior: Each scheduler session has an upload command buffer (UploadCommandBuffer) that is submitted ahead of the primary one, so uploads no longer interrupt rendering. StagingBufferPool grows its 16 MB ring blocks or dedicated buffers instead of waiting. Deferred readback completions run on a separate PriorityPendingOpsThread. Minor caveat: idle dedicated staging buffers are trimmed after 120 submits and reallocated when needed, which can cause small allocation hitches.
findings.conditions: All games. Most benefit in streaming-heavy scenes.
findings.evidence: NEW vk_scheduler.cpp: UploadCommandBuffer (~94-105), BeginSession/EndSession, SubmitExecution submits upload+primary per session, PriorityPendingOpsThread. buffer_cache.cpp:479 (`scheduler.UploadCommandBuffer()`). vk_staging_buffer_pool.cpp:47-134 (no waits), 146-182 (trim). OLD buffer_cache.cpp has EndRendering at 217, 436, 651, 780, 916, 1043, 1095, 1106, 1170.

verdict.title: Uploads in a separate command buffer, staging buffers that never wait on the GPU, priority deferred-op thread (faster)
verdict.notes: Confirmed. NEW vk_scheduler.cpp UploadCommandBuffer and sessions; buffer_cache.cpp:479 records uploads into the upload command buffer. OLD buffer_cache.cpp had EndRendering at 217, 436, 651, 780, 916, 1043, 1095, 1106 and 1170, plus a Wait at 204 and a Finish at 232. Caveat: FlushSyncBatch(false), reached through CommitPendingGpuRanges (called by liverpool at fences, WriteData and Rewind), calls scheduler.BeginSession() (buffer_cache.cpp:545-547). That ends the primary command buffer and invalidates dynamic state, though mostly at points where OLD would also break. The staging pool grows instead of waiting (vk_staging_buffer_pool.cpp:47-134), and trimming is as described.

findings.title: Less work per submit: garbage collection is async and rare (faster)
findings.old_behavior: OnSubmit ran ProcessFaultBuffer (when DMA was used), texture-cache GC, buffer-cache preemptive downloads and buffer-cache GC on every submit.
findings.new_behavior: OnSubmit does buffer_cache.TickFrame and ProcessDownloadImages, clears sync records, and starts RunGarbageCollectorAsync only every 60 submits and only above the memory trigger.
findings.conditions: All games.
findings.evidence: NEW vk_rasterizer.cpp:646-665. OLD vk_rasterizer.cpp:373-382.

verdict.title: Less work per submit: garbage collection is async and rare (faster)
verdict.notes: Confirmed: NEW vk_rasterizer.cpp:646-665 versus OLD 373-382. OLD ran texture GC, buffer preemptive downloads and buffer GC on every submit.

findings.title: Compute clear/copy shortcuts and CPU fast paths (faster)
findings.old_behavior: Compute clear shaders ran as real dispatches. InlineData/CopyBuffer always went through the buffer cache on the GPU.
findings.new_behavior: IsComputeImageClear turns recognized 64-thread clear dispatches into a single vkCmdClearColorImage. FillBuffer/CopyBuffer use plain memset/memcpy when the range is not GPU-modified.
findings.conditions: Games that use the Gnm compute clear/copy helpers.
findings.evidence: NEW vk_rasterizer.cpp:935-992 (IsComputeImageClear), 1497-1554 (FillBuffer/CopyBuffer fast paths). OLD vk_rasterizer.cpp InlineData/CopyBuffer delegated to buffer_cache.

verdict.title: Compute clear/copy shortcuts and CPU fast paths (faster)
verdict.notes: Partly wrong. IsComputeImageClear (NEW 935-992) is new and real. But OLD BufferCache::CopyBuffer (old buffer_cache.cpp:382-392) already had the same memcpy fast path, and OLD InlineData already wrote to CPU memory when the region was unregistered. Only the FillBuffer memset path is new. Effect is minor and depends on the game; there is no evidence for UFC.

findings.title: DMA path much cheaper (faster when DMA is enabled)
findings.old_behavior: Every draw/dispatch from a shader using DMA looped over all GPU-mapped ranges, calling SynchronizeBuffersInRange plus a MemoryBarrier, under the mapped_ranges lock.
findings.new_behavior: buffer_cache.SynchronizeDmaBuffers() walks only resident arena ranges.
findings.conditions: Only with Direct Memory Access enabled (default off in both OLD and NEW) and shaders that use DMA.
findings.evidence: NEW vk_rasterizer.cpp:704-706. buffer_cache.cpp:220-228. OLD vk_rasterizer.cpp:413-423.

verdict.title: DMA path much cheaper (faster when DMA is enabled)
verdict.notes: Confirmed: NEW 704-706 versus OLD 413-423. But uses_dma is forced false unless directMemoryAccess is on (shader_info_collection_pass.cpp:182-183 in NEW, 179-180 in OLD). Default is false in both builds, and ApplyRecommendedSettings (config.cpp:1958-1968) does not enable it. No effect at default settings.

missed_by_analyst:
1) The analyst missed a fork-only GPU-thread round trip in the CPU write-fault path. Fork commit 84c6ede/01b32f4 made Rasterizer::InvalidateMemory take a from_fault flag (NEW vk_rasterizer.cpp ~1565-1567). page_manager.cpp:225 sets it on every write fault, and it routes to TextureCache::InvalidateMemory -> FlushBeforeCpuWrite (texture_cache.cpp:326 and 385-430). Trigger: a guest CPU thread writes into memory overlapping a GPU-modified render target or storage image that is not depth, not MSAA and not written back. The faulting thread then blocks in liverpool->SendCommand<true>(...) until the GPU thread has recorded TileImageToBuffer. The retried write faults again, and the buffer cache then downloads the range from the GPU, which is a GPU wait. OLD has nothing like this; it just invalidated the image. This can cause hitches when the game streams into memory that render or storage targets used before (the fork comment cites UFC 4 skin atlases). Frequency in fights is not verified. A/B: SHADPS4_FLUSH_CPU_WRITE=0. Origin: our fork. Magnitude: stutter, low to medium.
2) Two corrections to finding 1, which also apply to finding 5. Each queued image does its own Finish: the ProcessDownloadImages loop calls DownloadImageMemory(id, true) per image, and each call submits and waits. The drain also runs from liverpool WriteData of 8 bytes or less (liverpool.cpp:846) and Rewind (890), not only EOP/EOS/OnSubmit. Those are mid-frame points, so a single 1x1 or linear-storage image can stall the GPU before the frame ends.
3) DepthAsColor (finding 2) is worse than described. The bind transition right after the compute pass (vk_rasterizer.cpp:1232-1239) moves the alias General->ShaderReadOnlyOptimal. The next conversion moves it back to General. So each sampling draw costs at least two image barriers on the alias, plus the barrier on the depth image, plus the render pass restart.

summary:
I compared OLD a8d954e with NEW 12739d2 and checked what our fork changed using 88bd144..12739d2.

**Biggest difference: the shader and pipeline cache.** OLD had no shader cache on disk at all. It has no cache_storage.cpp, no vk_pipeline_serialization.cpp and no pipelineCache config option, and its Vulkan pipeline cache always started empty. So every run of OLD recompiled every shader while the game played. NEW has upstream's on-disk shader cache with WarmUp preloading, and our fork also saves the driver's VkPipelineCache to disk. On a new NEW install, ApplyRecommendedSettings switches the cache on (config.cpp:1958-1961; the code default is pipelineCacheEnable=false). From the second run on this should mean much less compile stutter than OLD (NEW faster). Two exceptions:
- **A player who kept an existing config.toml.** For example, one copied over from BBFork: the recommended settings are not applied, the code default (off) is used, and that player gets OLD-like compile stutter.
- **Our own save-every-50-pipelines code.** While new pipelines are being compiled (first run, new content), it writes the whole driver cache to disk synchronously on the rendering thread, which causes periodic hitches.

**Per-vendor changes that can lower FPS:**
- **Intel:**
  - Shaders must now run 32 lanes wide ("subgroup size 32", our fork). The driver can no longer pick narrower SIMD8/16 for register-heavy shaders, so slowdowns from register spills are possible.
  - Intel now also gets full workgroup barriers on shared-memory accesses (`needs_lds_barriers` extended to subgroup size < 64, our fork).
- **AMD with wave64 support (RDNA, upstream):** 64-wide waves are now required on every stage, where OLD let the driver choose.
- **All GPUs (our fork, default on):** subgroup control barriers in every compute shader that uses shared memory.
- **Intel and NVIDIA (our fork, on by default):** the NaN output guard and 1D compute workgroups. Both are cheap ALU additions.
- **NVIDIA only (upstream):** clip-distance emulation adds a discard at the start of fragment shaders, and a discard-only fragment shader to depth-only draws, whenever clip distances or user clip planes are enabled. This can turn off early-Z.

Most of these are correctness fixes for UFC 4.

**No FPS difference found:**
- Robustness: OLD already enabled robustBufferAccess2, robustImageAccess2 and nullDescriptor whenever supported; NEW requires them.
- Buffer type: OLD already forced every buffer to be a storage buffer, since IsStorage returned true.
- Primitive restart is now always dynamic state.
- glslang was removed.
- New extensions are enabled: maintenance5, image_view_min_lod, 2D view of 3D, shader_clock, sparse binding. Only enabling sparse binding needs checking against buffer_cache usage.
- Shader-patch lookup: our fork reads patches once per permutation instead of every draw. That only fixes a cost added by upstream after OLD, and OLD never had it.

**Small differences:**
- VK_EXT_legacy_vertex_attributes was removed, so vertex shaders always specialize on the attribute number class. This means a few more shader permutations on GPUs that had the extension.
- The texture garbage collector budget went from a fixed 2000 MB to 4 GB, and reported device usage is capped at 4 GB. This shifts the GC pressure and critical thresholds only slightly: pressure ~1.5 to 1.6 GB, critical 3 to 3.2 GB.

**A/B switches:**
- pipelineCacheEnable / pipelineCacheArchive in config.toml.
- SHADPS4_NAN_GUARD=0/1, SHADPS4_FLATTEN_WG=0/1, SHADPS4_LDS_ORDER=0/1/(default control barrier), SHADPS4_ALPHA_TO_MASK=0, SHADPS4_GPU. Any of these env vars also makes NEW use a separate shader cache directory.
- No switch exists for the required subgroup size (32/64), for Intel's `needs_lds_barriers`, or for NVIDIA's clip-distance emulation.

**Ask players for their log.** The log prints the "Subgroup size range X-Y, required size stages: ..." line, "NaN output guard: on/off", "Flatten compute workgroups: on/off", and "Vulkan pipeline cache: loaded N KB". These tell which paths are active for that player.

findings.title: OLD had no shader/pipeline cache on disk; NEW preloads cached shaders (WarmUp) and keeps VkPipelineCache on disk
findings.old_behavior: OLD a8d954e has no src/video_core/cache_storage.cpp, no vk_pipeline_serialization.cpp and no pipelineCacheEnable config entry. vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:270 (OLD) is createPipelineCacheUnique({}), an empty driver cache every run. Every shader and pipeline was translated, then compiled by the driver, while the game ran, on every launch. That gives hitches whenever a new effect, arena or cutscene appears, every session. The driver's own disk cache (NVIDIA/AMD/Intel) may soften this.
findings.new_behavior: PipelineCache ctor (vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:384-410) loads <serial>_vk_<vendor>_<device>.bin into the VkPipelineCache and calls WarmUp() (vk_pipeline_serialization.cpp:318-392). WarmUp recompiles every pipeline seen before, during loading, from the cached SPIR-V. New shaders are written to the cache folder on an IO worker thread (cache_storage.cpp WriteVector). New installs get pipelineCacheEnable=true and pipelineCacheArchive=false (config.cpp:1958-1961, our fork). From the second run, gameplay compile stutter should be far lower than OLD. Loading takes longer while WarmUp runs.
findings.conditions: All GPUs, second and later runs of a game, pipelineCacheEnable=true. The code default is still false (config.cpp:311). ApplyRecommendedSettings runs only when config.toml does not exist, or on Restore Defaults (config.cpp:1972-1977, 3007). A player who kept a config.toml from BBFork/older Shadlix runs with the cache OFF and gets OLD-like compile stutter. First runs after the ShaderBinaryVersion bump to 9 (vk_pipeline_serialization.cpp:15-16) also start empty.
findings.ab_toggle: config.toml [Vulkan] pipelineCacheEnable=true/false (GUI shader cache option); pipelineCacheArchive (zip vs folder)
findings.evidence: Serialization and WarmUp are upstream; 88bd144 already calls WarmUp(). Our fork e669792 adds VkPipelineCache persistence and atomic writes (git diff 88bd144 12739d2 -- vk_pipeline_cache.cpp: lines 384-450). b7285a7 turns the cache on in ApplyRecommendedSettings (config.cpp:1958-1961). OLD: `auto [cache_result, cache] = instance.GetDevice().createPipelineCacheUnique({});` (a8d954e vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:270).

verdict.title: OLD had no shader/pipeline cache on disk; NEW preloads cached shaders (WarmUp) and keeps VkPipelineCache on disk
verdict.notes: Confirmed. OLD a8d954e has no cache_storage.cpp or vk_pipeline_serialization.cpp, and vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:270 is createPipelineCacheUnique({}). NEW 12739d2 vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:384-410 loads <serial>_vk_<vendor>_<device>.bin, then WarmUp() runs (vk_pipeline_serialization.cpp:318-392). Defaults: config.cpp:311 pipelineCacheEnable(false), :312 pipelineCacheArchive(true). ApplyRecommendedSettings (config.cpp:1958-1961) sets enable=true and archive=false, and runs only when config.toml is missing (1972-1977) or on Restore Defaults (3007). I lowered the magnitude from high to medium. The gain is in stutter, not average FPS, and on Windows the NVIDIA, AMD and Intel drivers keep their own implicit disk caches, so on later runs OLD mostly paid only for its own GCN-to-SPIR-V translation. Upstream 88bd144 called WarmUp() before the VkPipelineCache existed. Our fork (e669792) moved it after the cache is created and added persistence of the cache. Second caveat, verified: if a stored profile does not match the current Shader::Profile, WarmUp closes the database (lines 337-351) and nothing is saved again. This one is listed under 'missed'.

findings.title: Synchronous VkPipelineCache dump to disk every 50 new pipelines, on the rendering thread
findings.old_behavior: OLD never serialized the driver pipeline cache.
findings.new_behavior: After every 50th newly compiled graphics or compute pipeline, GetGraphicsPipeline/GetComputePipeline call SaveVkPipelineCache() inline (vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:464-466, 494-496). It does getPipelineCacheData of the WHOLE driver cache (vulkan-hpp queries the size, then copies), writes a .tmp file and renames it (420-439). This all runs on the thread that records draws. The cache blob grows over the session; on NVIDIA it holds the compiled binaries and can reach tens of MB. Each dump is a frame hitch of several ms to 100+ ms, repeated every 50 new pipelines. It is also called at the end of the ctor and in the dtor (407-410, 442-446), which only affects load and exit.
findings.conditions: pipelineCacheEnable=true (default on new installs of NEW) and new pipelines being created: first run, new arenas/fighters/modes, or after a driver or GPU change. With a fully warm cache, few new pipelines appear, so the effect is small. Worst on a slow HDD and on NVIDIA (large cache blob).
findings.ab_toggle: pipelineCacheEnable=false disables it, but also the whole shader cache. There is no separate switch; moving the save to the IO worker or to shutdown only would be the fix.
findings.evidence: Commit e669792 'pipeline_cache: persist VkPipelineCache'. NEW vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:420-439 SaveVkPipelineCache(); 464 `if (++num_new_pipelines % 50 == 0) { SaveVkPipelineCache(); }`; 494 same for compute. 88bd144 had only `++num_new_pipelines;`.

verdict.title: Synchronous VkPipelineCache dump to disk every 50 new pipelines, on the rendering thread
verdict.notes: Confirmed in NEW vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:420-439 (SaveVkPipelineCache: getPipelineCacheData of the whole cache, write .tmp, rename) and at 464-466 and 494-496 (`if (++num_new_pipelines % 50 == 0) SaveVkPipelineCache();`) inside GetGraphicsPipeline/GetComputePipeline, so it runs inline on the thread that records draws. 88bd144 had only `++num_new_pipelines;`, so this comes from our fork (e669792). It also runs once at the end of the ctor at every launch (num_new_pipelines is always 0 after WarmUp, because WarmUp does not increment it) and in the dtor. Both of those affect only load and exit. It fires only while new pipelines are being compiled: first runs, new content, or after a driver or GPU change. Those frames already hitch from the compile itself, so the dump adds to an existing hitch rather than creating a new one. Its cost grows with the size of the blob, which is largest on NVIDIA. With a warm cache it is close to zero. No separate toggle; pipelineCacheEnable=false disables it.

findings.title: Intel: shaders must run 32 wide (requiredSubgroupSize=32), so the driver cannot pick SIMD8/16
findings.old_behavior: OLD did not enable subgroupSizeControl (no vk13 subgroupSizeControl in device features) and attached no PipelineShaderStageRequiredSubgroupSizeCreateInfo. The Intel driver chose SIMD8/16/32 per shader by register pressure.
findings.new_behavior: RequiredSubgroupSize() (vk_instance.h:252-263) returns 32 when maxSubgroupSize==32, minSubgroupSize<32, the default subgroupSize==32 and the stage is in requiredSubgroupSizeStages, which matches Intel Xe/Xe2. It is applied to every graphics stage (vk_graphics_pipeline.cpp:249-256) and to compute (vk_compute_pipeline.cpp:24-28). Register-heavy translated GCN shaders forced to SIMD32 may spill registers or lose occupancy, which can lower GPU throughput in heavy passes. This is a correctness fix: wave lockstep for LDS code, black squares in UFC 4.
findings.conditions: Intel Arc / Intel iGPU (Windows or ANV), only for stages listed in requiredSubgroupSizeStages. The NEW log prints 'Subgroup size range X-Y, required size stages: ...' (vk_instance.cpp, CreateDevice). Does not affect NVIDIA (min==max==32) or AMD (gets 64, see the AMD finding).
findings.ab_toggle: none (no env var or setting; would need a code switch to A/B)
findings.evidence: Commit 8034718. vk_instance.h:252-263 `if (vk13_features.subgroupSizeControl && vk13_props.maxSubgroupSize == 32 && vk13_props.minSubgroupSize < 32 && vk11_props.subgroupSize == 32 && (vk13_props.requiredSubgroupSizeStages & stage)) return 32;`. vk_instance.cpp:489 `.subgroupSizeControl = vk13_features.subgroupSizeControl` (absent in OLD).

verdict.title: Intel: shaders must run 32 wide (requiredSubgroupSize=32), so the driver cannot pick SIMD8/16
verdict.notes: Code confirmed: NEW vk_instance.h:252-262 RequiredSubgroupSize(); vk_graphics_pipeline.cpp:249-256; vk_compute_pipeline.cpp:24-30; vk_instance.cpp:489 enables subgroupSizeControl (absent in OLD). Comes from our fork (diff 88bd144..12739d2). It applies only to stages listed in requiredSubgroupSizeStages. On ANV that list is normally compute (plus task/mesh) only. Whether the Windows Intel driver includes graphics stages is not visible in the code; the NEW log line 'Subgroup size range ..., required size stages' shows it. Forcing SIMD32 on register-heavy compute shaders can cause spills on Intel. That is plausible but not measured, and it is a correctness fix: OLD on Intel ran wave-lockstep code at the wrong width. I lowered the magnitude to low-to-medium (low) because the effect is mostly on compute and is speculative. No toggle.

findings.title: Intel now gets workgroup-wide LDS barriers (needs_lds_barriers extended to subgroup size < 64)
findings.old_behavior: OLD: needs_lds_barriers = NVIDIA || MoltenVK (a8d954e vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:258). Intel compute shaders with 64-thread workgroups and shared memory had no inserted barriers.
findings.new_behavior: needs_lds_barriers = NVIDIA || MoltenVK || SubgroupSize() < 64 (vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:371-373). On Intel, SharedMemoryBarrierPass now puts a full OpControlBarrier(Workgroup) between dependent LDS writes and reads in every non-divergent block of 64-thread compute shaders. This stalls the workgroup and costs throughput in LDS-heavy compute (blur, reduction, skinning or culling passes). AMD stays at 64 and is unaffected; NVIDIA already had it in OLD.
findings.conditions: Intel GPUs (reported subgroupSize 32), compute shaders with shared memory and a 64-thread workgroup.
findings.ab_toggle: none for the workgroup barriers (SHADPS4_LDS_ORDER only controls the subgroup barriers)
findings.evidence: Commit 8034718. NEW vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:371-373 `instance.GetDriverID() == vk::DriverId::eMoltenvk || instance.SubgroupSize() < 64,`. src/shader_recompiler/ir/passes/shared_memory_barrier_pass.cpp:144 uses profile.needs_lds_barriers.

verdict.title: Intel now gets workgroup-wide LDS barriers (needs_lds_barriers extended to subgroup size < 64)
verdict.notes: Confirmed: NEW vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:371-373 adds `|| instance.SubgroupSize() < 64`. OLD a8d954e:258 was NVIDIA || MoltenVK only. The pass (shared_memory_barrier_pass.cpp) inserts workgroup Barrier() only for compute shaders with LDS whose workgroup size is exactly 64, and only in non-divergent blocks. On Intel SIMD32 such a workgroup is 2 hardware threads, so each barrier is cheap. Only those shaders are affected, so I rate it low rather than medium. Our fork, 8034718. No toggle for the workgroup barriers.

findings.title: Subgroup-scope control barriers inserted in every compute shader that uses shared memory, on all GPUs
findings.old_behavior: OLD inserted LDS barriers only on the NVIDIA/MoltenVK path for 64-thread workgroups. Other compute shaders had no extra barriers, so the compiler could freely schedule LDS loads and stores.
findings.new_behavior: Whenever the workgroup-barrier path is not taken (any GPU, workgroup != 64 or !needs_lds_barriers), and also in divergent blocks on that path, SharedMemoryBarrierPass inserts SubgroupBarrier between dependent LDS write and read (shared_memory_barrier_pass.cpp:137-191). By default (SHADPS4_LDS_ORDER unset) it is emitted as OpControlBarrier(Subgroup, Workgroup, AcqRel|WorkgroupMemory) (emit_spirv_barriers.cpp:37-57); upstream uses only a memory barrier. On AMD wave64 this is almost free. On NVIDIA it is a warp sync, and on Intel a subgroup sync. Both limit instruction scheduling in LDS-heavy compute.
findings.conditions: All GPUs; compute shaders with LDS. Cost is highest on Intel and NVIDIA.
findings.ab_toggle: SHADPS4_LDS_ORDER=0 (no subgroup barriers) / =1 (upstream memory-barrier only); the default is the control barrier. The env var also switches to a separate shader cache dir (cache_storage.cpp:112).
findings.evidence: Commits ca46b8b (upstream #5285 cherry-pick, which brings the subgroup barrier op) and 8034718 (ours: control-barrier default, barriers in divergent blocks). NEW shared_memory_barrier_pass.cpp:137-150 `static const bool lds_order_enabled = ... return !(env && env[0] == '0');`.

verdict.title: Subgroup-scope control barriers inserted in every compute shader that uses shared memory, on all GPUs
verdict.notes: Confirmed: NEW shared_memory_barrier_pass.cpp inserts SubgroupBarrier in every block of a compute shader with LDS when the workgroup is not 64 or needs_lds_barriers is false. This includes all LDS compute on AMD, where needs_lds_barriers is false. It also inserts them in divergent blocks on the workgroup-barrier path. EmitSubgroupBarrier (emit_spirv_barriers.cpp) defaults to OpControlBarrier(Subgroup, Workgroup, AcqRel|WorkgroupMemory). SHADPS4_LDS_ORDER=1 switches to upstream's OpMemoryBarrier(Subgroup), and =0 removes these barriers. The mechanism is upstream #5285, cherry-picked as ca46b8b; the control-barrier default and the divergent-block insertion are ours. OLD had none of this. Cost is mainly lost overlap of LDS latency. Low is reasonable. The env var uses its own cache directory (cache_storage.cpp:112-116).

findings.title: AMD with wave64 support: 64-wide waves now required on all shader stages
findings.old_behavior: OLD did not enable subgroupSizeControl and attached no required subgroup size. On RDNA the driver chose wave32 or wave64 per shader (wave32 is often chosen for compute and VS on Windows AMD).
findings.new_behavior: IsSubgroupSize64Supported() (subgroupSizeControl && maxSubgroupSize >= 64) makes RequiredSubgroupSize return 64 for every graphics and compute stage (vk_instance.h:245-254, vk_graphics_pipeline.cpp:249-256, vk_compute_pipeline.cpp:24-28). Note that the 64 path does not check requiredSubgroupSizeStages. Wave64 matches GCN semantics, which is good for correctness, but can be slower or faster than the driver's own choice depending on the shader.
findings.conditions: AMD RDNA dGPU or iGPU (e.g. Radeon 680M/780M). GCN or Vega already runs only wave64, so no change there.
findings.evidence: 88bd144 already has IsSubgroupSize64Supported and requiredSubgroupSize = 64; our fork only generalized it to RequiredSubgroupSize(). OLD vk_compute_pipeline.cpp: shader_ci had no pNext.

verdict.title: AMD with wave64 support: 64-wide waves now required on all shader stages
verdict.notes: Confirmed. OLD did not enable subgroupSizeControl and had no pNext on the stage create infos. 88bd144 already forced requiredSubgroupSize=64 when IsSubgroupSize64Supported (subgroupSizeControl && maxSubgroupSize>=64), so this is upstream; our fork only made it general. It affects RDNA dGPUs and iGPUs (680M/780M). Vega/GCN iGPUs are wave64 only. Whether it is faster or slower depends on the shader. No toggle.

findings.title: NVIDIA: clip-distance emulation adds discard to fragment shaders and a discard-only FS to depth-only draws
findings.old_behavior: OLD wrote native ClipDistance outputs. Depth-only draws (no pixel shader) had no fragment stage, and no injected discard.
findings.new_behavior: When the VS exports clip distances or user clip planes are enabled (no GS), NVIDIA gets hw.fs.clip_distance_emulation (vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:224-234, profile needs_clip_distance_emulation at :378). InjectClipDistanceAttributes puts up to 4 `if (attr < 0) discard` at the start of the fragment shader. Pipelines without a pixel shader get an extra EmitDiscardFragmentShader stage (vk_graphics_pipeline.cpp:236-247). Discard in the FS stops the driver from writing depth early (early-Z), and depth-only passes such as shadow maps or a depth prepass gain a fragment stage. This can noticeably lower GPU throughput in those passes.
findings.conditions: NVIDIA proprietary driver only (GTX 1660, RTX 4060 Ti), and only for draws whose game state enables clip distances or user clip planes. Whether UFC 3/4 use them is not verified.
findings.evidence: Present in 88bd144 (vk_graphics_pipeline.cpp:235, vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:216-220). NEW src/shader_recompiler/ir/passes/inject_clip_distance_attributes.cpp:33-37 `ir.Discard(cond_id)`.

verdict.title: NVIDIA: clip-distance emulation adds discard to fragment shaders and a discard-only FS to depth-only draws
verdict.notes: Code confirmed. OLD has native ClipDistance only and no clip_distance_emulation. 88bd144 already has it (profile.needs_clip_distance_emulation = NVIDIA proprietary, inject_clip_distance_attributes.cpp), so this is upstream. NEW vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:224-234 arms it when the VS exports clip distances (no LS stage) or when user clip planes are enabled (no GS). vk_graphics_pipeline.cpp:236-247 adds a discard-only FS to pipelines without a pixel shader. The cost (no early depth write, an extra FS in depth-only passes) only applies if UFC 3/4 actually enables clip distances or user clip planes, and the code does not show whether it does. I lowered it to low until a log or RenderDoc confirms it. No toggle.

findings.title: NaN output guard and 1D compute workgroups switched on by default for Intel and NVIDIA
findings.old_behavior: OLD: no NaN sanitizing; compute LocalSize declared as the guest's 3D size; LocalInvocationId read directly.
findings.new_behavior: NeedsGcnWorkarounds() is true for the Intel Windows, Intel Mesa, NVIDIA proprietary and NVK drivers (vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:288-294). sanitize_nan_outputs adds OpIsNan+OpSelect on every float MRT export component and every float storage-image write (emit_spirv_context_get_set.cpp:352-356, emit_spirv_image.cpp:370-373). flatten_compute_workgroups declares LocalSize (x*y*z,1,1) and rebuilds the local id with UMod/UDiv (emit_spirv.cpp:398-401, emit_spirv_context_get_set.cpp:259-272). Both cost only a few ALU ops. On Intel, flattening also changes how threads are packed into subgroups (rows instead of driver tiles), so texture-cache locality in 2D compute passes may change slightly.
findings.conditions: Intel and NVIDIA GPUs (AMD unaffected).
findings.ab_toggle: SHADPS4_NAN_GUARD=0/1 and SHADPS4_FLATTEN_WG=0/1 (each uses its own shader cache dir, cache_storage.cpp:112-115). The log prints 'NaN output guard: on/off' and 'Flatten compute workgroups: on/off'.
findings.evidence: Commits 8034718 (Intel) and 731a29e (extends to NVIDIA). NEW vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:288-320, :374-375.

verdict.title: NaN output guard and 1D compute workgroups switched on by default for Intel and NVIDIA
verdict.notes: Confirmed: NEW vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:288-316 (NeedsGcnWorkarounds: IntelProprietaryWindows, IntelMesa, NvidiaProprietary, NVK) and :374-375. emit_spirv_context_get_set.cpp:352-356 adds OpIsNan+OpSelect per float MRT component. emit_spirv_image.cpp:370 does the same for storage-image writes. emit_spirv.cpp:398-401 sets LocalSize to (x*y*z,1,1). emit_spirv_context_get_set.cpp:259-272 rebuilds the local id with UMod/UDiv by constants. Each costs a few ALU ops. On NVIDIA, flattening does not change how lanes are packed into warps, because x-major order is already linear. Our fork (8034718, 731a29e). A/B with SHADPS4_NAN_GUARD and SHADPS4_FLATTEN_WG, each with its own cache directory.

findings.title: VK_EXT_legacy_vertex_attributes removed: vertex shaders always specialize on attribute number class
findings.old_behavior: OLD enabled VK_EXT_legacy_vertex_attributes when available (NVIDIA recent drivers, Mesa). spec.num_class was then left empty (specialization.h:110 in OLD), so fewer vertex shader permutations were compiled.
findings.new_behavior: The extension is no longer enabled (vk_instance.cpp diff). spec.num_class = GetNumberClass(...) always (NEW specialization.h:110). This can create more VS permutations, meaning more compiles and a few more hitches on first sight. With the cache warm the effect is negligible.
findings.conditions: GPUs whose drivers expose VK_EXT_legacy_vertex_attributes; mainly first-run compile stutter.
findings.evidence: OLD a8d954e vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:237 `.support_legacy_vertex_attributes = instance_.IsLegacyVertexAttributesSupported()`. Removed in NEW, along with the LegacyVertexAttributesFeaturesEXT device chain entry.

verdict.title: VK_EXT_legacy_vertex_attributes removed: vertex shaders always specialize on attribute number class
verdict.notes: Confirmed: OLD vk_instance.cpp:295 enabled the extension, and OLD specialization.h left num_class empty when it was supported. NEW specialization.h:110 always uses GetNumberClass. This only adds VS permutations when the same shader is used with vertex buffers of different number classes, which is rare. It affects only first-sight compiles, and the shader cache hides it. It does not affect steady-state FPS. Upstream.

findings.title: Memory budget for texture GC raised from 2000 MB to 4 GB, and reported device usage capped at 4 GB
findings.old_behavior: GetTotalMemoryBudget() returned 2000_MB. The texture GC thresholds came out to trigger 0, pressure 1.5 GB, critical 3 GB. GetDeviceMemoryUsage returned the true heap usage.
findings.new_behavior: GetTotalMemoryBudget() returns 4_GB (vk_instance.h:474-476). GetDeviceMemoryUsage is clamped to 4 GB (vk_instance.cpp:825-826). Resulting thresholds: trigger 0, pressure ~1.6 GB, critical ~3.2 GB (texture_cache.cpp:51-68). Eviction is about as aggressive as before, slightly later. NEW also runs an async GC check every 60 frames (vk_rasterizer.cpp:655-663; texture-cache area).
findings.conditions: All GPUs with VK_EXT_memory_budget; matters only when VRAM use goes above ~1.6 GB.
findings.evidence: Not in the 88bd144..12739d2 diff of vk_instance.*, so upstream. OLD vk_instance.h:433-435 `return 2000_MB;`.

verdict.title: Memory budget for texture GC raised from 2000 MB to 4 GB, and reported device usage capped at 4 GB
verdict.notes: Confirmed: OLD vk_instance.h:433-435 returns 2000_MB; NEW vk_instance.h:474-476 returns 4_GB; NEW vk_instance.cpp:825-826 clamps usage to 4 GB. My calculation: OLD pressure=1536 MB, critical=3 GB; NEW pressure about 1638 MB, critical about 3277 MB; trigger is 0 in both. Practically the same. The 4 GB clamp does not matter because both thresholds are below it. The member total_memory_budget, which our fork changed for iGPUs (max(...,2_GB)), is never read, because GetTotalMemoryBudget returns a constant. Upstream. The every-60-submits async GC call in vk_rasterizer.cpp:655-663 exists, but it is outside this area.

findings.title: Fix (neutral vs OLD): shader-patch lookup once per permutation instead of on every draw
findings.old_behavior: OLD checked for patches only when compiling a new shader.
findings.new_behavior: Upstream (88bd144) re-read the patch file on every cached GetProgram call when patchShaders was on. Our fork limits this to once per permutation with Module::patch_checked (vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:845-855, vk_pipeline_cache.h Program::Module). NEW therefore matches OLD; listed only so nobody blames it.
findings.conditions: Config patchShaders on.
findings.evidence: Commit a29dc76; git diff 88bd144 12739d2 -- vk_pipeline_cache.cpp (`if (Config::patchShaders() && !it->patch_checked)`).

verdict.title: Fix (neutral vs OLD): shader-patch lookup once per permutation instead of on every draw
verdict.notes: Confirmed: NEW vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:845-855 is guarded by `Config::patchShaders() && !it->patch_checked`. patchShaders defaults to false in both OLD and NEW (config.cpp:284 NEW, :177 OLD). OLD called GetShaderPatch only in CompileModule. Neutral compared with OLD.

missed_by_analyst:
1) The shader cache can silently stay cold after an update (verified, upstream logic made worse by our fork's Profile change). NEW vk_pipeline_serialization.cpp:337-351: if the stored 'profile' blob has a different size or does not compare equal to the current Shader::Profile, WarmUp logs 'Pipeline cache isn't compatible with current system. Ignoring the cache', calls DataBase::Close() and returns, and does not rewrite the profile. Every later RegisterPipelineData/RegisterShaderMeta/RegisterShaderBinary then returns early on !IsOpened() (lines 24, 43, 64, 85). So that game's cache is never used and never written again until the player deletes the user/cache/<serial> folder. Our fork inserted sanitize_nan_outputs and flatten_compute_workgroups into the middle of Shader::Profile (profile.h diff 88bd144..12739d2). sizeof stays 64 bytes (40 bools + 6 u32), so the size check passes, but the bool fields that follow shift position. The compare will almost certainly fail on Intel and NVIDIA (sanitize/flatten are true there, and needs_lds_barriers changed for Intel), and probably on AMD too. A player who used a Shadlix or earlier fork build with the shader cache on, and who keeps the default folder (no SHADPS4_* env vars), gets shader-compile stutter on every launch in NEW, the same as OLD. The VkPipelineCache .bin file still persists, which softens the driver-side compile. Check: look for that warning in the log; fix: delete the cache folder.
2) Small CPU win for NEW (verified, upstream). For every graphics stage on every draw, OLD GetProgram returned std::optional<FetchShaderData> by value inside a tuple, and RefreshGraphicsStages copied it again. FetchShaderData holds a std::vector<VertexAttribute> (a8d954e fetch_shader.h:52-63), so that meant heap allocations and copies per draw. NEW stores a pointer to the cached data instead (vk_pipeline_cache.cpp GetProgram: `fetch_shader = &fetch;`). The gain is small, on the CPU-bound render thread, and favours NEW.
3) Our fork's cache_storage.cpp WriteVector now writes each shader-cache entry to a .tmp file and renames it. This runs on the PipelineCacheIO worker thread, not the render thread, so it has no FPS effect. I mention it only to rule it out.
Neither (1) nor (2) changes average FPS on a warm cache; (1) can explain 'more stutter than expected' rather than lower FPS.

summary:
I read the diffs for src/shader_recompiler: a8d954e..88bd144 (upstream/Shadlix) and 88bd144..12739d2 (our fork). Several changes make NEW shaders do more work. No single change in this area clearly explains a large FPS drop on every GPU, but four can reasonably cost FPS.
(1) Upstream: V_MAD_F32, V_MAC_F32 and V_MADMK_F32 used to emit one FMA. They now emit FMul+FAdd marked NoContraction, so the driver cannot fuse them. MAD/MAC are among the most common PS4 ALU ops. This affects all GPUs and has no switch.
(2) LDS ordering barriers, from our fork merged with upstream #5285. Every compute shader that uses shared memory now gets subgroup-scope OpControlBarriers around LDS read/write switches and at the end of each block. This applies on every vendor, AMD included. Intel now also gets full workgroup barriers, because needs_lds_barriers now includes SubgroupSize()<64. SHADPS4_LDS_ORDER can partly A/B this.
(3) Our fork (vk_instance, commit 8034718, outside src/shader_recompiler but it sets how these shaders run): Intel is forced to a required subgroup size of 32 for every stage the driver allows. Before, the driver chose SIMD8/16/32. There is no switch.
(4) Upstream: SignedZeroInfNanPreserve for fp32 is now set on every shader, which turns off the driver's fast-math folding.
Smaller costs: our NaN-aware min/max/med3 and the dropped AMD trinary min/max extension; LegacyMul selects on mul/mac/mad_legacy; RCP/RSQ/LOG clamps; the NaN output guard and 1D workgroups (Intel/NVIDIA by default, can be A/B tested); alpha-to-mask discard (ours); NVIDIA clip-distance discard emulation (upstream); wave64 ballot/readlane lowering through LDS plus two workgroup barriers (NVIDIA/Intel); user data now read from an SSBO instead of push constants; and more permutation keys, which mean more pipeline compiles and more stutter.
Changes that make NEW faster: OLD wrapped every LDS load, store and atomic in a bounds-check branch or select, and NEW removed them. With DMA enabled (off by default in both builds), immediate ReadConsts no longer go through the BDA page-table function.
Per vendor:
- Intel Arc gets the most new work: SIMD32 forced, workgroup and subgroup LDS barriers, NaN guard, 1D workgroups, wave64 lowering, plus every all-GPU change.
- NVIDIA gets the NaN guard, 1D workgroups, subgroup barriers in divergent LDS code and in all non-64 workgroups, wave64 lowering, and clip-distance discard.
- AMD gets subgroup barriers in all LDS compute shaders, loses the FMin3/FMax3/FMid3 AMD extension, and gets the all-GPU MAD split and InfNanPreserve.
I did not measure any of this. Magnitudes are estimates from instruction counts and how much each pattern is used.

findings.title: V_MAD_F32 / V_MAC_F32 / V_MADMK_F32 split from one FMA into FMul+FAdd (NoContraction, cannot be re-fused)
findings.old_behavior: OLD emitted ir.FPFma for V_MAC_F32, V_MADMK_F32 and V_MAD_F32 (and for V_MAC_LEGACY/V_MAD_LEGACY via those handlers): one OpFma per GCN mad/mac (OLD vector_alu.cpp:557-567, 1113-1118).
findings.new_behavior: NEW emits ir.FPAdd(ir.FPMul(a,b),c). EmitFPMul32 and EmitFPAdd32 both decorate the result NoContraction (emit_spirv_floating_point.cpp:9-12, 76-78), so the driver may not fuse them back into an FMA. Every GCN v_mad_f32/v_mac_f32/v_madmk_f32 now costs 2 ALU ops instead of 1. V_MADAK_F32 and V_FMA_F32 still use FMA. This is a correctness change: GCN mad is unfused.
findings.conditions: All GPUs (Intel, NVIDIA, AMD), all games, all shader stages. Matters most in ALU-bound pixel and compute passes. v_mac/v_mad are among the most frequent PS4 ALU instructions, so the extra instruction count can be large in those shaders. It could reach the high range in ALU-bound scenes, especially on the iGPU.
findings.evidence: NEW src/shader_recompiler/frontend/translate/vector_alu.cpp:737-742 (V_MAC_F32: FPAdd(FPMul(src0,src1),dst0)), 744-749 (V_MADMK_F32), 1390-1395 (V_MAD_F32). OLD a8d954e vector_alu.cpp:557-560 'ir.FPFma(...GetSrc(inst.dst[0]))', 562-567, 1113-1118 'ir.FPFma(src0, src1, src2)'. The change is in diff a8d954e..88bd144; 88bd144..12739d2 does not touch these lines.

findings.title: LDS ordering: subgroup control barriers in every LDS compute shader on all vendors, plus workgroup barriers newly on Intel
findings.old_behavior: OLD SharedMemoryBarrierPass returned early unless workgroup size == 64 AND needs_lds_barriers (NVIDIA proprietary or MoltenVK only). AMD and Intel got no LDS barriers at all. NVIDIA got workgroup barriers only at divergence depth 0.
findings.new_behavior: NEW, when workgroup size != 64 or !needs_lds_barriers (all AMD compute with LDS, NVIDIA/Intel non-64 workgroups), inserts a SubgroupBarrier in every block of the shader: before each LDS read after a write, before each write after a read, and at the end of every block that touched LDS (shared_memory_barrier_pass.cpp:138-152). Inside the workgroup-barrier path, divergent blocks also get subgroup barriers (184-191). Shared atomics now count as writes (19-26). EmitSubgroupBarrier defaults to OpControlBarrier(Subgroup, Workgroup, AcquireRelease|WorkgroupMemory) (emit_spirv_barriers.cpp:37-57). That is stronger than upstream's memory-only barrier and forces LDS waitcnt and execution sync. Separately, needs_lds_barriers now also includes SubgroupSize()<64 (vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:371-373). Intel therefore now gets full workgroup OpControlBarriers for 64-thread workgroups, plus merge-block barriers after divergent ifs and loops.
findings.conditions: Compute shaders that use LDS (shared_memory_size>0): blur, downsample, reductions, tiled lighting, SSAO. AMD: subgroup barriers (cost mostly LDS-latency waits). NVIDIA: subgroup barriers in divergent and non-64 workgroups (bar.warp.sync + membar). Intel Arc: heaviest, with workgroup barriers plus subgroup control barriers; Xe2 runs SIMD32 as two SIMD16 halves, so each subgroup barrier is real synchronization. Expect noticeable cost in LDS-heavy compute passes; it could be higher on Intel.
findings.ab_toggle: SHADPS4_LDS_ORDER=0 removes all subgroup barriers; =1 uses a memory-only barrier (upstream behaviour). Either setting gets its own shader cache dir (cache_storage.cpp). The Intel workgroup barriers from needs_lds_barriers (SubgroupSize<64) have no toggle.
findings.evidence: NEW src/shader_recompiler/ir/passes/shared_memory_barrier_pass.cpp:129-152, 184-191; src/shader_recompiler/backend/spirv/emit_spirv_barriers.cpp:37-57 (OpControlBarrier Subgroup by default); src/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:371-373 '|| instance.SubgroupSize() < 64'. OLD a8d954e shared_memory_barrier_pass.cpp:90-99 (early return 'shared_memory_size == 0 || threadgroup_size != GcnSubgroupSize || !profile.needs_lds_barriers'); OLD vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:258-259 (NVIDIA/MoltenVK only). Fork commits 8034718 and ca46b8b (upstream #5285 merged with ours; ours chose the control barrier as default).

findings.title: Intel: required subgroup size 32 forced for compute (and any other stage the driver allows)
findings.old_behavior: OLD set requiredSubgroupSize=64 only when wave64 was supported (AMD). On Intel no pNext was passed, so the driver picked SIMD8/16/32 per shader based on register pressure.
findings.new_behavior: Instance::RequiredSubgroupSize returns 32 when maxSubgroupSize==32, minSubgroupSize<32, subgroupSize==32 and the stage is in requiredSubgroupSizeStages (the Intel case). Compute and graphics pipelines pass it for every stage (vk_compute_pipeline.cpp:24-28, vk_graphics_pipeline.cpp:249-255). This forces SIMD32 even for register-heavy shaders where the driver would have chosen SIMD16/8. That can cause register spills or lower occupancy; on Xe2 SIMD32 runs as two SIMD16 passes.
findings.conditions: Intel Arc / Intel iGPU only, and only for stages listed in requiredSubgroupSizeStages (at least compute). Heavy shaders are hit hardest. Not in src/shader_recompiler, but the LDS-barrier and wave64 code above assumes this size.
findings.evidence: NEW src/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_instance.h:249-262 (RequiredSubgroupSize), vk_compute_pipeline.cpp:24-28, vk_graphics_pipeline.cpp:249-255. OLD: '.requiredSubgroupSize = 64' with pNext only if IsSubgroupSize64Supported() (shown in the 8034718 diff). Fork commit 8034718.

findings.title: SignedZeroInfNanPreserve (fp32) execution mode added to every shader
findings.old_behavior: OLD SetupFloatMode only set DenormFlushToZero/RoundingModeRTZ for fp32. The driver was free to apply fast-math folding (x*0->0, x+0->x, x-x->0, reassociation of special values).
findings.new_behavior: NEW SetupInfNanPreserveMode adds the SignedZeroInfNanPreserve capability and the fp32 execution mode on every shader when the device supports it (plus fp16/fp64 when used), along with DenormPreserve for fp16/64. Driver compilers must keep IEEE NaN/Inf/-0 semantics and drop some algebraic simplifications.
findings.conditions: All GPUs that report shaderSignedZeroInfNanPreserveFloat32 (NVIDIA, AMD and Intel all generally do). All shaders. Usually a few percent at most, but it applies everywhere.
findings.evidence: NEW src/shader_recompiler/backend/spirv/emit_spirv.cpp:592-634 (SetupInfNanPreserveMode), 601 'AddExecutionMode(main_func, SignedZeroInfNanPreserve, 32U)', 640 call in SetupFloatMode. OLD a8d954e emit_spirv.cpp SetupFloatMode had only DenormFlushToZero/RoundingModeRTZ.

findings.title: NaN-aware min/max/med3/saturate and removal of the AMD trinary min/max extension
findings.old_behavior: OLD: FPMin/FPMax were OpFMin/OpFMax (OpNMin/NMax only for the legacy variants). FPMinTri/MaxTri/MedTri used OpFMin3AMD/OpFMax3AMD/OpFMid3AMD when supports_trinary_minmax (AMD). FPSaturate was OpFClamp.
findings.new_behavior: NEW: every FPMin/FPMax is OpNMin/OpNMax (ours). min3/max3 are two NMin/NMax ops and the AMD extension is gone. med3 is 3x IsNan + 2x LogicalOr + 4x FMin/FMax + 2x NMin + Select (about 12 ops instead of 1 on AMD). Saturate is OpNClamp. V_MIN/MAX_LEGACY add IsNan x2 + Or + Select (upstream).
findings.conditions: All GPUs. Cost per instruction is small (NVIDIA and Intel min/max are already IEEE minNum-like), but on AMD v_min3/v_max3/v_med3 turn into multi-instruction sequences. Only matters for shaders heavy in min3/max3/med3 (tonemapping, TAA clamps).
findings.evidence: NEW src/shader_recompiler/backend/spirv/emit_spirv_floating_point.cpp:42-74 (OpNMax/OpNMin, EmitFPMedTri32 with IsNan/Select), 144-152 (OpNClamp). NEW vector_alu.cpp:637-659 (legacy min/max select, upstream). OLD a8d954e emit_spirv_floating_point.cpp EmitFPMax32 is_legacy?OpNMax:OpFMax, with the FMin3AMD/FMid3AMD path. Fork commits 02d3b06 and 5157080 (cherry-pick of upstream c495290 / #5257, which drops the AMD extension).

verdict.title: NaN-aware min/max/med3/saturate and removal of the AMD trinary min/max extension
verdict.notes: Confirmed. NEW emit_spirv_floating_point.cpp:42-74: OpNMin/OpNMax everywhere, min3/max3 as nested NMin/NMax, med3 as 3 IsNan + 2 Or + 4 FMin/FMax + 2 NMin + Select. Lines 144-152: Saturate is OpNClamp. 88bd144 still had OpFMin/FMax plus FMin3AMD/FMid3AMD (supports_trinary_minmax). In NEW the AMD trinary path is gone from the integer emitters too (no supports_trinary_minmax use left in 12739d2 src). Origin is our fork (02d3b06, 5157080). AMD compilers usually re-form min3/max3 from nested ops, but med3 with the NaN select will not collapse to v_med3. Small, and only in shaders heavy in min3/max3/med3.

findings.title: Legacy multiply semantics: V_MUL_LEGACY, V_MAC_LEGACY and V_MAD_LEGACY now emit compare/select sequences
findings.old_behavior: OLD mapped V_MUL_LEGACY_F32 to plain FMul, and V_MAC_LEGACY_F32/V_MAD_LEGACY_F32 to one FMA (vector_alu.cpp:25-28, 341-342).
findings.new_behavior: NEW LegacyMul is FPEqual(a,0) || FPEqual(b,0) ? 0 : a*b (about 5 ops), then FPAdd for mac/mad. So mul_legacy goes from 1 op to about 5, and mac/mad_legacy from 1 to about 6.
findings.conditions: All GPUs. PS4 shader compilers emit v_mul_legacy_f32 in pow() lowering (log2 * y -> exp2) and DX9-style code. The extra cost scales with how often these appear.
findings.evidence: NEW src/shader_recompiler/frontend/translate/vector_alu.cpp:609-627, 1994-1999 (LegacyMul). V_MUL_LEGACY change was already in 88bd144 (upstream). MAC/MAD_LEGACY come from fork commit 5157080 (cherry-pick of upstream #5257).

findings.title: RCP/RSQ/LOG clamp variants now clamp, and RSQ_LEGACY adds a zero test
findings.old_behavior: OLD mapped V_RCP_CLAMP_F32 to V_RCP_F32, V_RSQ_CLAMP/V_RSQ_LEGACY to V_RSQ_F32, and V_LOG_CLAMP to V_LOG_F32 (one transcendental op each).
findings.new_behavior: NEW adds an FClamp(±FLT_MAX) after each. V_RSQ_LEGACY also adds FPEqual(src,0) plus Select.
findings.conditions: All GPUs. These are uncommon opcodes, so expect 1-2 extra ALU ops where used.
findings.evidence: NEW src/shader_recompiler/frontend/translate/vector_alu.cpp:1050-1056, 1087-1117. Fork commit 5f7d8a1 (cherry-pick of upstream #5346).

findings.title: NaN output guard on render-target and storage-image float writes (Intel and NVIDIA by default)
findings.old_behavior: No sanitizing of outputs.
findings.new_behavior: When profile.sanitize_nan_outputs is set, each float MRT component store gets OpIsNan + OpSelect, and each float storage-image write gets a vec4 IsNan + Select before OpImageWrite.
findings.conditions: On by default for Intel (Windows and Mesa) and NVIDIA (proprietary and NVK); off on AMD. About 2 ALU ops per output component, so negligible except in very light full-screen passes.
findings.ab_toggle: SHADPS4_NAN_GUARD=0/1 (uses a separate shader cache dir)
findings.evidence: NEW src/shader_recompiler/backend/spirv/emit_spirv_context_get_set.cpp:352-356; emit_spirv_image.cpp:370-373; src/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:285-305 (NeedsGcnWorkarounds/SanitizeNanOutputs), 374. Fork commits 8034718 and 731a29e (enabled on NVIDIA).

verdict.title: NaN output guard on render-target and storage-image float writes (Intel and NVIDIA by default)
verdict.notes: Confirmed. NEW emit_spirv_context_get_set.cpp:352-356 adds IsNan+Select per float MRT component. vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:285-305 turns it on by default for Intel proprietary/Mesa and NVIDIA proprietary/NVK; SHADPS4_NAN_GUARD overrides. Two ALU ops per exported component, negligible except in trivially light full-screen passes. Our fork (8034718, 731a29e).

findings.title: Compute workgroups declared 1D, with the 3D LocalInvocationId rebuilt by UMod/UDiv (Intel and NVIDIA by default)
findings.old_behavior: LocalSize(x,y,z) as the guest specified, and LocalInvocationId read from the builtin.
findings.new_behavior: LocalSize(x*y*z,1,1). LocalInvocationId components are computed from LocalInvocationIndex with UMod/UDiv by constants (a few integer ops per use). This may also change how the driver tiles 2D groups, which can affect texture/L1 locality for image-heavy compute.
findings.conditions: Intel and NVIDIA by default (AMD off). Compute shaders with 2D/3D workgroups.
findings.evidence: NEW src/shader_recompiler/backend/spirv/emit_spirv.cpp:395-405; emit_spirv_context_get_set.cpp:259-276; spirv_emit_context.cpp:503-515; vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:307-318, 375. Fork commits 8034718 and 731a29e.

findings.title: Alpha-to-mask (DB_ALPHA_TO_MASK) emulated with a fragment discard on single-sample targets
findings.old_behavior: DB_ALPHA_TO_MASK was ignored, so no discard.
findings.new_behavior: When the register is enabled and num_samples<=1, the MRT0 export adds FragCoord→quad index math, a threshold select chain and ir.Discard(alpha<threshold). A discard in a depth-writing PS can force late-Z or turn off early-Z for those draws. This is also a new permutation key (alpha_to_mask in HwFragmentRuntimeInfo::operator==).
findings.conditions: All GPUs. Only draws with alpha-to-mask (UFC 4 hair cards and similar). Can add overdraw cost in hair-heavy close-ups.
findings.evidence: NEW src/shader_recompiler/frontend/translate/export.cpp:96-118; src/shader_recompiler/runtime_info.h:213-224; src/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:213-223. Fork commit 69ab199.

findings.title: NVIDIA: clip-distance and user-clip-plane emulation through fragment-shader discards
findings.old_behavior: OLD used hardware ClipDistance outputs and ignored user clip planes (PA_CL_UCP).
findings.new_behavior: On NVIDIA proprietary (needs_clip_distance_emulation), when the VS exports clip distances or UCP lowering is active, every fragment shader of that pipeline gets 4 extra input reads plus 4 conditional Discards at the start (InjectClipDistanceAttributes; upstream's own comment calls it an 'expensive discard in PS'). LowerUserClipPlanes also adds a ClipPlanes buffer binding to every hardware VS, even when no plane is enabled (returns after push_back).
findings.conditions: NVIDIA proprietary only, for draws that use clip distances or user clip planes. Can turn off early-Z for those draws. Unknown whether UFC 3/4 use them.
findings.evidence: NEW src/shader_recompiler/ir/passes/inject_clip_distance_attributes.cpp:11-38; lower_user_clip_planes.cpp:19-29 (buffer always added); recompiler.cpp TranslateProgram (InjectClipDistanceAttributes call, comment 'expensive discard in PS'); vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:224-234, 378.

verdict.title: NVIDIA: clip-distance and user-clip-plane emulation through fragment-shader discards
verdict.notes: The code exists in NEW and already in 88bd144 (inject_clip_distance_attributes.cpp and lower_user_clip_planes.cpp are in the 88bd144 tree), so it is upstream. OLD a8d954e has none of it. needs_clip_distance_emulation is NVIDIA proprietary only (vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:378). The fragment discard applies only when the VS enables clip distances or UCPs; it is unknown whether UFC does. LowerUserClipPlanes adds the ClipPlanes buffer to every hardware VS before checking the mask (lower_user_clip_planes.cpp:24-33). That is one extra binding per VS draw: minor CPU/descriptor cost and no GPU ALU.

findings.title: Wave64 emulation: ballot/readlane in >32-thread compute lowered through LDS with two workgroup barriers each
findings.old_behavior: No lowering. Ballots were 32-wide on 32-lane hosts, which was faster but gave wrong results for 64-lane GCN code.
findings.new_behavior: LowerWave64BallotPass, when profile.subgroup_size != 64 and the workgroup has more than 32 threads, replaces each Ballot (unpacked to 64-bit) and each ReadLane with an immediate lane by WriteShared + Barrier + LoadShared + Barrier, and adds LDS scratch. MaskedBitCount gets emulated arithmetic.
findings.conditions: NVIDIA and Intel (subgroup 32). Not AMD with wave64. Only compute shaders using ballots, readlane or mbcnt in uniform control flow (prefix sums, compaction, culling).
findings.evidence: NEW src/shader_recompiler/ir/passes/lower_wave64_pass.cpp:106-196; recompiler.cpp pass list (LowerWave64BallotPass after DeadCodeElimination).

findings.title: Guest user-data SGPRs read from the flatbuffer SSBO instead of push constants
findings.old_behavior: OLD EmitGetUserData loaded user data from the push-constant block (ud_regs0..3).
findings.new_behavior: NEW EmitGetUserData is EmitFlatbufferLoad(reg), a storage-buffer load. The push block lost its 4 ud_regs vec4s. On NVIDIA, push constants are read straight from the constant bank, while an SSBO load goes through L1.
findings.conditions: All GPUs, for shaders that use user-data SGPRs directly as values (not only as resource descriptors). Loads are uniform, so the cost is usually small.
findings.evidence: NEW src/shader_recompiler/backend/spirv/emit_spirv_context_get_set.cpp:50-54; spirv_emit_context.cpp DefinePushDataBlock (AuxData no longer has ud_regs). OLD a8d954e emit_spirv_context_get_set.cpp EmitGetUserData (PushConstant OpAccessChain on UdRegsIndex).

verdict.title: Guest user-data SGPRs read from the flatbuffer SSBO instead of push constants
verdict.notes: Confirmed. OLD a8d954e emit_spirv_context_get_set.cpp:48-57 used a PushConstant access chain; NEW 50-54 uses EmitFlatbufferLoad on a StorageBuffer (DefineBuffer always uses StorageClass::StorageBuffer). Same in 88bd144 (upstream). The loads are uniform and NonWritable, so drivers scalarize them. Impact is very small.

findings.title: V_CMP/V_CNDMASK now go through real 64-bit wave masks (Ballot/InverseBallot); V_READFIRSTLANE is now a real subgroup op in all stages
findings.old_behavior: OLD stored compare results as per-thread booleans (SetVcc/SetThreadBitScalarReg). V_CNDMASK read the bool directly. V_READFIRSTLANE was an identity outside compute/TCS.
findings.new_behavior: NEW writes SetDst64(Ballot(result)), and V_CNDMASK uses InverseBallot(mask). InverseBallotEliminationPass folds the common patterns back to booleans (Ballot→arg, And/Or/Xor/Not/Select/Phi). Masks it cannot trace, such as masks from memory, odd s_* combinations or immediates other than 0/~0, stay as real OpGroupNonUniformBallot/InverseBallot. V_READFIRSTLANE always emits OpGroupNonUniformBroadcastFirst. Exec as an operand (exec_lo/hi) emits a ballot.
findings.conditions: All GPUs. Usually folded away, so the residual cost depends on the shader. Subgroup ops in pixel shaders can also block some driver optimizations.
findings.evidence: NEW src/shader_recompiler/frontend/translate/vector_alu.cpp V_CNDMASK_B32 (InverseBallot) and V_CMP_* (SetDst64(..., ir.Ballot(...))); src/shader_recompiler/ir/passes/inverse_ballot_elimination_pass.cpp:59-171; data_share.cpp V_READFIRSTLANE_B32 (always ReadFirstLane).

findings.title: Written guest buffers with MTYPE 3, and shared memory lowered to SSBO, decorated Coherent
findings.old_behavior: No Coherent decoration on any SSBO.
findings.new_behavior: DefineBuffer decorates written buffers Coherent when buf_sharp.mtype==3 (guest uncached) or buffer_type==SharedMemory. Coherent loads and stores skip L1 / non-coherent caches on all vendors.
findings.conditions: All GPUs. Only buffers the guest marks MTYPE 3 (UC), and compute shaders whose LDS is lowered to a storage buffer (LDS larger than the host limit, or no workgroup explicit layout support with mixed types).
findings.evidence: NEW src/shader_recompiler/backend/spirv/spirv_emit_context.cpp:820-827 (Decorate Coherent), 855-861 (is_coherent = SharedMemory || mtype == 3).

findings.title: More shader permutation keys, so more pipeline compiles (first-time stutter)
findings.old_behavior: OLD did not specialize the VS attribute num_class when support_legacy_vertex_attributes was available. Fewer RuntimeInfo fields were compared.
findings.new_behavior: NEW always specializes on GetNumberClass for VS attributes. Also compared: ImageSpecialization.num_bindings, RuntimeInfo.props.dx10_clamp (ours, from #5257), hw.fs.alpha_to_mask (ours), blend_self_scale, user_clip_plane_mask and front_face_all_bits. Any of these varying per draw creates a new SPIR-V module and pipeline. The ShaderBinaryVersion bumps also invalidate old caches once.
findings.conditions: All GPUs. Shows up as compile hitches, mostly early or in new scenes. Pipeline-cache settings reduce it.
findings.evidence: NEW src/shader_recompiler/specialization.h (num_class no longer gated by support_legacy_vertex_attributes; num_bindings added); runtime_info.h:213-224 (alpha_to_mask in operator==), 246-260 (dx10_clamp bit).

findings.title: Removed bounds checks around every LDS load, store and atomic (and buffer accesses on non-robust devices)
findings.old_behavior: OLD wrapped every LoadShared/WriteShared in AccessBoundsCheck with a constant size: an OpULessThan plus OpSelectionMerge/BranchConditional plus OpPhi per access. Shared atomics had the same wrapper, so every compute shader with LDS had a branch per LDS op. Buffer loads and stores were also bounds-checked when !supports_robust_buffer_access (normally not on desktop).
findings.new_behavior: NEW issues the LDS loads, stores and atomics directly. emit_spirv_bounds.h is gone, and buffer accesses no longer have shader-side bounds checks.
findings.conditions: All GPUs, every compute shader that uses LDS. This partly offsets the new LDS barriers.
findings.evidence: NEW src/shader_recompiler/backend/spirv/emit_spirv_shared_memory.cpp:9-49 (plain OpLoad/OpStore); emit_spirv_atomic.cpp:19-60 (no bounds wrapper). OLD a8d954e emit_spirv_shared_memory.cpp (AccessBoundsCheck<16/32/64> with ConstU32(num_elements)), emit_spirv_atomic.cpp:21-63, emit_spirv_bounds.h:42-87.

findings.title: With DMA enabled, immediate-offset ReadConst reads the flatbuffer directly instead of going through the BDA page-table function
findings.old_behavior: OLD: any ReadConst set uses_dma and bound the BDA page table and fault buffer. Immediate-offset ReadConsts called read_const (BDA page lookup, branch, fault marking, fallback to flatbuf).
findings.new_behavior: NEW: only dynamic ReadConst (flatbuf offset 0) enables DMA. Immediate ReadConst becomes EmitFlatbufferLoad, and the SRT walker flattens more pointer patterns (flatten_extended_userdata_pass rewrite).
findings.conditions: Only when directMemoryAccess is on. It defaults to false in both OLD and NEW, and ApplyRecommendedSettings does not turn it on. All GPUs.
findings.evidence: NEW src/shader_recompiler/backend/spirv/emit_spirv_context_get_set.cpp:56-66; src/shader_recompiler/ir/passes/shader_info_collection_pass.cpp:155-161, 181-184. OLD a8d954e shader_info_collection_pass.cpp:129-145 (uses_dma=true for every ReadConst), emit_spirv_context_get_set.cpp EmitReadConst (OpFunctionCall read_const for immediate offsets).

missed_by_analyst: AMD wave64 forced on all stages (upstream, between a8d954e and 88bd144). OLD a8d954e passed no VkPipelineShaderStageRequiredSubgroupSizeCreateInfo at all; git grep finds no requiredSubgroupSize anywhere in OLD src. NEW passes requiredSubgroupSize=64 to every compute stage and every graphics stage (VS/PS/GS/etc.) whenever IsSubgroupSize64Supported() (subgroupSizeControl && maxSubgroupSize>=64), via Instance::RequiredSubgroupSize. See NEW vk_instance.h:249-262, vk_compute_pipeline.cpp:24-28 and vk_graphics_pipeline.cpp:249-255; 88bd144 already did this for compute:25-28 and graphics:249-252. On AMD RDNA (Radeon iGPUs 680M/780M and dGPUs), the old build let the driver choose wave32 or wave64 per shader. AMD normally picks wave32 for VS/CS and wave64 for PS. Forcing wave64 on vertex and compute shaders can lower occupancy or efficiency in divergent and register-heavy shaders, but it can also help through RDNA3 dual-issue, so the direction is unclear. I estimate low to medium, AMD RDNA only, with no toggle. The analyst's Intel finding also misstates OLD: it says OLD forced 64 on AMD, but that is the 88bd144 behaviour. A smaller point: in NEW EmitBarrierInBlock (shared_memory_barrier_pass.cpp:60-63), any block with even one LDS access gets a trailing barrier. On AMD (subgroupSize 64, so needs_lds_barriers is false) every LDS compute shader therefore takes the subgroup-control-barrier path, even 64-thread groups. In OLD, AMD never got any LDS barrier.

summary:
I read the full diffs of liverpool.cpp/h, pm4_cmds.h, videoout (driver/video_out), gnmdriver, vk_presenter, perf_stats, the host_shaders folder (plus the FSR/PP host passes, swapchain and common/thread that they use). Present-path defaults are the same in OLD and NEW: present mode Mailbox, vblankFrequency 60, FPS limiter off, FSR on, RCAS on at 250, HDR off, collectDebugLogs off. The swapchain and FSR/PP passes are unchanged apart from the shaders being compiled ahead of time. The present path itself (vk_presenter) shows no regression. The new screenshot code only runs when a screenshot is requested, and the PerfStats/GameFPS hooks cost only a cached-bool check when Collect Debug Logs is off.

The main candidates for "NEW is slower" in this area are in the GPU command processor (liverpool):
(1) Synchronous image downloads that call scheduler.Finish() (a full GPU stall) at every fence: EOP, EOS, ReleaseMem and small WRITE_DATA. The mechanism came from upstream. Our fork (e565b66) made it fire by default for every linear image of 64x64 or larger that a compute shader writes. OLD did these downloads asynchronously, once per submit, and only when Readback Linear Images was on.
(2) Upstream now emulates occlusion queries and predication: a Vulkan occlusion query around every draw while the game has ZPASS counting on, plus deferred counter writeback. OLD wrote a fake "visible" counter at once and had no queries.
(3) The GPU timestamps games read (EOP/ReleaseMem PerfCounter) are now scaled to the 800/911 MHz GPU clock. OLD wrote raw host RDTSC, so measured GPU durations looked about 3 to 5 times longer. This matters only for games that scale their resolution from GPU timing.
(4) Our fork's depth-as-color compute pass, which runs on every bind of a depth texture read as R16/R32_UINT (the UFC shadow maps).

The changes that make NEW faster: draw/dispatch debug-marker strings are no longer built per draw when markers are off; PFP_SYNC_ME no longer ends rendering and inserts a barrier; host shaders are precompiled SPIR-V, so no runtime glslang compile of the tiling shaders; the swapchain submit lock is held for less time; the flip queue is deeper.

The FPS limiter semantics changed in our fork (15b0af1). With the limiter on, UFC 3/4 now get the configured FPS, where OLD gave half of it. With the limiter off (the default for both), UFC runs at 30 FPS in both builds. A player who carried over an OLD config with the limiter on will see NEW try to run at twice the frame rate OLD gave them, which can look like more stutter if the GPU cannot hold it.

findings.title: Synchronous image downloads with full GPU wait at every fence; fork made linear compute-written images download by default
findings.old_behavior: OLD liverpool.cpp only did CommitPendingGpuRanges at fences found by FenceDetector. Image downloads ran once per submit (Rasterizer::OnSubmit -> texture_cache.ProcessDownloadImages, OLD vk_rasterizer.cpp:373-381) and were asynchronous: OLD texture_cache.cpp:96-145 recorded the copy and handed the data to DownloadedImagesThread by tick, with no CPU wait. Images were only queued when Config::getReadbackLinearImages() was on (OLD texture_cache.cpp:583-598, default false).
findings.new_behavior: Every EVENT_WRITE_EOP, EVENT_WRITE_EOS and ReleaseMem, and every WRITE_DATA of 8 bytes or less, calls CommitPendingGpuRanges + ProcessDownloadImages + OnFence. OnFence calls ProcessDownloadImages again (NEW liverpool.cpp ~768-797 and 840-853 for gfx, ~1252-1300 for compute; vk_rasterizer.cpp:671-673 and 1615). TextureCache::ProcessDownloadImages calls DownloadImageMemory(id, sync=true), which does scheduler.Finish(), a full CPU wait for the GPU (NEW texture_cache.cpp:102-140). Our fork (e565b66) also queues every non-tiled 2D storage image of 64x64 or larger that is not depth or block-compressed, whenever a compute shader binds it as storage. This is on by default and has no config gate (NEW texture_cache.cpp:83-97 ReadbackLinearStorage, 966-975). Volume linear storage images are always queued (upstream).
findings.conditions: Any game whose compute shaders write linear storage images of 64x64 or larger. UFC 4 does it for fighter pictures (the reason for e565b66); per-frame use would mean one or more full GPU stalls per frame. Render targets also queue with Readback Linear Images on (default off). Affects all GPU vendors. Larger relative cost on weak iGPUs and Intel Arc, where every Finish drains the queue.
findings.ab_toggle: SHADPS4_LINEAR_STORAGE_READBACK=0 (disables the fork's linear-storage readback); 'Readback Linear Images' setting off (default) for render targets
findings.evidence: Mechanism (sync download + per-fence calls) is upstream: 88bd144 already has DownloadImageMemory(image_id, true) in ProcessDownloadImages. The always-on trigger is our fork commit e565b66 (git diff 88bd144 12739d2 -- src/video_core/texture_cache/texture_cache.cpp adds ReadbackLinearStorage + download_images.emplace in FindTexture). liverpool.cpp NEW: `if (rasterizer) { rasterizer->CommitPendingGpuRanges(); rasterizer->ProcessDownloadImages(); rasterizer->OnFence(); }` in the EventWriteEos, EventWriteEop and ReleaseMem handlers; WriteData: `if (data_size <= sizeof(u64) && rasterizer) {... ProcessDownloadImages(); }` and `rasterizer->OnFence()`. OLD: `} else if (fence_detector.IsFence(header) && rasterizer) { rasterizer->CommitPendingGpuRanges(); }`. Overlaps the texture-cache area; listed here because the per-fence trigger lives in liverpool.

verdict.title: Synchronous image downloads with full GPU wait at every fence; fork made linear compute-written images download by default
verdict.notes: Confirmed. NEW liverpool.cpp:768-771 (EOS), 789-792 (EOP), 844-850 (WriteData with 8 bytes or less, now any such WriteData, not only detected fences), 889-890 (Rewind), and 1256-1261/1292-1294 (compute) call CommitPendingGpuRanges + ProcessDownloadImages + OnFence. OLD only called CommitPendingGpuRanges at fences found by FenceDetector (old liverpool.cpp:633/646/697/1055/1087). NEW texture_cache.cpp:102-108 loops DownloadImageMemory(id, true), which runs scheduler.Finish() once per queued image (lines 133-137). The second call in OnFence (vk_rasterizer.cpp:671-673) is a no-op because the set is already cleared. OLD texture_cache.cpp:89-145 was asynchronous: TileImage plus a DownloadedImagesThread keyed by tick, and images were queued only with getReadbackLinearImages (OLD lines 585/597). Upstream 88bd144 queued only linear volume storage images. Fork e565b66 adds linear 2D storage images of 64x64 or larger with no config gate (NEW texture_cache.cpp:83-97 and 966-975); SHADPS4_LINEAR_STORAGE_READBACK=0 disables it. The image is re-queued every time it is bound as storage, and GpuModified is set again in FindTexture. Any game that writes such an image every frame therefore gets at least one full CPU-GPU drain per frame, on every vendor. The cost appears only if UFC writes linear 2D storage images of 64x64 or larger every frame. The commit only shows the fighter-picture or save path (an occasional hitch); the 64x64 threshold was chosen to skip per-frame helpers, and no per-frame user is proven. Medium, not high, unless a per-frame case is found. The analyst framed the new NEW CommitPendingGpuRanges calls as costly; they are cheap. In NEW they only flush the buffer-cache upload batch (buffer_cache.h:102 -> FlushSyncBatch, non-blocking), whereas OLD's version did preemptive downloads.

findings.title: FPS limiter now limits the presented frame rate (vblank rate = limit x (flip_rate+1)); OLD limited the vblank rate
findings.old_behavior: OLD driver.cpp PresentThread: with the limiter on, the vblank period was 1e9/fpsLimit. UFC 3/4 flip every 2nd vblank (flip_rate=1), so limit 60 gave 30 FPS and you needed limit 120 for 60 FPS. With the limiter off, the vblank period was 1e9/vblankFrequency (60), giving 30 FPS in UFC.
findings.new_behavior: NEW driver.cpp:392-422: with the limiter on, the AccurateTimer interval is set to 1e9/(fpsLimit*(flip_rate+1)) each time the game's flip_rate changes. Limit 60 therefore gives 60 FPS in UFC (vblank 120 Hz), and limit 120 gives a 240 Hz vblank aiming at 120 FPS. With the limiter off, behaviour matches OLD (vblankFrequency 60, so UFC at 30 FPS). On a new install, ApplyRecommendedSettings (config.cpp ~1958-1969) leaves the limiter off and presets fpsLimit to the monitor refresh rate (capped at 240).
findings.conditions: Only when the FPS limiter is enabled, in games with flip_rate>0 (UFC 3/4). A carried-over OLD config with the limiter on, e.g. 120 to get 60 FPS in UFC, makes NEW target 120 FPS. A GPU that cannot hold it gives an uncapped-looking, uneven frame rate that players may read as worse. Default installs (limiter off) behave the same in both builds: 30 FPS in UFC.
findings.ab_toggle: FPS limiter on/off and value (GPU settings: fpsLimiterEnabled / fpsLimit); vblankFrequency
findings.evidence: Fork commit 15b0af1 (git diff 88bd144 12739d2 -- src/core/libraries/videoout/driver.cpp): `const int64_t period_ns = std::max<int64_t>(kNanosPerSec / (fps_limit * (flip_rate + 1)), 1); timer.SetTargetInterval(...)` at NEW driver.cpp:414-422. Defaults are the same in both builds: fpsLimiterEnabled(false), vblankFrequency(60), fpsLimit(60), presentMode Mailbox (OLD config.cpp:142,178,181,256; NEW config.cpp:224,286,289,385). Fork commits b7285a7/f0038b9 add the refresh-rate preset.

verdict.title: FPS limiter now limits the presented frame rate (vblank rate = limit x (flip_rate+1)); OLD limited the vblank rate
verdict.notes: Confirmed in NEW driver.cpp:392-422 (fork 15b0af1). OLD PresentThread used FpsCap = 1e9/fpsLimit as the vblank period, with no flip_rate scaling. With the same config (limiter on, limit 60) NEW therefore presents twice as many frames in a flip_rate=1 game; the 2x applies only if UFC really uses flip_rate=1, which the fork comment asserts and the code does not show. Defaults are the same (limiter off, vblank 60, Mailbox), so a default install shows no difference. ApplyRecommendedSettings (config.cpp:1957-1969) keeps the limiter off and only presets fpsLimit to the monitor refresh rate, capped at 240. The analyst missed two side effects. First, with the limiter on, the guest-visible vblank rate (vblank events, vblank_status.count) runs at limit*(flip_rate+1), e.g. 120 Hz for limit 60. Second, SetCurrentThreadRealtime still uses the unscaled FpsCap. Neither lowers FPS. A carried-over OLD limit of 120 becomes a 120 FPS target in NEW. A/B: fpsLimiterEnabled/fpsLimit.

findings.title: Occlusion-query (ZPASS) and predication emulation: per-draw Vulkan occlusion queries and deferred counter results
