findings.old_behavior: OLD liverpool.cpp: SET_PREDICATION was ignored (LOG_DEBUG), so all draws executed. On a ZPASS_DONE/PixelPipeStatDump event, OLD wrote fake counters immediately (`*results = pixel_counter | ValidMask; pixel_counter += 0x2FFFFFF`). The game always saw valid, 'visible' results at once, with no GPU queries.
findings.new_behavior: NEW liverpool.cpp:454-486 and ~729-765: PixelPipeStatControl toggles counting. While counting is on, each draw gets a query slot plus beginQuery/endQuery (vk_rasterizer.cpp:435-455 and 516-545; vk_predication.cpp:319-349). ZPASS dumps are written to guest memory only after the GPU tick completes (DumpZpassCounters, vk_predication.cpp:210-237, via scheduler.DeferOperation). Predicated draws are skipped on the CPU or wrapped in VK_EXT_conditional_rendering. A small compute reduction (host_shaders/occlusion_predicate.comp) builds the predicate. PRED_EXEC and COND_EXEC are now evaluated.
findings.conditions: Only games that use occlusion queries or predication; unknown whether UFC 3/4 do. Cost: per-draw query begin/end, plus EndRendering + resetQueryPool per draw on GPUs without host query reset (unlikely on Vulkan 1.2+). Results that arrive later than OLD's instant fake values can add latency or stalls if a game spins on the valid bit. On the other hand, correct predication can skip occluded draws, which would be faster.
findings.evidence: vk_predication.cpp/h are new in 88bd144 (git cat-file shows it in 88bd144, not in a8d954e). liverpool.cpp is not changed by our fork (no diff 88bd144..12739d2). NEW liverpool.cpp case SetPredication -> predication->EnableFromZpass/EnableFromBool; EventWrite PixelPipeStatDump -> predication->DumpZpassCounters(address, num_counter_pairs). OLD: `*results = pixel_counter | OcclusionCounterValidMask; ... pixel_counter += OcclusionCounterStep;`

verdict.title: Occlusion-query (ZPASS) and predication emulation: per-draw Vulkan occlusion queries and deferred counter results
verdict.notes: The code difference is confirmed and comes from upstream (vk_predication.cpp exists in 88bd144; liverpool.cpp has no fork diff). OLD ignored SET_PREDICATION and wrote fake, instantly valid ZPASS counters (old liverpool.cpp:411-412 and 611-619). NEW liverpool.cpp:456-486 and 732-748 handles predication. The per-draw query cost exists only while PixelPipeStatControl has turned counting on (PrepareDrawQuery returns nullopt otherwise, vk_predication.cpp:319-322). Without host query reset, every counted draw does EndRendering + resetQueryPool (lines 341-347). EnableFromBool always does EndRendering plus a copy and a compute reduce. DumpZpassCounters writes guest results only after the GPU tick completes (DeferOperation, lines 225-236), so a CPU spinning on the valid bit would wait for the GPU. Nothing in the code shows that UFC 3/4 use ZPASS or SET_PREDICATION, so its FPS relevance for these games is unproven. Magnitude is low until shown otherwise. No A/B toggle.

findings.title: GPU timestamp (EOP/ReleaseMem PerfCounter) now in GPU-clock ticks instead of raw host TSC
findings.old_behavior: OLD pm4_cmds.h, PM4CmdEventWriteEop::SignalFence and PM4CmdReleaseMem::SignalFence with DataSelect::PerfCounter: wrote Common::FencedRDTSC(), the raw host TSC (about 3-5 GHz). sceGnmGetGpuCoreClockFrequency returned 800/911 MHz in both builds. A game converting GPU-timestamp deltas with the GPU clock therefore saw GPU durations about 3-5 times longer than real.
findings.new_behavior: NEW pm4_cmds.h:347-355 GetGpuPerfCounter(): sceKernelReadTsc() scaled by gpu_freq/tsc_freq, used at pm4_cmds.h:487 and in ReleaseMem. Games now get consistent GPU-clock timestamps.
findings.conditions: Only games that read GPU timestamps for dynamic resolution or quality scaling. In OLD such a game would believe the GPU was overloaded and lower the internal resolution, giving more FPS but a blurrier image. NEW gives the real value, which could mean higher resolution and lower FPS. Not verified for UFC; the fork's fixed render-resolution patch for UFC (memory_patcher) suggests UFC does not use dynamic resolution.

findings.title: Depth-as-color compute conversion on every bind of a depth texture read through R16/R32_UINT

Each time a shader samples a D16/D32 image with a non-depth format, the code calls texture_cache.UpdateImage, issues barriers, and dispatches host_shaders/depth_to_color.comp ((w/8)x(h/8)xlayers groups per mip) into an R16/R32_UINT alias that is then bound. This can break the current rendering pass through the Transit/FlushBarriers calls.
findings.conditions: UFC 3/4 spotlight shadow maps: 6-layer D16 array read by compute shaders every frame. Cost scales with the number of binds per frame and the shadow-map size. The commit says frame rate was unchanged on UFC 3, but the extra dispatches and barriers matter most on iGPUs. All vendors.

ConvertDepthToColor(depth, alias); ... }`.

verdict.title: Depth-as-color compute conversion on every bind of a depth texture read through R16/R32_UINT
verdict.notes: Confirmed (fork 7225129). In NEW vk_rasterizer.cpp:1197-1210, BindTextures calls ConvertDepthToColor on every non-storage bind of a 16- or 32-bit single-sample depth image whose view format is not depth- or stencil-compatible. ConvertDepthToColor (lines 83-215) always calls scheduler.EndRendering(), which breaks any active render pass, transitions the depth image to DepthStencilReadOnly and the alias to General, then dispatches (w/8)x(h/8)xlayers groups for every mip. The data is not cached: the conversion repeats on every bind even when the depth image is unchanged. It runs on all vendors, including NVIDIA, where the old path had worked. The commit reports unchanged frame rate on UFC 3 (Arc). The cost scales with binds per frame, so it is low and possibly more on iGPUs. A/B: SHADPS4_DEPTH_AS_COLOR=0.

missed_by_analyst:
I verified two small changes the analyst did not report; neither is a big FPS factor.
(1) The FenceDetector pre-pass is gone, which makes NEW slightly faster (low; upstream). OLD liverpool.cpp:234 and :841 built a FenceDetector (a8d954e:src/video_core/amdgpu/fence_detector.h). For every DCB and ACB it scanned the whole command buffer once more and kept an unordered_map of fence addresses before processing. NEW removes that scan and instead calls CommitPendingGpuRanges (now a cheap, non-blocking FlushSyncBatch upload flush) and ProcessDownloadImages at every EOP/EOS/ReleaseMem and every WriteData of 8 bytes or less. The extra sync points cost something only when download_images is non-empty, which is the trigger in finding 1.
(2) gnmdriver.cpp adds a new m_submit_lock (NEW gnmdriver.cpp:299, 348, 391, 2359; upstream). sceGnmDingDong, the Submit*CommandBuffers calls and sceGnmSubmitDone now take it before WaitGpuIdle, so submissions from different game threads are serialized, and a thread waiting in WaitGpuIdle holds the lock. This could cause slight contention in games that submit compute (DingDong) from another thread; it is low impact and has no toggle.
Nothing else in this area changes default behaviour. The app0 storage scheduler hook in Flip (driver.cpp:281-288) is off by default (app0_read_bandwidth_mibps=0, config.cpp:232), and the Render Resolution patch defaults to empty, which keeps the game's own resolution.

summary:
I compared memory.cpp/h, address_space.cpp/h, signals.cpp, libraries/kernel (threads, mutex, condvar, sleepq, rwlock, semaphore, event_flag, equeue, time, file_system, process, kernel), file_sys (fs.cpp, host_fs, storage_scheduler), ajm, audio, common/thread.cpp and common/logging between OLD a8d954e and NEW 12739d2. I also checked 88bd144..12739d2 to find what our fork changed.

Almost every CPU-side difference in this area came from upstream shadPS4/Shadlix. Our fork's changes here cost nothing at runtime: the AJM and audio PerfStats counters (only active with Collect Debug Logs), the Skip Intro string check in open(), the input-script hook, the Windows unhandled-exception logger, and restoring page protections on an address-space split.

Nothing in this area alone accounts for a large generic FPS loss. These are the differences most likely to make NEW slower:
1. sem_post and scePthreadSemPost now wake every waiting thread, not just one.
2. On Windows every log line written now also goes through OutputDebugStringW, and every new log entry looks up the thread name.
3. HR timer events of 1.2 ms or longer no longer finish with a short precision spin, and periodic timer events are rounded down to whole milliseconds.
4. TryWriteBacking (the GPU write-back and readback path) now takes a lock and copies whole VMA objects on every call.
5. The memory manager and guest rwlocks now use a reader-first mutex built on a condition variable.
6. Opening and stat-ing files makes more filesystem calls, and every read goes through an extra memcpy.

These differences make NEW faster:
- Log messages below the filter level (TRACE/DEBUG, for example 178 calls in gnmdriver) are no longer formatted. OLD formatted every one.
- Grouping of identical log lines is on by default, so repeated lines are not written.
- Event flags wake only the waiters whose condition is met, without the old 10 µs sleep loops.
- The old 1.2 ms yield-spin per HR timer is gone.
- On Windows, the UTC-to-local-time conversion no longer goes through tzdb.
- sceKernelIsNeoMode result is cached.

These settings exist but do nothing, so they cannot explain a difference:
- CPU Core Mode (config only; nothing calls getEffectiveCpuCores or SetThreadAffinity).
- app0 read bandwidth throttle: default 0, and the scheduler is never called from the read path.
- memoryCompressionLevel.
- Guest thread affinity: commented out in both builds.

Defaults in this area, OLD vs NEW: logType is "sync" in both, logEnabled is true in both, logFilter is "" in both. isIdenticalLogGrouped is new and defaults to true. collectDebugLogs defaults to false, so the PerfStats counters do nothing.

Good A/B switches for a player:
- [Debug] logEnabled=false. In NEW this removes all logging cost; in OLD formatting still happened.
- [General] logType="async". This moves the console, file and OutputDebugString writes off the game threads.

My copies of both trees are in <scratch>/cpucore/{old,new}. Line numbers below refer to those copies.

findings.title: POSIX/scePthread semaphores: sem_post now wakes ALL waiters (thundering herd) instead of one
findings.old_behavior: PthreadSem wrapped a CountingSemaphore (a Win32 semaphore on Windows). posix_sem_post did ++value and semaphore.release(), which wakes exactly one waiter. posix_sem_wait called semaphore.acquire() directly.
findings.new_behavior: PthreadSem is now an atomic value plus a std::list of waiting Pthreads behind a mutex. posix_sem_post does a CAS increment, then releases wake_sema on every waiter and clears the list. Each woken thread retries the CAS; the losers push themselves back onto the list (a heap allocation each time) and sleep again. Every post and wait also does ScopedPthreadCritical atomics, PthreadTestCancel, ClearWake (a WaitForSingleObjectEx(0) syscall on Windows) and list add/remove under the mutex. scePthreadSemPost/Wait/Timedwait all go through this path.
findings.conditions: Games whose job systems block several worker threads on one scePthreadSem/sem_t and post often. With N idle workers each post causes N wakeups and N-1 wasted context switches. Hits every GPU vendor; worse on CPUs with few cores (iGPU laptops). sceKernelSema (OrbisSem) is unchanged. Whether UFC 3/4 use pthread semaphores is unverified.
findings.evidence: NEW src/core/libraries/kernel/threads/semaphore.cpp:25-30 (struct PthreadSem now holds value, wait_mutex and a list of waiters), :67-150 (PthreadSemWait loop), :426-451 (posix_sem_post: `for (Pthread* waiter : (*sem)->waiters) { waiter->wake_sema.release(); } (*sem)->waiters.clear();`), :486-519 (scePthreadSemWait/Post call posix_sem_*). OLD semaphore.cpp: `CountingSemaphore semaphore;` ... `(*sem)->semaphore.release();` in posix_sem_post.

verdict.title: POSIX/scePthread semaphores: sem_post now wakes ALL waiters (thundering herd) instead of one
verdict.notes: The code matches the description. NEW semaphore.cpp:24-29 has the atomic value, wait_mutex and std::list<Pthread*>; :426-451 posix_sem_post releases wake_sema on every waiter and clears the list; :67-131 waiters retry the CAS and re-push themselves. OLD semaphore.cpp:24-29 wrapped CountingSemaphore (Win32 CreateSemaphore); :304-316 post was ++value + ReleaseSemaphore. The analyst left out that the uncontended path is now FASTER. OLD posix_sem_wait (:268-276) always called WaitForSingleObjectEx, a kernel call, even when the count was >0, and every post called ReleaseSemaphore. NEW wait succeeds with a user-mode CAS (PthreadSemTryAcquire), and post with no waiters is a CAS plus an uncontended mutex. The thundering herd only costs anything when 2 or more threads block on the same sem at once. Nothing shows that UFC 3/4 use scePthreadSem* or sem_*; sceKernelSema (OrbisSem) is unchanged. Net direction depends on the game, so it is unclear. Comes from upstream (not in git diff 88bd144 12739d2). No A/B toggle.

findings.title: Windows logging: every log line written now also calls OutputDebugStringW, and each new log entry looks up the thread name
findings.old_behavior: ForEachBackend wrote to the console and file backends only; `// lambda(debugger_backend);` was commented out. An Entry had no thread name.
findings.new_behavior: On Windows ForEachBackend also calls DebuggerBackend: UTF8->UTF16 conversion plus ::OutputDebugStringW. That raises DBG_PRINTEXCEPTION_WIDE_C, which goes through vectored-exception dispatch, and the emulator's VEH returns CONTINUE_EXECUTION. So every written line costs an exception round trip of a few µs. Each new Entry also calls Common::GetCurrentThreadName(): a string copy for guest threads, or GetThreadDescription + UTF16->UTF8 + LocalFree for host threads such as the GPU and presenter threads. The format string now also contains the thread name. In the default sync mode all of this runs on the calling game or GPU thread under a global grouping mutex.
findings.conditions: Windows only. Matters when the game logs many distinct Info-or-higher lines per frame (stubbed functions, LOG_ERROR spam, posix_kevent LOG_INFO on every call, Atrac9 decode errors). Identical consecutive lines are collapsed by grouping and skip this cost.

verdict.title: Windows logging: every log line written now also calls OutputDebugStringW, and each new log entry looks up the thread name
verdict.notes: Confirmed. NEW backend.cpp:106-118 DebuggerBackend::Write calls OutputDebugStringW. ForEachBackend calls lambda(debugger_backend) under #ifdef _WIN32. OLD had `// lambda(debugger_backend);`. NEW signals.cpp handles DBG_PRINTEXCEPTION_C/WIDE_C in the VEH with EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_EXECUTION, so each written line costs a RaiseException round trip (user->kernel->KiUserExceptionDispatcher), a few µs. Common::GetCurrentThreadName (NEW thread.cpp:393-417) runs once per new distinct entry. Guest threads pay a string copy; host threads call GetThreadDescription. Defaults are the same in both builds: logType="sync", logEnabled=true, logFilter="" (config.cpp OLD :126-127,:209; NEW :189-190,:324). So the extra cost lands on the calling thread. It only matters if the game emits many distinct lines that pass the filter per frame. A/B: [Debug] logEnabled=false, or logType=async. Upstream (src/common/logging unchanged by our fork). src/common/logging/log.cpp (spdlog) is new but is not in CMake, so it is dead code.

findings.old_behavior: FmtLogMessageImpl called fmt::vformat(format, args) for every LOG_* call before PushEntry checked the filter, so every LOG_TRACE/LOG_DEBUG in hot paths (for example the 178 calls in gnmdriver.cpp, one per sceGnm* call) paid formatting and string construction even though it was filtered out. Every passing line was written to file and console with fflush(stdout) in sync mode.

findings.evidence: NEW src/common/logging/backend.cpp:186-192 (`if (!filter.CheckMessage(...) || !Config::getLoggingEnabled()) return; const auto message = fmt::vformat(format, args);`), :216-224 (grouping); NEW src/common/config.cpp:392 `static ConfigEntry<bool> isIdenticalLogGrouped(true);`. OLD backend.cpp:328 (vformat before PushEntry), :204 (filter checked inside PushEntry after formatting); OLD gnmdriver.cpp LOG_TRACE("called") at lines 127, 160, 174, ...

verdict.title: Logging: filtered-out messages are no longer formatted, and identical-line grouping is on by default
verdict.notes: Confirmed. OLD backend.cpp FmtLogMessageImpl called fmt::vformat before PushEntry, and the filter check came later in PushEntry. NEW FmtLogMessageImpl (:388-395) passes format and args, and PushEntry runs filter.CheckMessage/getLoggingEnabled before vformat. LOG_TRACE/LOG_DEBUG are not compiled out in either build (log.h macros identical), so OLD formatted every trace/debug call in hot HLE paths: 178 LOG_TRACE/LOG_DEBUG in OLD gnmdriver.cpp alone, plus video_core. Each saved vformat is roughly 50-200 ns, so the gain is small. isIdenticalLogGrouped defaults to true (NEW config.cpp:392). It takes a global mutex and a string compare per passing line, but saves the write and fflush for repeated lines. Upstream.

findings.title: Equeue HR timers lose the 1.2 ms precision spin; periodic timer events are rounded down to whole milliseconds
findings.old_behavior: sceKernelAddHRTimerEvent scheduled the asio timer 1200 µs early (HrTimerSpinlockThresholdUs). HrTimerCallback then added a 1200 µs small timer, and WaitForEvents finished the wait with a std::this_thread::yield() busy loop (WaitForSmallTimer). That was precise but burned one core for about 1.2 ms per expiry. sceKernelAddTimerEvent used microseconds(usec) as the interval.
findings.new_behavior: HR timers of 1.2 ms or longer are pure boost::asio timers on the KernelServiceThread with no spin, so their precision is whatever asio and the Windows timer resolution give (no timeBeginPeriod anywhere in the source). HR timers under 1.2 ms still spin. sceKernelAddTimerEvent stores usec/1000 and uses milliseconds(data): 16666 µs becomes 16 ms, 33333 µs becomes 33 ms, and anything under 1000 µs becomes 0 ms, which re-fires continuously (a busy KernelServiceThread plus constant wakeups of the game thread).
findings.conditions: Only games that pace frames or work with sceKernelAddHRTimerEvent or sceKernelAddTimerEvent. A late HR timer gives lower or less even FPS; the old spin cost a core. Sub-ms periodic timers become a CPU busy loop. Unverified whether UFC uses them.
findings.evidence: NEW src/core/libraries/kernel/equeue.cpp:25 (HrTimerSpinlockThresholdNs only used for <1.2ms small timers, :518), :51-70 (AddEvent: Timer interval = milliseconds(event.event.data)), :175-205 (WaitForEvents no longer spins after an asio-triggered HR timer), :543-555 (`event.event.data = usec / 1000;`). OLD equeue.cpp:18, :28-33 (interval offset by 1200 us), :130-137 (spin via WaitForSmallTimer), :305-311 (HrTimerCallback adds 1200us small timer), :390 (`event.event.data = usec;`).

verdict.title: Equeue HR timers lose the 1.2 ms precision spin; periodic timer events are rounded down to whole milliseconds
verdict.notes: The code differences are real. NEW equeue.cpp:25 has HrTimerSpinlockThresholdNs; :518-520 uses the small-timer spin only for <1.2 ms; AddEvent :57-70 + :110-114 schedules a plain asio timer; :554 `event.event.data = usec / 1000;` with milliseconds() at :59. OLD :18 HrTimerSpinlockThresholdUs, :28-33 offset, :130-137 spin, :305-311 HrTimerCallback adds a 1200 µs small timer, :390 data=usec. OLD sceKernelAddHRTimerEvent also rejected any timespec with tv_nsec<100000 (EINVAL), so many valid HR timers did not work at all in OLD. The rounding makes a 16666 µs periodic timer fire at 62.5 Hz instead of 60 Hz, which is faster, not slower. A sub-ms periodic timer becomes interval 0 and re-fires continuously. Neither build calls timeBeginPeriod (git grep finds nothing in either), so asio precision is equally coarse in both. Nothing shows that UFC 3/4 use these timers, so this is not a demonstrated FPS factor. Upstream.

findings.title: MemoryManager::TryWriteBacking now locks and deep-copies VMAs on every call (GPU write-back and readback path)

findings.new_behavior: Takes std::shared_lock on the memory manager's SharedFirstMutex (a mutex plus condvar; lock and unlock both take the internal mutex). findings.title: Memory manager mutex and guest rwlocks now use reader-first SharedFirstMutex; Windows AddressSpace adds a global mutex
findings.old_behavior: MemoryManager used std::mutex. Guest PthreadRwlock used std::shared_timed_mutex. Windows AddressSpace::Impl Map/Unmap/Protect took no lock of their own.
findings.new_behavior: MemoryManager uses Common::SharedFirstMutex (mutex + condvar, readers first, writers can starve; unlock() always notify_all) plus a separate unmap_mutex. Guest rwlocks use the same SharedFirstMutex, so under contention a writer can wait behind a stream of readers and every write-unlock wakes all waiters. Windows AddressSpace Map/Unmap/Protect take a std::mutex, so page_manager write-protect calls (GPU memory tracking) serialize with guest map/unmap. ClampRangeSize now does a locked map lookup for buffers of 1 GB or more (was 3 GB).
findings.conditions: Games with contended pthread rwlocks, or heavy map/unmap while the GPU thread protects or tracks pages. Mostly a source of stutter, not lower average FPS.

OLD pthread.h: `std::shared_timed_mutex lock;`, OLD memory.h `std::mutex mutex;`, OLD memory.cpp:72 MinSizeToClamp = 3_GB.

verdict.title: Memory manager mutex and guest rwlocks now use reader-first SharedFirstMutex; Windows AddressSpace adds a global mutex
verdict.notes: Confirmed. NEW shared_first_mutex.h is a mutex+condvar; unlock() calls notify_all. NEW memory.h:387-388 has SharedFirstMutex + unmap_mutex (OLD memory.h:365 std::mutex). NEW pthread.h:213 PthreadRwlock uses SharedFirstMutex (OLD :191 std::shared_timed_mutex). On MSVC, std::shared_timed_mutex is itself mutex+condvar based, not SRWLOCK, so the uncontended guest-rwlock difference is small. NEW address_space.cpp:440,509,552 scoped_lock(mutex) in Windows Map/Unmap/Protect. Protect is the page_manager GPU tracking path (page_manager.cpp:211-217). findings.title: File I/O: extra memcpy on every read and several extra stat calls on every open/stat

findings.title: Windows address space: splitting a mapped region now also queries and restores page protections (our fork)
findings.old_behavior: OLD (a8d954e) handled a partial unmap by unmapping the whole allocation and re-mapping the remainder. Protections were lost.
findings.new_behavior: Upstream SplitRegion unmaps and remaps the parts. Our fork (914c5a1 cherry-pick #5317) adds a QueryProtections loop (VirtualQueryEx over the region) and a VirtualProtectEx for each sub-range with a different protection. This adds syscalls only when a mapped region is split; it is a correctness fix that keeps GPU write-tracking protections.
findings.conditions: Windows; only on partial unmap, protect or remap of large mappings. Not per frame in normal play.
findings.evidence: NEW src/core/address_space.cpp:235-310 (MapRegion protections loop), :312-330 (QueryProtections), :350-430 (SplitRegion calls). git diff 88bd144 12739d2 -- src/core/address_space.cpp shows these lines as fork additions.

verdict.title: Windows address space: splitting a mapped region now also queries and restores page protections (our fork)
verdict.notes: Confirmed by git diff 88bd144 12739d2 -- src/core/address_space.cpp: QueryProtections (VirtualQueryEx loop) runs in SplitRegion when the region is mapped, and MapRegion re-applies VirtualProtectEx per sub-range. This adds syscalls only on a partial unmap or remap of a mapped placeholder, which is not per frame. One VirtualQueryEx runs per protection run, so a large heavily-tracked region could take many calls in one split; that is a rare one-off hitch at most. It is a correctness fix that keeps GPU tracking protections. Our fork (cherry-pick of #5317).

findings.title: Event flags: wake only the waiters whose condition is met; old 10 µs sleep loops removed
findings.old_behavior: One condition_variable: Set() called notify_all, waking every waiter to re-check. Set/Clear/Cancel spun with sleep_for(10us) while a Cancel was in progress.
findings.new_behavior: A list of waiters, each with its own condvar. Set() checks each waiter's condition, applies the clear mode and notifies only the matching ones. A waiter whose condition is already met returns without blocking. No sleep loops.
findings.conditions: Games using sceKernelEventFlag with several waiters (common in job and streaming systems).
findings.evidence: NEW src/core/libraries/kernel/threads/event_flag.cpp:34-50 (Waiter), :105-175 (Wait), :187-205 (Set notifies matching waiters only). OLD event_flag.cpp:111-121 (sleep_for(10us) loop + m_cond_var.notify_all), :128, :140, :155.

verdict.title: Event flags: wake only the waiters whose condition is met; old 10 µs sleep loops removed
verdict.notes: Real, but overstated. OLD Set (event_flag.cpp ~:111-121) did notify_all on one condvar. findings.title: Condvar, mutex and thread changes: cancellation-point bookkeeping added; hot paths otherwise equivalent
findings.old_behavior: Cond wait: ClearWake (one try_acquire), Sleep, re-lock. SleepqLock/Unlock were plain spinlocks. Threads were created with NtCreateThread on the guest stack, and guest entry went through Core::ExecuteGuest.
findings.new_behavior: Each cond wait and sem wait adds PthreadTestCancel, cancel_point atomics, locklevel fetch_add/fetch_sub in SleepqLock/Unlock with a PthreadCancelInterrupt check, and FIFO waiter order (push_back). Signal-to-thread does a ThrState::FindThread. Pthread mutex is unchanged (same spin and yield loops; m_owner is now atomic). Threads are created with CreateThread and switch to the guest stack via _runOnAnotherStack, and each guest thread is converted to a fiber for a VEH stack (initialized but RunOnVehStack is never called). This adds a few atomics per sync call: negligible unless sync is extremely hot.
findings.conditions: All games; overhead is tens of ns per sync operation.

missed_by_analyst:
Verified items the analyst missed or got wrong:
(1) The SDK version change is bigger than reported. OLD sceKernelGetCompiledSdkVersion returned param.sfo SYSTEM_VER (OLD process.cpp:24-28). NEW returns 0 (NEW process.cpp:57-63 plus the emulator.cpp:112-130 stub). gnmdriver therefore takes the pre-2.00 init packet and the pre-4.00 DrawInitToDefaultContextState (NEW gnmdriver.cpp:2181, 2864, 2872). This is a behaviour difference from upstream, not an FPS factor.
(2) A/B caveat that matters for FPS testing: for UFC 4 (CUSA14204/CUSA14209) our fork forces Readback Speed Disable/Unsafe to Low (NEW config.cpp:1238-1261, commit ef844c9). UFC 4 players cannot remove readback cost with the setting, while OLD defaulted to Disable (OLD config.cpp:173). The readback cost itself is a video_core matter.
(3) Windows timed waits: Semaphore::try_acquire_for (NEW sync/semaphore.h:103-135) used to return false on WAIT_TIMEOUT. It now loops until a steady_clock deadline and re-waits with ceil(ms), at least 1 ms. Timed condvar, sem and event waits can therefore oversleep by up to one extra Windows timer tick when WaitForSingleObjectEx returns slightly early. Neither build calls timeBeginPeriod. This is a possible small stutter source. Upstream; no toggle.
(4) The SDL audio backend (NEW sdl_audio_out.cpp:235-261, upstream) adds HandleTiming. It runs std::this_thread::sleep_for inside Output() while holding port->mutex, on top of the existing AccurateTimer pacing in AudioOutputThread (NEW audioout.cpp:164-205). OLD sdl_audio.cpp Output never slept. It affects only the audio thread and the guest's blocking sceAudioOutOutput, so the FPS impact is low or none. Default audioBackend is SDL in NEW (config.cpp:242).
(5) Buffer-cache uploads now read guest data through CopySparseMemory from the physical backing, using a 16 KB page-table lookup per page (NEW memory.cpp CopySparseMemory; buffer_cache.cpp:354,474). They no longer read the virtual address directly. This avoids access-violation faults on protected pages and is neutral-to-faster.
No high-magnitude CPU-core difference was found that would explain a large generic FPS drop. The likely large factors are outside this area (readback defaults and forcing, video_core).

summary:
I compared OLD a8d954e and NEW 12739d2 for config defaults on a new install, for an existing config.toml, and for emulator startup. Shadlix base is 88bd144.

**Biggest config-side reason NEW can be slower: GPU readbacks.** OLD defaults Readback Speed to Disable. NEW does two things (both our fork):
- a new install gets Low (ApplyRecommendedSettings, commit b7285a7);
- UFC 4 (CUSA14204/14209) always runs Disable/Unsafe as Low (gpuReadbackSpeed, commit ef844c9), so there is no way in the release to turn readbacks off for UFC 4.

With Low, GPU-written pages are write-protected, and CPU reads wait for a GPU download.

**Other slower-in-NEW items:**
- **Windows logging (upstream).** Every log line now also goes to OutputDebugStringW. With the unchanged default logType = sync this runs on the game thread. Identical-line grouping (default on) adds a global mutex per line.
- **Fresh install loses old tweaks.** A new config.toml means vblank 60, so UFC runs at 30 FPS. A player who raised vblankFrequency in OLD gets half the FPS until they set it again (or turn on the FPS limiter).
- **Readback "Fast" changed (upstream).** In OLD, Fast mostly behaved like no readback. In NEW it protects pages like Low. An old config with Fast is slower in NEW.
- **Shader-cache saves.** With the shader cache on (new install), the Vulkan pipeline cache is written to disk on the GPU thread every 50 new pipelines, which can cause hitches.

**Faster in NEW:**
- Disk shader cache plus warm-up (OLD had no disk cache), on for new installs.
- Log messages are filtered before they are formatted.
- With the FPS limiter on at N, UFC now shows N FPS instead of N/2.

**Checked and unchanged or neutral:**
- Same defaults in OLD and NEW: vkValidation, sync/GPU validation, crashDiagnostic, host/guest markers, rdoc, copyGPUBuffers, DMA, readbackLinearImages, nullGpu, patchShaders, vblankFrequency 60, presentMode Mailbox, FSR/RCAS on, isPS4Pro off, logType sync, logEnabled true, FPS limiter off.
- Process priority ABOVE_NORMAL is set in both. emulator.cpp does not change timer resolution in either version.
- New NEW-only settings that do nothing by default:
  - memoryCompressionLevel 0: stored only, does nothing.
  - useHostMemoryFallback: off.
  - cpuCoreMode All: getEffectiveCpuCores is never called.
  - app0 read bandwidth 0: no worker threads, no throttling.
  - collectDebugLogs: off. PerfAdd returns early, and the freeze watchdog only runs when enabled or when SHADPS4_DEBUG_LOGS / SHADPS4_FREEZE_* is set.
  - renderResolution "": no patch, the game keeps 1600x900.
  - skipIntroVideo and autoUpdate: no in-game cost.
- devtools: the new GPU memory widget only runs when opened, and the FPS counter is off by default in both.
- Big Picture mode: a side bug in our fork. Opening its settings re-applies the recommended settings, including readback Low.

**A/B tests:**
- Readback: Settings > Readback Speed = Disable, for UFC 3 and other games only.
- Logging: logType=async, logEnabled=false or isIdenticalLogGrouped=false in config.toml.
- Shader cache: the "Enable Shader Cache" checkbox.
- Render resolution: the selector or SHADPS4_RENDER_RES.
- PS4 Pro mode: SHADPS4_PS4PRO.
- Debug logs: SHADPS4_DEBUG_LOGS.

findings.old_behavior: OLD has no disk shader or pipeline cache. Every run recompiles every GCN shader and pipeline when it is first used, which causes in-game stutter.

missed_by_analyst:
The analyst missed one verified upstream change: Disable no longer fully skips GPU-to-CPU syncs on CPU writes. OLD memory_tracker.h InvalidateRegion (around line 99) only flushed when `Config::readbackSpeed() != Disable && IsRegionModified<GPU>`. NEW memory_tracker.h:91-105, already the same in Shadlix 88bd144, flushes whenever the page is GPU-modified, whatever the readback mode.

In NEW, GPU writes still set the GPU-modified bits in Disable mode (memory_tracker ForEachUploadRange around line 139 -> ChangeRegionState<GPU,true>). A guest CPU write to such a page then goes this way:
1. The write faults on the protected page, and page_manager.cpp:225 GuestFaultSignalHandler calls InvalidateMemory.
2. BufferCache::InvalidateMemory (buffer_cache.cpp:98-101) runs on_flush, which calls ReadMemory.
3. ReadMemory downloads a window of up to 512 KB around the address. It goes through liverpool SendCommand<true>, which blocks on a semaphore until the GPU thread runs the download (liverpool.h:105-117).

In OLD with Disable, the same write only marked the page CPU-modified, with no download and no wait. So even players who keep Readback Speed = Disable (or Off after cdfb6fa) can see GPU syncs in NEW wherever the game rewrites memory the GPU wrote, for example reused constant or vertex ring buffers. There is no setting to A/B this. Magnitude is unmeasured, possibly medium (stutter); it belongs to the buffer-cache area but undercuts the claim that NEW Disable equals OLD Disable.

Two smaller verified points:
- NEW config.cpp static defaults for every key present in both versions are byte-identical to OLD, including readbackSpeedMode Disable, logType sync, vblank 60, copyGPUBuffers, directMemoryAccess, readbackLinearImages and fpsLimiterEnabled. The only default differences come from ApplyRecommendedSettings (cache on, archive off, readback Low, fpsLimit=refresh) and from the new keys: isIdenticalLogGrouped true, inlineFetchShader false, memoryCompressionLevel 0, useHostMemoryFallback false, app0 bandwidth 0. None of the new keys adds cost by default except the log grouping mutex.
- NEW driver.cpp PresentThread adds a few LOG_INFO lines, but only once at thread start, so no per-frame cost.

summary: The Windows build toolchain is essentially the same in OLD (a8d954e) and NEW (12739d2), and nothing in the build setup explains a general FPS drop. Both workflows build Release with BUILD_TYPE: Release (OLD build.yml:13, NEW build.yml:25) and use clang-cl + Ninja with -DCMAKE_INTERPROCEDURAL_OPTIMIZATION_RELEASE=ON (OLD build.yml:87/136, NEW build.yml:74/125). Both compile x86_64 code with -march=x86-64-v3 (CMakeLists.txt:65 NEW, :64 OLD). Tracy is off in Release, with the same block in externals/CMakeLists.txt in both. Neither has sanitizers, PGO, explicit -O flags, NDEBUG/assert changes or compile-time log-level stripping. The ENABLE_LTO option is OFF in both. These externals are at the same commit in both trees: VMA, zlib-ng, glslang (ENABLE_OPT OFF in both, so the SPIRV-Tools optimizer is not used by either), boost, tracy and xbyak. The flags NEW adds (-mno-avx512f, which does nothing on top of x86-64-v3, and -mpclmul -maes -msha, needed by Crypto++) and the /MAP linker option (our fork) do not change speed. Our fork changed only three things in this area: it trimmed CI to Windows, added the beta pre-release step, added /MAP, and gave CryptoPP's interface the same ASM defines as the library. CryptoPP is used for PKG install, not gameplay. Everything else came from upstream/Shadlix. The only measurable runtime differences found next to the build area are in the logging backend, which is compiled the same way but changed behavior. On Windows NEW also sends every logged line to OutputDebugStringW, and on host threads it also calls GetThreadDescription. With the default logEnabled=true, logType=sync and an empty filter, this runs on the calling (game/GPU) thread. This can cost speed when a game produces many log lines. On the other hand, NEW now checks the log filter before formatting the message, which is faster when a filter is set. Other library bumps should have little or no effect on speed: sirit only gained opcodes (OpNClamp, subgroup shuffle, OpReadClockKHR), SDL3 went from 3.3.0-dev to 3.5.0-dev, Vulkan-Headers changed slightly, and OpenAL-soft, protobuf, abseil, freetype and others were added. Host shaders are now compiled to SPIR-V at build time instead of at runtime with glslang, which only shortens startup. Upstream also removed ExecuteGuest's 12 KB optnone stack clear per guest callback, a small gain for NEW. The Qt version went from 6.10.0 to 6.9.3, but Qt only runs the launcher: in both builds the game runs in a separate process started with QProcess. I could not check the actual clang-cl version on the CI runner image (the SDL job moved to windows-2025-vs2026; the Qt job stays on windows-2025 in both).

verdict.title: Windows log lines now also go to OutputDebugStringW (DebuggerBackend enabled)
verdict.notes: Confirmed. OLD a8d954e backend.cpp ForEachBackend has `// lambda(debugger_backend);`. NEW 12739d2 backend.cpp:324-330 calls it under #ifdef _WIN32, and :112 formats the line again, converts it to UTF-16 and calls OutputDebugStringW. This was already in 88bd144 and our fork did not change it (git diff 88bd144 12739d2 -- src/common/logging is empty). The magnitude is overstated. NEW signals.cpp:52-55 (upstream) has the vectored exception handler return EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_EXECUTION for DBG_PRINTEXCEPTION_C/WIDE_C, so each call costs one exception raise and dispatch (a few microseconds) and does not take the DBWIN mutex/shared-memory fallback. The console and file backends cost about as much per line or more, in both builds. The 100 MB file limit point is true but minor, because the console backend also keeps running after it. The default logType is 'sync' in both (OLD config.cpp:127, NEW :190), so the cost lands on the thread that logs. It only adds up under log spam (thousands of lines per second), where it could reach a few percent on a CPU-bound thread. With DebugView or a debugger attached it costs much more. A/B test: turn logging off (logEnabled) or set logFilter to *:Error. There is no switch for the debugger backend alone. Origin: upstream/Shadlix.

findings.title: Per-message logging overhead: grouping mutex and thread-name lookup
findings.old_behavior: OLD built one Entry per message without a lock and without looking up the thread name.
findings.new_behavior: NEW groupIdenticalLogs defaults to true (config.cpp:392). Every message that passes the filter now takes a global std::mutex (backend.cpp:217) and compares strings with the previous message. Every Entry also calls Common::GetCurrentThreadName() (backend.cpp:245/257). For host threads (no g_curthread) that means GetThreadDescription + UTF16ToUTF8 + LocalFree on Windows (thread.cpp:402-409), and for fiber threads it means fmt::format. Identical lines repeated back to back are merged, so file and console writes go down during spam.
findings.conditions: Windows. Only matters with heavy logging from several threads at once (lock contention). Merging repeated identical lines partly offsets the cost.
findings.ab_toggle: The group-identical-logs setting (isIdenticalLogGrouped); logEnabled=false removes all of it.
findings.evidence: NEW src/common/logging/backend.cpp:216-249 (grouping branch, std::unique_lock entry_loc(_mutex)), :245,:257 `.thread = Common::GetCurrentThreadName()`, :351 `std::mutex _mutex;`. NEW src/common/thread.cpp:393-409. NEW src/common/config.cpp:392 `isIdenticalLogGrouped(true)`.

verdict.title: Per-message logging overhead: grouping mutex and thread-name lookup
verdict.notes: Confirmed. NEW config.cpp:392 sets isIdenticalLogGrouped(true). NEW backend.cpp:216 takes a global std::unique_lock(_mutex), and every new entry calls GetCurrentThreadName() (thread.cpp:393-409: guest name copy, fmt::format for fibers, or GetThreadDescription+UTF16ToUTF8+LocalFree for host threads). One detail the analyst missed: in sync mode the mutex is still held while ForEachBackend writes the previous entry to the debugger, console and file backends (backend.cpp:228-234). So under spam, every thread that logs waits for one shared slow write path. OLD wrote without any lock. Merging repeated identical lines partly offsets this. It only matters with heavy multi-thread logging. A/B test: the group-identical-logs setting, logEnabled or logFilter. Origin: upstream/Shadlix.

findings.title: Log filter is now checked before formatting the message
findings.old_behavior: OLD FmtLogMessageImpl formatted every LOG_* call with fmt::vformat before PushEntry checked filter.CheckMessage (OLD backend.cpp:328 then :204). So messages that were filtered out (such as LOG_DEBUG/LOG_TRACE in hot paths) still paid the full formatting cost.
findings.new_behavior: NEW PushEntry checks filter.CheckMessage and getLoggingEnabled first, then formats (NEW backend.cpp:188-192). Filtered-out messages cost almost nothing.
findings.conditions: Only helps when logFilter hides classes or levels or logging is turned off. With the default empty filter everything at Info level and above is formatted in both builds.
findings.evidence: NEW src/common/logging/backend.cpp:186-192 `if (!filter.CheckMessage(log_class, log_level) || !Config::getLoggingEnabled()) return; const auto message = fmt::vformat(format, args);`. OLD backend.cpp:326-329 formats in FmtLogMessageImpl, :204 checks afterwards.

verdict.title: Log filter is now checked before formatting the message
verdict.notes: Confirmed. OLD FmtLogMessageImpl runs fmt::vformat before PushEntry checks filter.CheckMessage. NEW PushEntry (backend.cpp:186-192) checks the filter first. The stated conditions are too narrow. The default Filter level is Info (filter.h:32) and the default logFilter is empty, so at default settings every LOG_DEBUG/LOG_TRACE call was still formatted and thrown away in OLD (log.h macros are not compiled out in Release), and NEW skips them. So NEW wins at default settings too, in chatty HLE paths, though only by a small amount (about 100-300 ns per call). Origin: upstream/Shadlix.

verdict.title: Compiler, optimization and arch flags are effectively identical
verdict.notes: Confirmed. Release, clang-cl, Ninja and IPO are the same in both build.yml files. -march=x86-64-v3 is unchanged. -mno-avx512f does nothing on top of v3. -mpclmul/-maes/-msha only enable intrinsics (Crypto++). verdict.title: CI runner image / compiler version drift (cannot verify the actual clang-cl version)
verdict.notes: The YAML differences are as described: NEW build.yml:47 is windows-2025-vs2026 for SDL, :86 is windows-2025 for Qt, and Qt is 6.9.3 instead of 6.10.0. findings.title: zlib-ng no longer built with WITH_NATIVE_INSTRUCTIONS

verdict.title: zlib-ng no longer built with WITH_NATIVE_INSTRUCTIONS
verdict.notes: Confirmed: the diff removes `set(WITH_NATIVE_INSTRUCTIONS ON)` from externals/CMakeLists.txt, and WITH_AVX512 is OFF in NEW CMakeLists.txt:74-75. zlib is not used per frame.

findings.title: Host shaders compiled at build time instead of at runtime by glslang
findings.old_behavior: OLD compiled GLSL host shaders (detilers, FSR, post_process, blit, fault buffer) to SPIR-V at emulator startup through linked glslang (vk_shader_util.cpp Compile(), disableOptimizer=false but glslang ENABLE_OPT OFF, so no real optimization).
findings.new_behavior: NEW builds glslang-standalone (ENABLE_GLSLANG_BINARIES ON) and precompiles the host shaders into SPIR-V headers at build time, without spirv-opt (same optimization level as before). vk_shader_util.cpp only creates modules from SPIR-V. Tiling now uses one tiling.comp with per-BPP defines instead of separate detiler files. Any GPU-time difference in that shader belongs to the texture-cache area.
findings.conditions: Startup time only. No per-frame effect from the toolchain change itself.
findings.evidence: diff externals/CMakeLists.txt: `ENABLE_GLSLANG_BINARIES ON CACHE BOOL "" FORCE`. NEW src/video_core/host_shaders/CMakeLists.txt:20-58 add_host_shader(... glslang-standalone --target-env vulkan1.3 ...). NEW src/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_shader_util.cpp:9-19 (CompileSPV only). OLD vk_shader_util.cpp:162 Compile(std::string_view code,...).

verdict.title: Host shaders compiled at build time instead of at runtime by glslang
verdict.notes: Confirmed. OLD host_shaders/CMakeLists.txt embedded GLSL source as strings and vk_shader_util.cpp:162 Compile() ran glslang at runtime. NEW builds SPIR-V headers at build time with glslang-standalone (host_shaders/CMakeLists.txt:16-58, ENABLE_GLSLANG_BINARIES ON). This only saves startup time, plus maybe a one-time hitch the first time a host shader was compiled lazily. No steady-state FPS effect. Our fork only added the depth_to_color shaders (diff 88bd144..12739d2).

findings.title: Removed optnone 12 KB stack clear on every host-to-guest callback (ExecuteGuest)
findings.old_behavior: OLD tls.h ExecuteGuest called EnsureThreadInitialized() plus ClearStack<12_KB>(), an __attribute__((optnone)) alloca and memset of 12 KB, on every host-to-guest call. These calls came from avplayer file read/alloc callbacks, NGS2 host alloc, IME, net_ctl, pthread TLS destructors and thread start.
findings.new_behavior: NEW removes ExecuteGuest/ClearStack. TLS is set up once per thread through Core::InitializeTLS() in pthread start (pthread.cpp:261), and callbacks call guest code directly.
findings.conditions: CPU side. Matters only for frequent guest callbacks, e.g. video playback through avplayer.
findings.evidence: OLD src/core/tls.h:45-61 (`__attribute__((optnone)) void ClearStack()`, `ExecuteGuest`). NEW src/core/tls.h:47-48 `void InitializeTLS();`. NEW src/core/tls.cpp:209. Callers in OLD: avplayer_impl.cpp:15-72, ngs2.cpp:163, pthread.cpp:211.

verdict.title: Removed optnone 12 KB stack clear on every host-to-guest callback (ExecuteGuest)
verdict.notes: Confirmed: OLD tls.h:45-61 has ClearStack<12_KB> in ExecuteGuest, and NEW tls.h has only InitializeTLS() and HostCallWrapperImpl. A 12 KB memset takes well under 1 microsecond, and the callers (avplayer, ngs2 alloc, IME, TLS alloc, thread start) are not called per frame in large numbers. The effect is negligible, and this is not a build-toolchain change.

missed_by_analyst: I found no important FPS-relevant build or toolchain difference that the analyst missed. Two refinements I checked in the code: (1) NEW src/core/signals.cpp:52-55 (upstream) makes the vectored exception handler return EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_EXECUTION for DBG_PRINTEXCEPTION_C/WIDE_C. This limits the cost of the newly enabled OutputDebugStringW backend to about one exception dispatch per log line, so it is low, not medium, unless a debugger or DebugView is attached. (2) With the default group-identical-logs setting and sync logging, NEW holds the global log mutex while it writes to all backends (backend.cpp:216-234). Under log spam, threads that log wait on each other's console, file and debug writes. OLD had no lock. Also missed, though not FPS-relevant: fmt 10->12, ffmpeg-core, hwinfo and ImGui submodule bumps. The sirit bump c58f4d4->fc2b42d came in through our fork's cherry-pick 5157080, not through Shadlix 88bd144.
